 LIKE 3
Rahul Mukerji: Mridhangit
By Maciej Stasiowski
May 31, 2026
View read count
Mridhangit is a portmanteau of the instrument mridangam, employed extensively on the new record by Rahul Mukerji, and the Hindi word for song or music (git/geet). First ignited on the artist's 2017 release Ma De Re Sha (Self Produced, 2017), the project has solidified into a recognisable signature: guitar-led instrumentals anchored in Indian percussive rhythms, shaped through tablas (both programmed and live) and the mridangam, with occasional accents of clarinet and duduk.

The compositions are concise, introducing their melodic core with little delay before unfolding into densely layered arrangements. Yet Mridhangit is most persuasive when it is given room to breathe. This is especially evident in the more relaxed, atmospheric pieces ("Twelve Ganeshas," "Enjoymaddi") and the funk-inflected grooves of "Kalli Penn" and "Funky Pakora"; to an extent, even tracks driven by more angular guitar heroics, such as "Rahu Ketu," benefit from this spaciousness. A sense of unrestrained velocity and exuberance courses through the album, with relentless soloing woven around the mridangam and tabla patterns.

The album's fusion vocabulary evokes less the jazz-rock spiritualism of John McLaughlin's Mahavishnu Orchestra or Ralph Towner's Oregon, and more often recalls Steve Hackett's multifaceted engagements with Middle Eastern and Far Eastern melodic traditions. "Funky Pakora," guided by clarinet lines and buoyed by clear, driving melodies, establishes an expansive atmosphere, while elsewhere the music acquires an elastic buoyancy through its guttural bass work—almost as though it were situated across the street from Jonas Hellborg's mansion of funky ragas. At any moment, this fluidity can erupt into distorted, quasi-orchestral guitar detonations, as in "Dushtan." Most tracks function as dialogues or trios, yet it is in the latter format that the music truly catches fire, at times approaching the combustible interplay of the Bozzio-Levin-Stevens (Terry Bozzio-Tony Levin-Steve Stevens) records.

Fortunately, Mridhangit is balanced rather than relentless, closing with two contemplative statements. "Four Seas" allows space and emotional resonance to take precedence; its understated beauty leaves the listener lingering over its brevity. "Mutabor," meanwhile, eases the album toward its conclusion through yearning duduk melodies and shimmering tabla rhythms underpinning a circular guitar motif. Even at 50 minutes, the record retains a sense of momentum, deftly guiding the listener through a broad emotional spectrum—from a tandavam dawn to an abhoga dusk. One can only hope that Mukerji will eventually devote an entire record to the more subdued incarnations of his otherwise intensely kinetic music.

 LIKE 5
Pierre Favre: Bird Food
By Glenn Astarita
May 31, 2026
View read count
Captured live at Radio Studio Zurich in 1968, this is the earliest known recording of the Pierre Favre Trio, dormant for more than half a century until Favre and trombonist Samuel Blaser unearthed it while sorting through forgotten tapes. That it survived at all feels faintly miraculous, the jazz equivalent of finding cash in an old winter coat.

The lineup now reads like a rough sketch of European free jazz before the paint dried. Pierre Favre anchors the session with concentrated intensity, already displaying the instincts that would make him one of the continent's defining percussionists. Pianist Irene Schweizer—who penned three of the four compositions—plays with fearless abandon, her Cecil Taylor influence worn proudly and loudly. Then there is the bassist credited here as Jiří Mráz, years before he became George Mraz in the United States, where he would go on to support figures such as Dizzy Gillespie, Oscar Peterson, Stan Getz and Tommy Flanagan with remarkable versatility.

The program is lean but loaded: four tracks in roughly 30 minutes, beginning with Ornette Coleman's title piece before shifting into Schweizer's originals. The Coleman composition establishes the atmosphere immediately—a collective urge to dismantle structure simply to examine what remains standing afterward.

"Sound II" drifts like a cosmic lullaby assembled from jagged angles and sudden detours, the trio moving through asymmetrical currents that rise and collapse without warning. "Hinten," by contrast, charges ahead with sharp momentum. Schweizer pushes the piano into overdrive while Favre hovers nearby and  Mraz stretches confidently across the shifting terrain, threading fluid lines through Favre's subtle but persistent undercurrent.

Schweizer's closing work, "The Attack," earns its title honestly. Her left-hand hammers out dense, dissonant clusters while the right searches stubbornly for melodic daylight amid blues fragments and bop-inflected runs. Favre responds with controlled force, then eases away just enough to let silence finish the sentence.

This 57-year-old radio tape holds up rather well. Still, headphones repay the effort. They separate the instruments and reveal the micro-dynamics that make Favre's quieter gestures every bit as compelling as his louder eruptions. In the end, Bird Food stands as raw evidence of three musicians already operating beyond their years—a session that required neither spotlight nor audience to burn with complete conviction.

items._cn_summary: 《Bird Food》是瑞士电台1968年的现场录音，是Pierre Favre三重奏目前已知最早的专辑。三位乐手均展现出超越时代的即兴演奏水平：Pierre Favre以集中而富有爆发力的鼓点奠定基础；钢琴家Irene Schweizer受Cecil Taylor影响显著，演奏风格狂放不羁；低音提琴手George Mraz（当时名为Jiří Mráz）在专辑中展现了后来成为美国爵士界传奇伴奏手的潜力。专辑收录四首曲目，包括奥内特·科尔曼的同名作品及Schweizer原创曲目，呈现早期欧洲自由爵士的典型特征——解构传统结构、追求声响边界、强调集体即兴的动态对话。乐队在《Sound II》中展现不对称流动与突然转折的张力，《The Attack》则以激烈的左手敲击与碎片化旋律构建紧张氛围。作为一张尘封五十七年后被重新发掘的历史录音，其实验性与音乐价值依然鲜明，Blaser Music独立发行。

Home » Jazz Articles » Album Review » Phillip Golub: Partisan Ship

LIKE 3
Phillip Golub: Partisan Ship
By Mike Jurkovic
May 31, 2026
View read count
In a lot off ways, it is a game of catch-up listening to Brooklyn pianist/improvisor/composer Phillip Golub once he kick-starts the oddly titled Partisan Ship into high gear with "Loyalty Oath," a piece of mad musical fiction that holds attention in place with its octopi rhythms and runaway melodies rushing in all at once. 

Partisan Ship is oddly titled because Golub, an unapologetic polymath far out on the progressive spectrum, and his juiced and jazzed up cohorts—clarinetist and saxophonist Yuma Uesaka, trumpeter Amir ElSaffar, Anna Webber -flute and tenor sax, David Leon -alto sax, Layale Chaker, five string violin, drummer and percussive everyman Jonathan Starks, bassist Sam Minaie, and multi keyboardist Elias Stemeseder—keep their feet to the fire. Not many traditionalists are going to go along with the hyperkinetic title track: the saxophones flying, the drums avalanching. 

Whatever Golub's prime instrument, the Flexichord, does exactly what is best left for an MIT grad to explain, but Golub is not afraid to use it to Partisan Ship's cranked-up advantage. With seemingly all the keyboards and electronics at the ready, Golub, Stemeseder, and Starks (whose sensory percussion might need explaining, too) cut loose on the pulse pounding "interlude (adrift)." "mutiny meeting," with its impish blend of Horace Silver and Herbie Hancock. The relative quiet of "blue-orange reflections." The vertigo head rush encountered throughout "cries of the initiated."

Golub, whose 2024 breakout Abiding Memory (Endectomorph Music/Berthold Records) and 2025's duet with drummer Lesley Mok, dream brigade (Infrequent Seams) were the five alarm fires clearing the way for "utopian microtonation" of Partisan Ship's most gnarly, yet immersive salvo. ElSaffar sails above Webber's imploring flute while the rest of the ensemble smooths things out big band style. The lunatic "afterword: partisan session" follows and closes Partisan Ship, a set of music that veers like a tornado, with its own destination.

items.body:
Chicago quartet U.S. Maple's best album, 'Acre Thrills' is an American avant-rock masterpiecce that torches established formula unremittingly, singlehandedly creating music that's never quite been repeated - or bettered. Essential listening FFO Gastr del Sol, Hella, even black midi.

By the time U.S. Maple released 'Acre Thrills' in 2001, they'd already proved what they needed to prove, building up a so-called "math rock" sound out of the bones of Captain Beefheart's deconstructed 'Trout Mask Replica' and tearing it apart on the fly. And even when they brushed with the college rock underground's top levels, opening for Pavement and potentially glomming onto a completely new audience, they stuck to their guns, getting weirder rather than sanding down their sharp edges. This album isn't as dark as its predecessor by any means (we're gonna blame 'Talker' producer Michael Gira for that one), but it's more delicately arranged somehow - a perfectly imperfect lattice of angular, xenharmonic riffs and interlock'd polyrhythms that still somehow manage to couch vocalist Al Johnson's almost inhuman groans and monologues. His delivery's like Marmite, undoubtedly, but it's another element of the U.S. Maple sound that makes them impossible to properly replicate - despite bands endlessly trying ever since.

Although 'Acre Thrills' almost relishes its own knottiness, it's packed with moments that sound almost welcoming, at least to us. Opener 'Ma Digital' is surprisingly soft, Johnson's voice just a low hum underneath Mark Shippy and Todd Rittman's pretty breezy, almost hummable riffs, and if you didn't know better, you might confuse 'Babe' for a bluesier post-hardcore experiment, like Karate through a blender. By 'Untitled' though, their claws are fully on show with an instrumental that deconstructs itself as it plays through, falling apart into run-out-groove noise that's supposed to make you question what you're listening to. And when the album jolts back to life with 'Obey Your Concert', it's bolder, trickier and edgier, with Johnson veering from David Thomas to David Bowie in a matter of seconds. In the wrong hands, this kind of studied, hyper-technical grandstanding would be like nails on a chalkboard, so it's genuinely shocking that U.S. Maple managed to make it sound not just effortless but enduringly edgy. It's not noodly prog, it's grinding, painful, urgent music that understands the all-important polarity of blues, rock and all its variants.
items._cn_summary: 美国芝加哥四人组U.S. Maple于2001年发行的这张专辑被定义为美国前卫摇滚佳作，融合数学摇滚、Captain Beefheart式解构主义与后硬核布鲁斯元素。专辑中角状不和谐音与多节奏编织形成独特的声响结构，人声部分采用近乎超现实的表达方式。评论指出该作品虽具有高度实验性和技术复杂性，却未流于繁琐的即兴演奏，而是保持了紧迫的摇滚能量与布鲁斯根基。Boomkat评论内容详实，深入分析了音乐结构与乐队的艺术追求。作为独立地下厂牌发行的前卫摇滚作品，与用户关注的实验/前卫音乐品味高度匹配，跨领域融合度亦十分突出。

items.body:
Reissued almost 30 years after it arrived at Drag City HQ, U.S. Maple's third album was produced by Michael Gira and sharpens their noisy, Beefheart-inspired deconstructions, forming a nail-biting atmosphere of microtonal clangs, half-sung vocals and aborted rhythms that's still way, way out on its own.

U.S. Maple might get lumped in with Don Caballero and Shellac, but the further removed we are from peak math rock era, the more different they hit. In fact, listening back to 'Talker' now, it sounds more in line with gear from peers like Brainiac, Royal Trux and Gastr del Sol - it's hardly surprising to us that it was Jim O'Rourke who recommended them to Drag City back in 1999. And it was a prescient signing; they only released three more records but became one of the Chicago label's most defining acts. 'Talker' was a mark in the sand, a break from their Skin Graft era that showed a darker side to their sound: noisier, heavier, bleaker material that seemed to balance on Al Johnson's pained delivery and Mark Shippy and Todd Rittman's intertwined, dissonant riffs. For his part, drummer Pat Samson (who would leave the band just a couple of years after 'Talker' was tracked) seems to control the chaos, leaving fragments of rhythms in its dark corners, rather than laying down any kind of driving forward motion.

Musically, 'Talker' follows few of the math rock scene's core aesthetics. Johnson owes more to Pere Ubu's David Thomas, while the rest of the band seem to be deconstructing post-punk and no-wave standards in the same way that 'Trout Mask Replica' dispersed blues and country. There's even a waft of Keiji Haino's cracked noise/psychedelia when Johnson bellows over his bandmates' tempestuous roar of tangled strings and thudding, fractured rhythms. Hilariously, U.S. Maple toured with Pavement when 'Talker' was released, opening to boos from the crowds of frat slackers. Thankfully, the experience led them to dub the intricately divisive 'Acre Thrills', which might be even stronger. Crucial listening.
items._cn_summary: U.S. Maple的《Talker》是一部实验摇滚与后朋克解构的力作，融合了数学摇滚、无浪潮与Captain Beefheart式的声音分解。人声部分借鉴Pere Ubu的David Thomas，配合错综复杂的无调性riffs与碎片化的节奏结构，营造出混沌而可控的声响景观。乐队受Keiji Haino噪音迷幻影响，展现出强烈的实验性与原创性。这张专辑超越了数学摇滚的框架，呈现出独特的艺术视角，是90年代实验摇滚场景中极具个性的作品。

items.body:
Sydney-based drummer Laurence Pike lands on Balmat with a solo fusion of jazz, post-rock and trip-hop that nestles between Burnt Friedman, Makaya McCraven and Barry Adamson.

Remember Pivot? Or Triosk? The Leaf-signed experimental jazz outfit that famously fabricated the ace '1+3+1' LP with Jan Jelinek way back in 2003? Pike's been active on the international scene for what seems like forever - he even joined Liars in 2018. And 'Possible Utpias...' is his follow-up to 2024's ambitious "requiem mass for drums, electronics and choir" 'The Undreamt-of Centre'. Thankfully, this one's a little more approachable than that; there's no quartet to be found, it's just Pike and his gear, imagining what kind of music a jazz musician from an "idealized culture of the future" might make. 

It's a fascinating concept that drives a selection of impeccably played and produced sketches that Pike fleshes out with a little help from his friends: Ben Lerner on alto horn and Novak Manojlovic on keys. But it's Pike's affair and he's most successful when he disregards jazz altogether. On the excellent 'Night Bird', a whirring beat is juxtaposed with Michael Mann-like FM synths and an eerie, wide-open environment and the title track relegates Pike's percussion to the deep background, letting it scrape and scratch beneath dreamy electric piano repetitions.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由悉尼鼓手Laurence Pike发行于独立厂牌Balmat，融合了爵士、后摇与Trip-hop元素。专辑概念围绕“理想未来文化中的爵士乐”展开，Pike邀请了Ben Lerner和Novak Manojlovic参与录制。在'Night Bird'中，旋转的节拍与Michael Mann式的FM合成器相结合，营造出空旷深邃的氛围；标题曲则将鼓声置于背景层，配合梦幻的电子钢琴循环。专辑最成功之处在于Pike对爵士框架的突破——他更倾向于运用实验性的声响设计而非传统爵士语法。这种融合实验性、创新概念与小众独立厂牌的特质，与用户的实验/前卫、学院派爵士、电子音乐偏好高度匹配。

items.body:
In 'The Rhythm of Design', Zurich-based fine arts duo Michael Meier & Christoph Franz explore urban displacement and its impact on the local music scene.

"Focusing on six venues that have disappeared or are under threat, the artists collected materials on site - wood, metal, and other architectural elements and, with the support of professional instrument builders, transformed them into six musical instruments. Six artists and groups connected to these spaces, namely Kalabrese, Tobibi Ferrari-Bienz, Rafal Skoczek, Lucien Badoux & Jeremy Sauter, Nicola Kazimir, and Dualism each composed a piece for them, forming the basis for site-specific performances in September 2025. Rather than performing as an ensemble, the works ranging from experimental funk and punk to kraut, noise, and drone unfolded simultaneously in spatial fragments at the original locations. Only through movement and listening across the city did the composition emerge as a whole. The work was realized in collaboration with the City of Zurich, Art in Public Space (KiöR). Eight months after the original performances took place, the pieces are released via Switzerland-based publishing platform Präsens Editionen."
items._cn_summary: 苏黎世艺术二人组Michael Meier & Christoph Franz将六处已消失或面临拆除的场所的建筑材料转化为乐器，邀请六组艺术家创作实验 funk、punk、kraut、noise 与 drone 风格的作品。这些分散在城市原址的场地特定表演，要求听众通过移动和聆听来拼凑完整的音乐体验。建筑材料的声音转化、城市空间与音乐的互动关系，以及多风格并置的实验性构思，都与用户的实验/前卫和电子音乐偏好高度契合。由瑞士小众厂牌 Präsens Editionen 发行，兼具艺术概念完整性与声音实验价值。

items.body:
Forever Records presents an extensive reissue edition of the first 'fully released' Psychick Warriors Ov Gaia album.

"Dancing on the wildest edge of the 90s outsider techno zeitgeist while proudly independent of any so-called scene, Ov Biospheres And Sacred Grooves: A Document Ov New Edge Folk Classics is both of its time and out of time. Rooted in the experiments of electronic music pioneers, industrial culture and ethnic music from around the globe while responding to the house and techno explosion, Robbert Heynen, Reinier Brekelmans, Reinoud van den Broek and Tim Freeman's freewheeling masterpiece takes in lush electronica and murky abstraction on its singular voyage through parts unknown.

Originally released in 1992, this is the first time the full, previously CD-only, version of Ov Biospheres and Sacred Grooves will be pressed on vinyl. The original LP and CD artwork from the various editions released in the early 90s has been combined and designed by the band, and the audio has been remastered with their full approval. 

Forever Records is a reissue series dedicated to rediscovering lost musical treasures from across the spectrum of head-feeding, heart-rending electronic music. Established by Rush Hour co-founder Christiaan Macdonald and Delsin founder Marsel van der Wielen, Forever Records places heartfelt faith in a carefully curated sequence of seminal, largely forgotten records from disparate eras, scenes and spaces within electronic music history. Tipped towards the mellow and introspective, these are albums that stop time when the needle hits the groove, stirring only when it's time to flip over before you sink back into the experience. That's what albums were always meant to be about, back then, right now, always and forever."
items._cn_summary: 荷兰实验电子四人组Psychick Warriors Ov Gaia于1992年发行的地下 techno 杰作，由独立厂牌Forever Records重制发行。专辑融合了实验电子、工业文化与世界民族音乐元素，在自由即兴与程序化声响之间游走。评论指出其“游走于90年代边缘 techno 时代精神的最狂野边缘”，同时吸收全球 Ethnic 音乐传统，以“丰富的电子音乐与模糊的抽象声响”构建独特的听觉空间。Forever Records由Rush Hour与Delsin联合创始人创立，致力于发掘电子音乐史上的失落珍宝。 remastered版本整合了早期各版本的原始视觉元素，完整呈现这支非主流地下乐队的艺术愿景。作为实验电子与世界音乐融合的跨界之作，其独立精神与创新性高度契合目标用户的审美偏好。

items.body:
This is pure class! Bobby Ingham’s darkly cinematic debut LP seriously strikes a nerve for admirers of Space Afrika, Mark Leckey, Burial & Low End Activist with its evocation of life in C.21st West Yorkshire manifest in a tensely paranoid, homesick patch-work of knifed samples wrapped up in weightless grime & UKG structures

‘Angel Of The North’ inarguably hits a high water mark of Sneaker Social Club’s retro-futurist UK fixations with a deeply impressive demonstration of sound design tekkerz at the service of immersive, narrative-driven impressionism. For 30 mins the 24 year old Ingham belies his yung years with a grasp of melancholic pathos, atmospheric subtlety and articulate crud that one may expect from an artist years his senior. He effectively has us rapt front to back, from the frisson of noctilucent pads and dread subs in ‘Lynne’ to the lush resolution of ‘I Can’t Believe It’, hustling listeners heavy into what the label term a “social-realist inversion of sound system music that relishes negative space while telling a street-level story.”

That story is most suggestively limned via judicious sampling from a mix of personal and public archives, diffused across a spectra of ghostly, ephemeral arrangements perfused with flashes of the music he grew up with; from snatches of Wonder & T2 in the chamber grime abstract ‘Easy Mush’, thru skipping UKG reduced to Burial-esque degrees on ‘WYD Tomorrow Night.’ But it’s the poetic sense of restraint and sensuality that practically makes it a spiritual successor to label boss Low End Activist’s own evocation of life growing up on Oxford council estates (‘Hostile Utopia’ & ‘Municipal Dreams’), and clearly comparable to Mark Leckey’s collaged art-film soundtracks as much as the northern romanticism of Space Afrika’s liminal ambiance, or even EXLRUTH’s chamber adaptations of makina in its dare-to-differ approach and spellbinding effect. 

Big tip!
items._cn_summary: Bobby Ingham的首张专辑由独立厂牌Sneaker Social Club发行，融合grime、UKG与dark ambient元素，展现实验电子的前卫气质。专辑以采样拼贴为核心手法，结合个人与公共档案素材，营造幽灵般的氛围编排。被拿来与Low End Activist、Mark Leckey、Space Afrika等实验艺术家相比，呈现出叙事驱动的印象主义美学。西约克郡的地域特色与工人阶级生活图景贯穿始终，声音设计细腻考究，30分钟内保持高度沉浸感。对于偏好实验/暗潮/电子的用户而言，此作在创新性与艺术性上均达到较高水准。

items.body:
After slaying with her cold fusions of ’90s R&B, ’00s brukfunk and footwork on 2024’s ‘Concentrate’ EP and last year’s ‘Come Alive’ album, NZO returns with a deadly hyper-jiggy session for DDS - huge one FFO Various Production, Beatrice Dillon, Dolo Percussion, Rian Treanor, Akufen, El-B.

Captured at Rotherham Minster (the finest perpendicular church in Yorkshire, don’t u know) for SoYo’s annual electronics music showdown, No Bounds, NZO’s custom-built results brim with an unusual grasp of the funk, prompting a uniquely jittery rush offset with a wicked refusal of rhythmic anticipation that does crazy things with your limbs. With the finest grasp of ghost snares and the confidence to slap and tickle drums where others wouldn’t, she deftly dances thru fresh routes of rhythmic pursuit. Low-key, this sort of experimental ingenuity betrays her background in the sciences, as much as a keen ear for offbeat and upfront dance musics -  effortlessly joining and short-circuiting oblique dots between Timbaland x The Neptunes’ rugged nuance, El-B’s whipsmart torsion, RP Boo’s legwork and Beatrice Dillon’s precision-tooled arrangements, all gelled with daring confidence in her own thing. 

We can't tell you if NZO's a DJ or nah, but she approaches her set with a serious understanding of how to take control of your limbs, linking rhythms, samples and melodic phrases as if she's grandstanding on four CDJs. She rushes towards euphoria with truncated R&B coos that she expertly threads between dub stabs and garage-y organ vamps, keeping the jerky rhythms intact throughout. And just when you think you've tapped in, sugar-sweet vocals and brassy fanfares cut into a shudder of drums, an 'ANTI EP'-era AE bass whoosh comes out of nowhere to remind you where you are. 

NZO patches together an authentically Yorkshire-coded reaction to New York's post-GHE20G0TH1K evolution, the self-consciously p2p-driven movement that helped shape visionary DJs like Total Freedom and Juliana Huxtable. But she’s less conspicuously "deconstructed" than her predecessors and champions Sheffield's avant history, referencing Warp's early run, Mark Fell's continuous influence and the perpetual grind of heavy industry, blending these elements with her spectrum of influences from further afield. Freaky, hyper-articulated movers need to check it at the nearest opportunity, trust.
items._cn_summary: NZO的现场演出专辑展现了实验电子音乐的多元融合，将90年代R&B、brukfunk、footwork与dub、garage等元素巧妙交织。评论强调其独特的节奏掌控能力和不循规蹈矩的音乐结构，创造出带有jittery质感的funk感。专辑中融入了Yorkshire地区文化和Sheffield的前卫音乐传统，结合Warped早期美学与当代舞曲元素。评论详细分析了其声音设计、节奏编排和跨流派融合方式，突显了音乐中的创新精神和自信态度。Boomkat作为独立乐评平台提供了深入的分析视角，整体评论具有原创性和专业性。对于关注实验电子和跨领域融合的听众而言，这是一张值得关注的作品。

items.body:
A seminal, early highlight of shoegaze that helped birth the idea of “dream pop”, also serving as a blueprint of sorts for Dean Blunt's world of sound, A.R. Kane’s debut album is among the most under-sung, yet foundational, records of its time. 

A.R. Kane were no doubt an anomaly in their field - far as we know, the only Black band of musicians operating in British indie-pop-rock music - which only makes their dare-to-be-different style even more exceptional, in hindsight. They would famously go on to create a major touchstone of acid house and dance-pop with their über-classic ‘Pump Up The Volume’ as M/A/R/R/S, but before that they released debut album ’SIxty Nine’, laying out a template for psychedelic, grooving pop music that remains practically peerless in its field, with echoes of its sound heard everywhere from Micachu & The Shapes to Dean Blunt in the current day. 

After 32 years ’Sixty Nine’ remains a most beautiful sore thumbs-up, with tenderly fragile yet powerful vocals set to a mix of psychedelia, dub, jazz-funk, free jazz spirits and keeling amounts of guitar feedback, in a style that the band’s Alex Ayuli would describe as “dream-pop” - a term which has stuck and blossomed ever since. Mercifully, “dream-pop” provides a catchy phrase for their hard-to-place sound for clumsy writers like we, and is practically the only way to encompass their sound here; taking in the range of their jangling sorta Afrobeat/indie hybrid styles in ‘Crazy Blue’, thru to swooning dub-rock-pop of ‘Baby Milk Snatcher’, the charred guitar feedback scapes of ’Sulliday’, and the thizz of their spine-tracing vox, guitar, and hi-hats in ‘Spermwhale Trip’, alongside the chamber-like oddity of ‘The Madonna Is With Child.’ And considering that it was issued in a pivotal year for new music, it’s always worth listening to Simon Reynolds’ take, who sums up ’69’ very neatly in his review for Melody Maker as “the outstanding record of ’88.”

Seriously there’s nowt quite like this album. A 100% must check if you don’t already know.
items._cn_summary: 这张1988年的专辑被视为shoegaze与dream pop的开创性作品，融合了迷幻、dub、爵士放克、自由爵士精神与Afrobeat等多元风格。乐队作为当时英国独立音乐界唯一的黑人音乐人组合，展现出强烈的实验意识与跨界融合能力。吉他反馈、dub节奏与人声处理构成了独特的声响景观，对后续音乐人产生深远影响。评论指出其"几乎无与伦比"的风格特质，以及对Dean Blunt等当代音乐人的启示意义。作为"dream pop"术语的源头之一，该专辑在实验性与历史价值上都具有重要意义，完全契合偏好实验、前卫与爵士融合的听者口味。

items.body: 28 years after the wintry North, BJ Nilsen has released a surprise companion piece as Hazard. That’s a long time, but as one looks back, one gains perspective on earlier works. Winter is approaching in the Southern Hemisphere, which makes the release date fitting for these regions ~ even if these sounds of snow, ice and wind come from the Arctic north. The title, Pre-Lapsarian, refers to the time before the Fall of Humanity, when everything was innocent and pure. Regardless of one’s theology, it’s easy to hear the Arctic soundscape as pristine and undisturbed, even if to human ears it may sound forlorn and abandoned. A soft drone and cold wind launch the recording into the frigid air. Nilsen’s footsteps can be heard amid the quiet rustle, crunching into the snow. Louder sounds in the fourth minute suggest snapping trees and an approaching storm, and as soon as the danger is registered, the pitch of the wind rises. Many artists incorporate field recordings into their music or the other way around, but Nilsen is one of the masters. Allowing the natural sounds to dictate their counterparts, he creates passages that sound entirely organic, even when one knows they are not. Pre-Lapsarian conveys the stark beauty of the Arctic landscape while sculpting a sonic narrative: the distillation of a winter event. When the sound levels subside in the eighth minute, one feels as if one has survived a necessary foray outside one’s shelter and returned just in time. The weather remains frightful, but as the zipper to the tent is re-secured, the field recordist is again safe and sound. (Richard Allen) Available here
items._cn_summary: 这是BJ Nilsen以Hazard名义发布的实验环境音乐作品，时隔28年推出前作《the wintry North》的延续篇。专辑采用北极圈极地风声、雪地脚步、折裂树枝等田野录音素材，与低沉嗡鸣和人造音效交织融合，构建出一幅冰冷荒寂的北极风景声景。评论者称Nilsen为田野录音与音乐融合的大师，强调其声场设计完全有机且难以辨认真假。作品聚焦前堕落时期的纯净意象，通过声学叙事手法描绘一场冬日风暴从逼近到消退的完整过程，听者仿佛经历了一次在风雪中从庇护所外出又返回的生存体验。此作深度契合实验/前卫、电子氛围、暗潮黑暗环境音乐等用户偏好范畴，兼具极地区域特色与跨领域融合的艺术原创性，属于独立/地下性质的深度实验制作。

items.body: Review by siLLy puPPy — An utterly unique band to emerge in Spain's late 70s prog scene, AZAHAR which was named after anorange blossom flower and really did bloom into its own unique cultivar of musical ingenuity thatcould be referred to as something like symphonic progressive space Rock Andaluz. This band was oneof the first progressive bands to emerge in 1976 after the collapse of the Franco regime anddelivered two extraordinary albums in its three year run before exiting the scene in 1979. Despiteits short run the band had a significantly different lineup on its two albums with only vocalistDick Zappala and guitarist Antonio Valls appearing on the two releases. On this debut ELIXIR whichcame out in 1977, keyboardist Gusatovo Ros and bassist Jorge Barrai filled the remaining slots.AZAHAR was a very rare breed in that it managed to release an entire album with no drummer to befound which is practically unheard of in any sort of rock music. Instead the primary rhythmicbackbone was delivered by the thumping bass grooves. An elegant album that featured seven distinct track that didn't quite reach the 38 minute mark,ELIXIR featured extremely lush and complex keyboard arrangements accompanied by catchy flamencoinfused melodies along with passionate vocals as well as driving rock guitar heft and heavy bassgrooves sounding something like an oddball mix of Triana, the French space rock act Pulsar, thepastoral folky aspects of Genesis along with knotty prog time signature workouts and unexpectedtransitions. Add to that beautiful Middle Eastern melodic touches all completely forged without theaid of a drummer. The extra emphasis is clearly on the rich layers of synthesizers, Fender Rhodesand mellotrons but the flamenco and rock guitar parts are very much in the forefront much of thetime as well. Very much in vein of the Rock Urbano that was underway, AZAHAR delivered passionateSpanish lyrics emulating the style of the Italian prog scene however the Andalusian flamenco kept itfirmly on Spanish territory.The opening "Campos de Azahar" ushers in the album with larger than life layers of keyboard swellswhich sets the tone for the space rock aspects of the album and it's not until well into the secondtrack "�Qu� malo hay, se�or juez?" that the rock guitar kicks in and then game on as the bandengages in one of those dialogue albums where the keys and guitar parts sound like their talking toeach other. The third track "�Es que esto no tiene nombre!" introduces a greater emphasis on moreangular progressive complexities time signatures run amok, hairpin turns into varying motifs and amost satisfying scorching acid rock soloing sequence that trades off with the keys in unique ways.In some ways it reminds me of what Symphony X would latch onto a couple decades down the road onlythis track is more like the ridiculously extreme crafty complex antics of bands like the ArgentineanAlas or Italian masters Museo Rosenbach. Some of the keyboards remind me of the French zeuhl actArcha�a when sustained oscillating high notes roar above it all.The balance between instrumental development and vocal led structured songs give the album abeautifully eclectic style as well as the dynamics shifting from more pastoral sensual folky motifsand then into crescendoing uproars of keys and guitars getting wild. Vocal aspects are diverse aswell with not only passionately delivered lyrics out of the Italian prog playbook but also findmoments of group harmonies. Extra touches from the mandolin and Middle Eastern rhythms weaved intothe flamenco and symphonic prog is beautifully performed. Other tracks such as "Mercaderes," "UnHombre Cansado" and "Cantaros de Fuego" continue the magic with the latter offering some of thecoolest bass lines in prog but the highlight may be the closing three part suit "Viaja a Marruecos"which wastes no time delivering the prog goods with an endless parade of variations throughsymphonic prog turf alternating with Spanish folk featuring Zappala's fluid vocal style. While nodrummer is one board a bit of exotic percussion actually finds its way onto this track offering someof the best excursions into Middle Eastern sounds. The band delivers on all pistons offering thisamazing climactic closer that ends in with a frenzied cyclical loop that ends the prog party well.I guess i'm on the opposite spin of most regarding this album considering how low its generallyrated but for my tastes this is one of my absolute favorite prog albums of the entire Spanish sceneand as far as Rock Andaluz bands go this band does it for me much more than Triana and other actsdue to the fact that this band had a creative edge unlike any other in Spain or anywhere for thatmatter. This album stands out as an utterly unique example of prog ingenuity nurtured in every waydelivering top notch melodies, brilliant arrangements and an even more impressive execution of itall. This album IMHO imbues the very essence of what Spanish prog was all about in the late 1970ssounding like all of the bands of the era rolled into one with the exception the jazz fusionists asthis album does not delve into jazz fueled frenzies however some of the most sophisticated progmoves do match that level of ingenuity. This is literally one of those albums i can listen torepeatedly and never tired of. Masterpiece in my book.
items._cn_summary: 西班牙1977年发行的前卫摇滚专辑，以无鼓手编制和贝斯驱动节奏为核心特色。专辑融合了安达卢西亚弗拉门戈旋律、中东音乐元素与古典先驱乐队的复杂编曲特征，键盘部分强调合成器、Fender Rhodes和Mellotron的丰富层次，同时弗拉门戈与摇滚吉他也占据重要位置。七个曲目以时间签名变换丰富、段落转换突兀著称，呈现出意大利前卫与阿根廷乐队Alas般的极端技术性。这种将西班牙民间音乐、空间摇滚与古典前卫融合的独特风格，使其成为1970年代西班牙前卫摇滚中极具独创性的作品。

items.body: Review by siLLy puPPy — One of the most important underground innovators of the psychedelic years in the former Soviet Unionwas the Crimean born YURI MOROZOV (later settling in St Petersburg) who was a multidisciplinarymulti-instrumentalist, sound engineer and prolific composer having released well over 50 albums thattackled virtually every modern genre of the era. Completely banned by the Soviet authorities anddenied access to the state label Melodiya, MOROZOV took matters into his own hands by releasing hismusic through the clandestine "samizdat" tape-trading networks which of course were totally illegalbut provided the means for experimental artists who dabbled out of the confines of the strict Sovietcensorship to release their music to the greater public at large.While the USSR was way behind the curve as far as Western musical innovations were concerned,bootlegs still infiltrated beyond the Iron Curtain and influences were adopted. What was really rarethough was for an artist to successfully record in such abundance and release dozens of recordingsto the public all without the sanctity of the state. MOROZOV was not only one of the most prolificand successful of these artists but one of the most wildly experimental. In fact i've never heardanything from USSR that matches his wild excursions into total psychedelic escapism as MOROZOV's 70sreleases with this one, "Сон в красном тереме (Dream of the Red Chamber)" sitting as one of the mostuninhibited albums of all to emerge from the former USSR.This renowned tape recording that finally found a vinyl release in 2014 was recorded between 1973and 1976 although the official date by some is 1975. Apparently the original release featured lesstracks than the 2014 reissue and like all Soviet artifacts from the past, especially from the deepunderground remains a little murky in details but one thing is for sure and that is the fact MOROZOVtruly captured the spirit of the psychedelic 60s and took it all the way to the level of the mostkosmische trip out musical statements of the German Krautrock scene. This album is based on aconcept adopted from the Chinese novel called "Dream Of The Red Chamber" but the musical flow ismore akin to a psychological mind trip taking the most lysergic aspects of psychedelic rock to theirmost terrifying limits. MOROZOV was a master of overdubbing and sound manipulation, sort of theAchim Reichel of the USSR only with a bit of Daevid Allen's Gong thrown in for good measure.The album original featured two versions of the title track broken down into two parts. Highlyexperimental in nature, the music features psychedelic rock, Russian folk, progressive rock and lotsof the earliest examples of the Soviet electronic music scene. It's a shape shifting type of albumthat goes for the psychedelic jugular. Many will find this aimless and simply self-indulgent as it'sa really difficult album to follow. Is there any point to it at all? Well, who knows. It sounds veryimprovisational with little to latch onto as far as structured compositions are concerned howeverit's psychedelic after all and if the aim of the genre is to create an ethereal otherworldly effectwhere the status quo is blissfully ignored and replaced by a consciousness recalibration sessionthen this is indeed the ticket especially considering the time and place of its creation. It's verymuch a dream state kind of album and in that regard it's brilliant. While the musical motifs are very non-musical there are plenty of avant-garde excursions thatimplement patterns of some sort. It's like listening to alien music in that regard. MOROZOV hasoften been called the Soviet version of Sun Ra and that would be quite fitting indeed as thisrelease is very much like Sun Ra's most "out there" moments even if it's not rooted in jazz.Obviously not to everyone's tastes but for the moments when i really want to take a deep dive intoextremely surreal soundscapes and simple psych flavored pop just won't cut it, albums like this riseto the top of the ranks and for my liking this is pure genius in how it exemplifies the spectrum ofthe most underground sounds compiled into a menagerie of free form psychedelic through the 65 minuteplaying time that is available for sampling (forget finding a real copy!) A true underground Sovietclassic here!4.5 rounded down
items._cn_summary: 苏联地下实验先驱YURI MOROZOV于1975年前后录制的这张专辑，是前苏联 psychedelic/space rock 领域最具突破性的作品之一。出生于克里米亚的 MOROZOV 作为多器乐演奏者和音响工程师，在官方渠道被封禁的情况下通过地下 samizdat 网络发行了大量作品。这张基于中国古典文学《红楼梦》概念的专辑，融合了迷幻摇滚、俄罗斯民谣、前卫摇滚以及早期苏联电子音乐元素，展现出惊人的声音实验性。MOROZOV 精通叠加录音和声音操控技术，其即兴与实验的结合方式被评论者比作德国 Krautrock 运动中的 Achim Reichel，带有 Gong 乐队的超现实主义色彩。专辑呈现出不断变化的形态，将迷幻音乐推向心理极限，是苏联地下音乐史上一张罕见的高度不受约束的实验之作，1973至1976年录制，直到2014年才正式发行黑胶版本。

items.body: After the extra-terrestial explorations of Eventyrferd, the previous album from Norway's Camilla Hole Trio, in which sci-fi synth sounds were married with traditional material, their latest release Langs is rather more earthbound. But the quest to look beyond their own country's folk music continues. Camilla Hole's main instrument being the soprano sax, the influence of jazz is unsurprising and this is evident in the opening track “Springleik,” signifying a tune used to accompany the springleik dance from the west of Norway. Initially Hole takes the melody with Egil Kalman and Knut Kvifte Nesheim providing rhythmic support on double bass and drums respectively, with the overdubbing of Kalman's modular synth and Nesheim's vibraphone adding colour. But characteristically for this trio, in which assigned roles are never clearly defined or adhered to, things soon start to move around, with Kalman taking up the melody on his bass, playing the melody in unison with Hole, while Nesheim opens things out further rhythmically. As the whole piece takes on a much more improvisatory feel, Hole plays the melody one more time as things draw to a close.
items._cn_summary: 挪威Camilla Hole Trio的新专辑《Langs》将传统民谣与现代爵士及电子声响相融合。乐队以高音萨克斯为核心，在三重奏编制中融入模块化合成器和颤音琴等元素，形成了传统与实验并存的声景。评论中描述的“角色定义模糊”体现了乐队去中心化的演奏方式，萨克斯手与低音提琴手交替演奏旋律，即兴段落与民谣素材自然交织。专辑延续了前作《Eventyrferd》的探索精神，但更趋于内省。作为独立厂牌发行的小众作品，这张专辑在即兴爵士的框架内融入了北欧传统舞蹈音乐元素，适合关注实验爵士与世界音乐融合的听众。

items.body: When one is asked to summarize one’s travels, for Verónica Cerrotta a month in the city of Valparaíso and a pair of festival appearances, one may respond in varying fashions. On Álbum de Viaje, Cerrotta offers a pair of side-long soundscapes; one travels through time and space, while the other condenses time. Together, they offer complementary ways of preserving experience through sound. The pieces of “Valparaíso” were collected as one might collect souvenirs: scrap by scrap, sound by sound. At first there is only a background hum, then the tapping and swirling of solid objects: metal, plastic, concrete? Then the first confident splash, accompanied by the sounds of workers by the sea. Traffic builds as the city comes to life. A child is playing in the distance, along with whistles and a brass symphony of undulating horns. If only all traffic were this way, offering something good along with the bad! The brass gives way to tinkling wind chimes, as one imagines the amalgamation of all the chimes from all the houses, ringing in time. The tin sound of a radio breaks through, the worker’s best friend. A massive wave bisects the composition, prefacing the appearance of sea lions and hungry gulls. As the velocity of the waves decreases, so does the biophony. A plane passes overhead, seemingly close. Church bells toll, marking time for the dockworkers. Glorious rain on tin roofs creates a percussionist’s paradise, followed by found objects used as percussion. Cerrotta has turned her idyllic month into a photo album of sound. “Otras Ciudades” takes a different approach, traveling backwards in time as it traces two festival appearances with Cerrotta’s band a.hop. “The world is ending,” an unidentified narrator begins; but in truth it is not; it is instead unwinding. A happy get-together in Berlin is accompanied by more church bells, louder than before: in this instance the chronic marker is questioned as the very concept of time is challenged. Small groups of people mill about; a dog barks; the bells continue to ring. The soundscape will eventually move through nations as well as days. The second movement begins with footsteps, first on solid ground and then seemingly through fallen leaves. Who can resist a good leaf patch? Even the nearby birds are laughing. Snippets of conversation are heard, dissolving into patches of music, a local musician, and even more bells. A barge approaches, sounding a warning. The water in this piece connects to the water in the first. Ironically, in concert people come to hear Cerrotta, where Cerrotta shares what she has heard, which in some cases may be the sounds created by audience members themselves. Viaje is a word with various interrelated meanings: trip, travel, journey. Álbum de Viaje honors all three. In the 17th minute, one hears the sound of what may be a map unfolding: a tactile way to approach travel. By the end, because the chronology is reversed, Cerrotta has not returned home, but remembered who she was before she left, when the map was just a map and each sound now heard was only a sound imagined. (Richard Allen)
items._cn_summary: 这是一张来自拉丁美洲的实验性音景专辑，艺术家Verónica Cerrotta通过采集城市生活声音素材构建两部时长较长的声音拼贴作品。第一部分“Valparaíso”以城市苏醒为主题，从环境底噪逐步加入交通、人声、海浪等生活片段；第二部分“Otras Ciudades”采用逆向时间叙事，呈现音乐节演出场景与城市环境的交织。专辑体现了典型的实验/环境音乐特征，使用采样和拼贴手法，强调声音的纹理与空间感。作为独立艺术家的创作，兼具声音艺术的实验性与拉丁美洲地区文化特色，适合偏好实验音乐和环境音景的听众。

items.body: A really enjoyable eerie, isolationist and wistful electronic ambient release with enough ideas and well-designed textures to enthrall the listener. Emotional despair collides with surreal, unearthly motifs Meldrop by IUGA   Unexplained Sounds Group, Eighth Tower and ZeroK represent a small community of labels headed by Raffaele Pezzella (alias Sonologyst) and which participate actively in the promotion of spaced-out/experimental and post-industrial ambient music. Each label has its own field of specialization. Unexplained Sounds Group easily represents the most abstract and conceptually inclined sonic soundscapes of the three mentioned above, delivering a body of work from confirmed projects to promising acts coming from a vast array of cultural and geographical cradles. IUGA is a totally new project; few informations are available online, but the least we can say is that it is a welcoming addition to the label’s usual sound signature. As illustrated by the cover artwork, the listener is invited to be immersed in a profound, deep, then isolated and menacing, harrowing, brainy musical bath where emotional despair collides with surreal, unearthly motifs. The atmospheres are partly soothing, darkly meditative, but also uncanny, foreboding, ghoulish. Massive hypnotic drone textures interact with broken electronic signals, technological derelicts, echoing concrete sounds and cyber-like flowing movements. The album also plays with various pitches, filters and sonic sound-expanding techniques. A track such as “Aspis” develops impeccable and transportive otherworldly tones. The whole thing will lead you to a dystopian futuristic world or to some long-forgotten eras. Some parts admit more soothing sequences, such as the repetitive and nebulous “Porcupine Quills.” The closing theme is a dynamic, eroded, meandering, then progressively corrosive, distorted ambient epilogue for looping textures and processing chains of micro-sounds: slow movements evolve through an infinitely static structure. Somewhere between Bad Sector, Kristoff Oustad, Vestigial, Reutoff, The Haxan Cloak—with a fancy for cryptic, strange and molecular sound explorations that won’t deny pioneering figures in bleak industrial/power electronics. A really enjoyable eerie, isolationist and wistful electronic ambient release with enough ideas and well-designed textures to enthrall the listener. Meldrop is available on Unexplained Sounds Group. [Bandcamp] Meldrop by IUGA
items._cn_summary: IUGA的《Meldrop》是一张充满实验性的暗潮电子氛围专辑，由意大利独立厂牌Unexplained Sounds Group发行。音乐融合了催眠式Drone纹理、破碎电子信号、技术废墟声效与赛博流动感，营造出深沉、隔离且带有威胁性的声景。情感绝望与超现实元素在其中碰撞交织，既有暗黑冥想的舒缓段落，也有诡异不祥的紧张氛围。专辑运用了多样的音高变化、滤波器处理和声音扩展技术，呈现出末日未来主义或远古时代的意境。与Bad Sector、Reutoff等暗潮工业先驱形成呼应，同时保持了独特的艺术视角。制作精良、概念完整，是暗潮与实验电子跨界融合的佳作。

items.body: Kristof Bathory brought Dawn Of Ashes to life in 2000. The first albums by this American artist were released through the now-defunct Noitekk label, immediately grabbing listeners by the throat with their raw, icy, and uncompromising blend of Dark-Electro and Aggrotech. More than twenty years later, this musical visionary can look back on a rich and successful career during which the project evolved through several distinct eras — from its original Dark-Electro-driven sound to Industrial-Metal, before ultimately returning to its Electronic roots on the previous opus, now infused with the Cinematic influences Bathory also explores in his solo work. With over two decades of dark visions, sonic aggression, and constant musical transformation, Kristof Bathory remains one of the most uncompromising figures within the scene. With “Anatomy Of Suffering,” released on Metropolis this spring, he not only confirms his return to a more Electronic approach, but also delivers a remarkably mature work in which he continues his meticulous exploration of mental anguish and psychological suffering. Dawn Of Ashes has always remained a project with a striking visual identity, perfectly aligned with the disturbing themes it addresses. As a listener, you can feel the suffering permeating every aspect of the project, balanced by a profound artistic vision and emotional depth. Time for a conversation with the artist himself. (Courtesy by Inferno Sound Diaries) Dawn Of Ashes interview Q: What does Dawn Of Ashes mean to you after more than a quarter of a century of existence, and what comes to mind spontaneously when you look back, even just for a moment? And, with the knowledge and experience you have today, what would you like to say to the young Kristof Bathory of the year 2000? Kristof: Dawn Of Ashes is an ongoing, evolving reflection of myself, revealing the different phases of my maturity and growth through both the music and the lyrics. There are things I can unearth from the past and give new purpose to in the present, and there are other things better left buried deep within the tomb. If I could speak to my younger self, early Kristof, I would tell him to make wiser decisions and to have patience before making impulsive choices. Q: Your new album “Anatomy Of Suffering” seems to leave little room for interpretation, but could you still tell us a bit more about it? What is the backstory of this opus, how personal is it, and how did you translate it into music? Kristof: “Anatomy Of Suffering” is a descent into the mind of suicide, pain, and the grotesque rot that festers within as a result of severe mental corrosion. It is both a deeply personal expression and a means of connecting with those who endure this same inner decay. Q: Psychological suffering has long been a recurring theme in your work, and I sometimes wonder how introspective and therapeutic music can be. Could it not also lead to even more suffering? What fascinates me is how obscure, dark, and even destructive themes can culminate in an artistic peak. How do you perceive that process? Kristof: I suppose it all depends on how you interpret it and how you absorb it. Art is subjective—it can either reflect destruction or illuminate a path toward blissfulness. Sometimes, suffering is a necessary part of healing. Q: Your music and influences have clearly evolved over the years, and your latest albums seem to represent a kind of synthesis: a return to the Dark-Electro of your early years combined with the Metal and Industrial influences that followed. How did this evolution come about, and what different stages did you go through to arrive at the final result of “Anatomy Of Suffering”? Kristof: My return to Dark-Electro is not only a response to the demand from the fans, but also a result of all the work I’ve done in the Dark-Ambient world. My love for synthesizers and Eurorack modular systems reignited my passion for Electronic music. While I haven’t completely drifted away from Metal, I’ve become far more selective with it, finding myself increasingly drawn to Electronic and Ambient music instead. Q: Now that Dawn Of Ashes is leaning more towards its Electronic side again, I assume this also impacts your live performances. How is that going these days, and do you notice a different audience or fanbase attending your shows? Kristof: Dawn Of Ashes is now more focused on performing both the older Dark-Electro material and the newer Dark-Electro work. We’re putting live Metal performances on pause for now, as this approach makes touring easier and allows us to focus more fully on the Industrial side of the live experience. Q: A final question that I consider quite important concerns the visual aspect that Dawn Of Ashes has always invested in. I’m thinking, for instance, of the music video for “Viral Decay” from the new album. What are your thoughts and experiences regarding a current zeitgeist in which ‘wokeism’ on the one hand and algorithm-driven censorship culture on the other stand in stark contrast to what you create? Kristof: To be honest, I’ve been much more careful with the visual side of things, as I feel some of the early Dawn Of Ashes themes leaned too heavily into edgelord aesthetics and shock for the sake of shock. Now, everything needs to carry substance and meaning. If the content is controversial, it has to symbolize something deeper—something metaphorical rather than merely provocative.
items._cn_summary: Dawn Of Ashes是美国暗黑电子先驱项目，由Kristof Bathory于2000年创立。专辑《Anatomy Of Suffering》延续其从Dark-Electro到Industrial-Metal再回归电子的演变脉络，并融入Cinematic氛围元素。音乐风格延续raw、icy、uncompromising的暗黑电子美学，同时探索心理痛苦与精神折磨等深层次主题。项目以强烈的视觉身份著称，歌词与音乐共同构建阴暗而内省的艺术空间。作为跨越二十余年的独立厂牌艺术家，其在暗潮与电子领域的持续探索与风格迭代体现了相当的实验精神，与用户关注的暗潮、电子及实验音乐方向高度契合。

items.body: Henrik Karlsson might ring a bell for fans of Seven Trees. However, it has been several years since this Swedish project released any new material. In the meantime, one of its members, Henrik Karlsson, began releasing his own music under the sonic alter ego Subverge. Four albums have since been released on his own label, Arcane Dirge. A selection of nine tracks from those albums has been brought together on this compilation, “Select”, and supplemented with three previously unreleased tracks, which also conclude the album. Seven Trees and Subverge are not really comparable, except for their shared Electronic foundations. That said, Subverge appears to draw inspiration from the legacy of Cold Meat Industry. A pronounced Dark-Ambient influence runs throughout the album, although it rapidly evolves into a more Cinematic sound. The result is an overwhelming production built upon an extremely dark undertone, frequently supported by slow rhythms and powerful orchestral percussion. At times, I even detected subtle Tribal elements. Dark strings color the atmosphere, while more delicate piano arrangements provide contrast and depth. Repetitive sequences create a sense of foreboding and further reinforce the album’s gloomy mood. To be fair, I must admit that the three previously unreleased tracks—seemingly older compositions that simply never found their way onto an album—do not add much to the overall experience and therefore offer little real bonus value. Nevertheless, “Select” presents an excellent overview of Subverge’s work and serves as the perfect introduction for newcomers, as well as an ideal opportunity for existing listeners to (re)discover the project. As far as I’m concerned, this is an absolute masterpiece. (Rating:8½). Listen to “Silver Circles”: https://aliensproduction.bandcamp.com/track/silver-circles
items._cn_summary: Subverge是瑞典音乐人Henrik Karlsson的个人电子项目，专辑《Select》精选了九首过往作品并收录三首未发行曲目。音乐以暗黑氛围为基调，融合Dark-Ambient与电影化音景，通过黑暗弦乐铺陈沉郁底色，钢琴编排增添层次对比，慢速节拍与厚重的管弦打击乐构建起压迫感。作品中隐约可见Cold Meat Industry系谱的影响，Tribal元素的融入进一步丰富了声响维度。整体制作精良且具艺术完整性，是探索暗潮与实验电子融合的上乘之作，既适合新听众入门，也可满足资深听众的聆听需求。

items.body:
Italian ambient maestro Gigi Masin returns to his happy place on 'Movement', following 2020's 'Calypso' with a record that surveys a quarter century of vintage back room sounds, pulling from kosmische, new age, early techno, glitch and balearic house. 

For the last few years, Masin has been busy with a litany of collaborations, working with Jonny Nash and Young Marco as Gaussian Curve, with dub techno OG Rod Modell on 2023's 'Red Hair Girl at Lighthouse Beach and with jazz pianist Greg Foat on a ruck of soundtrack-y downtempo material. In fact it's been years since his last solo release; the Apollo-released 'Calypso' came out six years ago and 'Movement' appears to pick up where it left off. The waterlogged, sun-bleached concept is all but gone, but the sounds, cherry-picked from across the downtempo spectrum, are very much in keeping. 

Opener 'Bed on Mars' is classic Masin and should appeal to fans of his cult 1986 breakout 'Wind', the long-overlooked album that featured 'Clouds', that new age/ambient anthem that relaunched his career after it was sampled by both To Rococo Rot and Björk. It's a fleeting moment, but it's packed to the brim with the good stuff: humid post-Vangelis pads, synthetic choirs and reflecting pools of reverb. And the atmosphere's pierced by loping rhythms almost immediately; 'Lost' matches its elasticated brass moans with a low-slung beat and then 'The Age of Sampling' appears to hark back to the Fairlight era, conjuring up an industrial soundscape with jerky low-bitrate drum hits, dialog samples and inclement textures that sound like they belong on Black Rain's 'Neuromancer' soundtrack.

The title track is even more surprising, a slippery 120bpm house groover that sounds as if it's been precision engineered for hazy sunrises, with sax wails and vocal pads ducking behind its rubbery beats. If that sounds a bit much, then there's a few quieter spells, like the piano-led 'UMI' and the Shuttle358-inspired closer 'Fifteen', but you can tell that for Masin, "ambient" doesn't mean beatless. The highlight, 'Deception Dance', sounds like classic beardy back-room techno, even - the sort of twitchy biz Carl Craig used to engineer when he was still moonlighting as 69.
items._cn_summary: 意大利氛围音乐名家Gigi Masin时隔六年推出的新作，专辑回溯二十五年的复古声响，整合了kosmische、新世纪、早期techno、glitch及balearic house等多种元素。整张专辑呈现跨流派融合特征，从ambient的冥想氛围过渡到节奏驱动的舞曲，再延伸至受Shuttle358影响的极简电子收尾。评论详细描述了各曲目的声响特征，包括后Vangelis式的合成器垫、弹性铜管、Fairlight时代的工业节拍以及萨克斯与人声垫的层叠运用。作为独立厂牌发行且涉及意大利音乐人的独特视角，该专辑在实验性与流派跨越上表现出色，符合用户对实验与电子音乐的偏好。

items.body:
Thessa Torsing (aka upsammy) and drum deity Valentina Magaletti consolidate their intentions on 'Seismo', rustling up an illusory combo of artificial and live sonics - properly RIYL early Squarepusher, Matmos or Mira Calix.

When roles are so clearly demarcated, it can be hard to keep things challenging. Magaletti's a percussionist first and foremost, while Torsing is clearly happiest working on the DAW or behind the decks, but neither artist wanted their collaboration to be quite so predictable. So they figured out a way to make their respective roles  a little more complicated; after recording Magaletti's acoustic parts in Amsterdam's labyrinthine Rijksmuseum, Torsing decided to compliment them with digital percussion - mallet-style instruments that mimic or at least harmonize with Magaletti's elements. The result is a puzzling assembly of samples, sequences and breathless improvisations that injects some much-needed energy into the '90s Artificial Intelligence scaffolding Torsing has been respraying for the last few years.

Opener 'It comes to an end' yanks us back to Squarepusher's beardy jazz crossover era, or Matmos's ace early electroacoustic experiments. But Torsing and Magaletti keep things fresh, offsetting their ornate biomechanical flurries with Reich-ian minimalist phrases and xenharmonic prangs that keep us on our toes. It's unashamedly percussive material and yet plays like a sequence of lullabies, its virtuosic drumwork (just check the smoove editing on 'Superimposed') almost inevitably offset by music box chimes or cloudy, dreamlike pads. The other element that sets the duo apart is the vocals; peppered throughout the album are dialog snippets that keep things confusing, countering their surreal twangs and iceberg-cracking whirrs with alien whispers that only just permeate the membrane.

Is there even a voice on 'Hyperlocalize', or is it just our imagination? We can't be quite sure. But the garbled syllables are more audible on 'Mementoes', sandwiched between soothing, rubbery lead synths and hallucinated xylophones. Needless to say, if you're into anything from Plaid to Midori Takada, this'll be worth a closer listen.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是荷兰实验音乐人Thessa Torsing与意大利打击乐手Valentina Magaletti的合作作品，融合了数字打击乐与现场录音。专辑在阿姆斯特丹国立博物馆录制声学部分，随后叠加数字音效采样，呈现出生物机械感与梦幻氛围并存的声景。音乐风格承袭90年代人工智能派电子乐的实验传统，同时融入Reich式简约主义与异调音乐元素。打击乐即兴与程序化音序的边界在此模糊，现场演奏的呼吸感与电子音色相互映衬，采样的人声片段更增添了超现实的听觉体验。对于偏好实验电子、IDM与自由爵士的听众而言，这是一张兼具技术复杂度与声音锐度的跨界之作。

items.body:
Returning after a 13 year absence, Boards of Canada's vision of hell isn't exactly surprising, swapping out the magic hour guitars of 'The Campfire Headphase' and the tired Carpenter-isms of 'Tomorrow's Harvest' for jagged distortions, dialog snippets and uneasy religious symbolism.

It can't be easy for Mike Sandison and Marcus Eoin; as soon as they cracked the code with 'Music Has the Right to Children' in 1998, their home-brewed signature sound - tape-warped, reverb-soaked monosynths, stuttering dialog samples and thumping MPC-breaks - became a sort of meme, regurgitated by a wave of bedroom musicians so frequently that the original references became fully hollow. Those early records were great because they sounded so unique, marking a landscape littered with post-'Chiastic Slide' crunches and choppy AFX-ian amens with new channels of thought. Just go back to their shadowy 'Twoism', 'Hi Scores', or that Mask 500 cover of 'Midas Touch' -  there was nowt else like it. By the time we got to 'The Campfire Headphase', a comparatively sunny, guitar-led misstep that arrived a few years later and then 2013's 'Tomorrow's Harvest' -  it all felt like diminishing returns.

'Inferno''s mysterious VHS rollout also felt overly familiar - and if you're gonna tease, the payoff best be worth it. Sadly, first single 'Prophecy At 1420 MHz' was damp and old fashioned, lumpen with boxy '80s drums and awkward prog rock synths - the signs didn't look good. Heard as a whole though, 'Inferno' hangs together pretty well. The brothers do a good job of laying out a vision of hell that's intricately connected to their well-worn source material: the lost future that was promised to wide-eyed 1970s kids raised on color TV, welfare and action figures. Back then, religious cults and street cranks were screaming of damnation, convincing weakened minds that judgement was coming while the Vietnam War raged - real hell was on the doorstep all along. And it's hard not to hear Boards' blend of seemingly old-fashioned religious symbolism (the Hare Krishna chants, chopped-up divinity school lectures and guided meditations) as an indirect reference to the wars raging right now. Certainly, it's their darkest album in years; not the aesthetic darkness of 'Tomorrow's Harvest', either. 'Father and Son', with its eerie Abrahamic symbolism, feels like an American Gothic reflection of Leslie Nielsen's comparatively benign narrations on 'Geogaddi', while 'Memory Death' feels like Boards actively sending off their own patented brand of hauntology with the EKG blip to prove it.

Throughout the record, BoC appear to juxtapose a cultural concept of hell with their own aesthetic responses, balancing dystopian robot voices with squelchy acid gurgles on the excellent 'The Word Becomes Flesh' and Bobby Beausoleil-style chiming strings on 'Blood in the Labyrinth'.  'The Process', meanwhile, offers a late-stage vision of aviation hell, a 'Langoliers'-style horror cue that neatly precedes the saccharine vintage BoC hit of 'You Retreat in Time and Space'. Perhaps unsurprisingly, it's these beatless moments that really hold things together - maybe they should have just leaned into it and done a full length of those vignettes. Still, 'Inferno' has its moments.

items._cn_summary: Boards of Canada时隔13年推出的专辑延续了乐队标志性的实验电子风格，融合了宗教符号、70年代文化元素与现代电子声响。专辑以“地狱”为主题，将印度教圣歌、神学院讲座片段与美国民间宗教意象相结合，创造出独特的幽灵学美学。音乐上延续了经典的磁带失真、单声道合成器和MPC鼓点等标志性元素，同时在《The Word Becomes Flesh》中融合了酸性合成器音效，在《Blood in the Labyrinth》中运用了弦乐编排，展现出跨风格的融合特征。评论指出这是乐队近年来最黑暗的作品，超越了《Tomorrow's Harvest》的美学层面，带有更深层的概念性表达。对于偏好实验电子、暗潮和前卫声响的听众而言，这张专辑具有较高的参考价值。

items.body:
STROOM fills in a gap on the timeline, excavating vital experiments made in Cologne in the wake of the cult 'Novaya Scena' compilation by Svitlana Nianio, Michael Springer, Guido Erfen, Soloveyka, Yewgeny Taran and Wolfram Burgtorf.

Back in 1993, a bizarre 20-track compilation appeared from Cologne's musical fringe. The idea for the set had come from artist and producer Erfen and sound engineer and percussionist Springer, two close friends who, taking advantage of cheap rent and disused buildings, put on regular events and established a recording studio in their neighborhood, off the beaten track. Erfen was a dedicated tape trader and had received a transmission from Kharkiv's Novaya Scena rock club that arrived with an essay and music from three local bands. At this time, Ukraine was still under Soviet rule and the music fascinated the two friends, shining a spotlight on a part of the world they were completely unfamiliar with. When singer and keyboardist Soloveyka visited cologne a year later, she handed Erfan more tantalizing music, inspiring him to make his own pilgrimage to Ukraine to investigate further. The research resulted in the 'Novaya Scene' CD, a set of tracks recorded between 1986 and 1992 that muddled prog with new wave, punk, folk and avant-garde rock. It was released on Hamburg's What's So Funny About label and was supposed to have a sequel.

That's where 'Aftermath and Transitions' comes in. Following the release of 'Novaya Scena', Erfen and Springer set up a series of sessions at their studio, inviting some of the Ukrainian artists to record with them. It's this period that resulted in Svitlana Nianio's 'Transilvania Smile' soundtrack that was properly released for the first time on Muscat sublabel Shukai in 2023. Nianio had been a member of Cukor Bila Smerť (the band who'd provided the stylistic anchor for 'Novaya Scena') and took the opportunity to launch her solo career, with Springer working as engineer. And there was more material from those sessions that Springer held back: the compilation's first four tracks are collaborations between Nianio, Springer, Taran and Springer's good friend Burgtorf. Opener 'Fake' was almost finished when Nianio showed up at the studio with her Casio in tow, so Springer plugged her in and she ended up lavishing the beat with vocals in Ukrainian and oddball keyboard vamps. The other three tracks were a little more organic, improvised in the studio while the artists got familiar with one another - there's the decelerated reggae experiment 'ManySpace', the instrumental groover 'Quiet Place' and best of all 'Політ Світляки', a wiry percussive jam that's not aged a day.

Erfen joins in on the ace exotica-tinged 'Whispering Walls' and 'Tired River', tracks from the group's final session in 1995. Nianio and Taran were planning to renew their visas and return to Cologne to record more, but it never happened - the recordings were shelved and the artists went about their lives independently. Then there's the three Solar tracks recorded by Soloveyka and Burgtorf who struck up a friendship after meeting at Springer's studio. Singing in Russian and English, Soloveyka breathes cabaret energy over Burgtorf's jerky, sample-heavy ethno-groove productions. And it's left to Taran to finish things off, with a "1996 Version" of his 'Death and the Bachelor' track that features none other than Nianio on keys. Phew. It's a brilliant set, really - not just one for STROOM obsessives, it'll speak to anyone whose interest in the Ukrainian underground was piqued by 'Transilvania Smile' or Muscut's ace Cukor Bila Smerť anthology.
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了1994至1996年间科隆地下录音室中的乌克兰实验音乐，是1993年重要合辑《Novaya Scena》的后续作品。专辑融合了prog、前卫摇滚、新浪潮、朋克与民谣元素，展现出东欧地下音乐独特的文化张力。其中Svitlana Nianio的配乐作品首次以正规发行形式出现，而开场曲《Fake》将乌克兰语演唱与古怪的电子键盘即兴相结合，极具实验性。中段的几首作品涵盖减速雷鬼节奏、器乐Groove以及充满部落感的打击乐即兴Jam，1995年最后录音阶段的作品则带有异域风情与氛围色彩。作为来自非主流音乐地区（乌克兰）的地下厂牌发行，这张专辑填补了东西欧实验音乐交流史的重要空白。

items.body:
Sandy B’s classic ‘90s SA kwaito templates are lent a subtly trippy, brooding sidespin by Belgian DJ, producer and compiler soFa Elsewhere, sealed with artwork by Cape Town’s Darren Christian.

‘Forward in Reverse (Pt. 1)’ is a crafty effort at replicating and adapting a sound perhaps best recognised for the likes of Sandy B’s ‘AmaJovi Jovi’ heater of ’94, as reissued to cult acclaim in 2017 by Awesome Tapes From Africa. One of only a handful of efforts at reviving the sound that we can recall, the seven tracks nail an ace balance of the OG ‘90s sound - a sort of ruggedly hypnotic, slower take on deep house - with more psychedelic detailing and added political impetus in Sandy’s pointed lyrics, which sometimes slip into english from his native KwaZulu-Natal region’s Zulu tongue. The difference can be attributed to Sandy B’s lived experience of the past 30 years since ‘AmaJovi…’ and the moodier tone of soFa Elsewhere’s input, perhaps emphasising a long latent parallel with ‘80s hip house or Belgian new beat’s pace and purpose. 

Sandy voices each cut in a mix of choral harmony, undulating sing-song and rapped spoken word, flowing effortlessly between them on opener ‘Mangamanga’, or suitably kitted with new beat-esque heave-ho and wickedly scribbly synth on ‘Siren Work’, and sunken to moodiest hunch on ‘Khuluma Kakhulu.’ His politics come to the fore in the exasperated delivery and refrain “what’s wrong with you / you selfish bastard” on the (corruption) house grind of ‘Politicians’ and taken to slowest, dankest levels in ‘Eat Promises’, or like a mardy Francis Bebey in ‘ Mo-fucka’, and the martial swag of ‘Isosha Elidakiwe (Drunk Soldier)’ could almost have emerged from the Teknokrat’s studio in ’89.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是南非经典kwaito音乐与现代电子制作的跨界融合，由90年代kwaito先驱Sandy B与比利时电子音乐人soFa Elsewhere合作完成。七首作品在保留原始粗糙、深沉催眠的deep house基底上，融入了迷幻电子的细节处理和更有政治张力的歌词表达。专辑中祖鲁语与英语的双语切换、合唱和声与说唱的交替运用，展现了南非本土音乐语言与欧式电子制作的对话。作品明显借鉴了80年代hip house和比利时new beat的节奏特征，同时注入了更具当代性的声响设计。来自非洲南部地区的音乐创作与欧洲制作人的合作视角，使其在实验性与世界音乐性之间取得了平衡。

items.body:
More gorgeous, hazed dreamweaving from mysterio label wherethetimegoes - the same crew that gave us a pair of stunners from Princ€ss and Nashpaints, here dissolving Dublin's special blend of peak Celtic futurism into a suite of effervescent fiddle-laced electroacoustic experiments that turn everyday musical elements into vivid, lysergic space-age landscapes, smeared with VHS infidelities.

Like Princ€ss, we've no idea who Dublin are - they're a "post modern classical" duo, as far as we can tell - but there's at least a breadcrumb trail. They emerged back in 2022 on wherethetimegoes with a CDr of bizarre jams, seemingly on violin and synth, that put them fully into their own zone, seamlessly blending Celtic folk music, West Coast new age, Eno-esque ambient and downtown-era improv without even trying to flex. 'Heavy Dublin' picks up where that set left off, presenting a similarly anonymous sequence of jams that pack into roughly the same creative space. "Oh," a voice exclaims in the opening seconds of 'Untitled 4', heralding a thick wall of digital synths and soundscapes that's sliced thru by a Conrad-esque pitch-wonked violin performance that's amplified in a way that's at odds with the other sounds. It's almost drawing a line in the sand, exclaiming that the fiddle is from our world and doesn't need to be sculpted to fit into another. And it's the perfect introduction.

On 'Untitled 2', the vibrating, powdery fiddle improvisations shiver across the kind of rhythmic, metallophone-like synth loops that you might find on any number of early Detroit techno b-sides. It's a canny reference, using two distinct future projections to create something new, an off-world cogitation from an unmistakably contemporary source that projects past the stratosphere towards a 'Solaris'-style space station. And the atmosphere continues to grow on 'Untitled 3', with subtlly glitchy rhythmic interjections that interrupt the flow of brushed aluminum synths and mangled acoustic instrumentation. It's Visible Cloaks' Fairlight futures meets Laura Cannell's archeofiction, a muddle of imaginations that pull us backwards and forwards on the timeline all at once. Similarly, there's a trace of Arthur Russell's reverb-heavy 'World of Echo' steez on 'Untitled 7', caught in a tangle of bit-chewed samples and noisy digital outbursts.

The album seems to build up to 'Untitled 5', a weightless cloud of steel pan loops, obscured voices, chimes and harmonically rich fiddle scrapes that sounds as if it's hanging off the timeline by a thread, linking Takehisa Kosugi's 'Catch Wave' concept into a catalog of sounds that you'd more readily find in the world of tape traders and private press 12"s. Fully mind-melting gear, no doubt.
items._cn_summary: 《Heavy Dublin》是都柏林匿名双人组合的实验电子新作，发表于独立厂牌wherethetimegoes。专辑延续了2022年CDr的神秘风格，将凯尔特民谣、西海岸新世纪、布赖恩·伊诺式氛围与下城即兴融为一体，通过小提琴与合成器即兴构建出迷幻的音景。评论提及Detroit techno的节奏模式、Visible Cloaks的数字美学、劳拉·坎内尔的考古声学以及阿瑟·拉塞尔的回响风格，展现出多维度的跨领域融合。VHS质感的音色处理与“科幻哨兵”式的小提琴演奏形成张力，将日常声音转化为超现实的空间体验。专辑以渐进式结构铺展，从数字合成器墙到钢盘循环与模糊人声，最终抵达吊悬于时间线边缘的实验段落。这是一部具备独特艺术视角的先锋作品，适合偏好实验与跨界融合的听者。

"WERNER DURAND has made himself a name with various projects with Dhrupad singerAMELIA CUNI, playing with URBAN SAX, ARNOLD DREYBLATT, HENNING CHRISTIANSEN, DAVID BEHRMAN, ELLEN FULLMAN, CATHERINE
items.body:
Mesmerising, illuminated sound environments conjured by Werner Durand, a key foil of CC Hennix & Amelia Cuni, joined by his Cuni spar Uli Hohmann on Mid-Eastern drums, Tibetan bells, and electronics on three intrepid, rhythmic drone excursions calling to mind Michael Ranta, Robert Rutman, Jon Hassell.

"WERNER DURAND has made himself a name with various projects with Dhrupad singerAMELIA CUNI, playing with URBAN SAX, ARNOLD DREYBLATT, HENNING CHRISTIANSEN, DAVID BEHRMAN, ELLEN FULLMAN, CATHERINE CHRISTER HENNIX, as the co-founder of THE 13th TRIBE, ARMCHAIR TRAVELLER and TONALIENS (with ROBIN HAYWARD and HILARY JEFFERY) plus numerous solo albums, released on labels like Black Truffle, Unseen Worlds or Edition Telemark. Having studied saxophone as well as Indian / Persian flutes, the Berlin based DURAND is a highly reputated protagonist in the drone scene, famous for his self-built wind instruments like buzz-clarinets or his PVC neys & horns.

His partner in FLOCKS (and longtime personal friend) is ULI HOHMANN whose early encounters with music from Asia, India and Africa led to studies with the Ghanaian master drummer MUSTAPHA TETTEY ADDY and later Tombak and Daf with NEMAD DARMAN (Iran). HOHMANN played in a couple of projects that explored the language of classical Persian music, and started building his own stringed instruments (being an educated carpenter). In 2014 he joined DURAND and AMELIA CUNI for the album "Clearing", and 2018 DURAND and HOHMANN decided to continue as a duo: FLOCKS was born.

On "Lagoon", the duo further explores the aesthetics it has crafted on its selftitled debut (2023, on the now defunct ZEHRA imprint): DURAND and HOHMANN shape drone-y soundscapes based on their self-built wind- & stringed instruments, Persian percussion and subtle electronics, drawing additional inspiration from Krautrock (listen to the irresistible, hypnotique, ever-changing rhythmic pattern of the title track) as well as JON HASSELL's "fourth world" aesthetics, placing the duo nicely between tradition and experiment!"
items._cn_summary: 专辑《Lagoon》由柏林 drone 场景核心人物 Werner Durand 与长年合作伙伴 Uli Hohmann 组成的双人组合 Flocks 创作。Durand 以自制管乐器（buzz-clarinets、PVC neys & horns）和印度/波斯长笛见长，Hohmann 则精通波斯打击乐（tombak、daf）及自创弦乐器。专辑延续其首张专辑的美学，以自制造声乐器、波斯打击乐与微妙电子元素构建绵延的音景，并融入 Krautrock 的催眠式节奏模式与 Jon Hassell「第四世界」的跨界美学。评论指出专辑标题曲展现了难以抗拒、不断变化的节奏型态，将传统波斯音乐语言与实验音乐手法有机结合，在传统与实验之间找到独特的平衡点。

items.body:
The roots of so much modern groove-driven music are reflected in Soundway’s study of rare jazz, calypso and drum music from ‘70s Trinidad & Tobago, the Caribbean nation off the coast of Venezuela.

In that time between artists first plugging in their instruments, and computerising them, the psychedelic sheen and sonification of US & UK pop and dance musics would also rub off on modernisers in the Caribbean. Under the Trinidadian term for calypso, “kaiso” the artists showcased here would blend Afro-American and West Indian traditions with certain studio innovations from disco and psych-rock to a clear purpose: driving dances - and everything that comes with them - in their lush isles.

The results are hip-gripping, heat-seeking gems that factor Black Atlantic links for a new, independent era un-tethered from colonial influence, ranging from the deeply soul-stirring jazz hush and rumble of ‘Ogun’ by Clive Zanda, thru Abdul Malik de Coteau’s plangent lament set to air-rippling steel drums, taking in the spiritual Latin jazz of Michael Boothman’s ‘Tabu’ brimming with optimism, to the muy caliente calypso of Andre Tanker, heads-down drum vibrations of Mansa Musa, and psych-funk fusioneering of Frends on ‘Mystery Music’.
items._cn_summary: 这张Soundway Records发行的特立尼达1970年代音乐合辑，收录了稀有爵士、卡吕普索与鼓乐作品，展现了加勒比音乐与非洲-美洲传统的深度融合。专辑涵盖灵魂爵士、铜管驱动的卡吕普索、拉丁爵士、迷幻摇滚及放克融合等多种风格。来自独立小众厂牌Soundway，具有明确的选辑视角与策展方向。音乐虽以驱动舞池为核心功能，但融入了丰富的实验性声响探索与跨文化融合，体现了Black Atlantic音乐链接在殖民历史语境下的独立表达。对于偏好实验与爵士融合的用户而言，具有一定的聆听价值与探索空间。

items.body:
Following records on Quiet Time and Miami's Schematic, Cairo-based producer Mostafa Onsy arrives on the mighty Drowned By Locals with a unique adaptation of 808 Mafia's iconic trap sound that pulls in influences from classic '90s Egyptian pop and mahraganat.

'Baba Fen' might come as a surprise if you've heard Onsy's previous records, like 2021's dark, trippy IDM suite 'MetaConc' and its predecessor, a nostalgia trip that took its blueprint from AFX's '90s gear. Here, the producer takes his cues from Southside, TM88 and Lex Luger's iconic Atlanta trap productions: the ratcheting hi-hats, overdriven 808 kicks and acidic trance risers that characterized American music in the wake of breakouts from Future. Honestly, it works - we've long maintained the similarities between IDM's skittering beats and trap's, and Onsy's a natural, dropping a familiar ATL snare and FL Studio synths between mahraganat hand drums and those ubiquitous pitched hi-hat runs on the scene-setting 'Zabet Ekaa3 (Intro)'.

He's joined by local vocalists Fara7 and Bleng on 'Fnan', who help assert the album's Egyptian relevance, draping their melancholy AutoTuned slurs and ad-libs around Onsy's clever fusion of half-speed local percussion and trap's signature soundset. And the two MCs are joined by gravelly-voiced rapper Sakt on the album's brilliant title track, where Onsy supplies his spookies FM-laced beats, phonk-adjacent slaps that wouldn't be out of place on one of Raider Klan's early mixtapes. Rubber-voiced Drowned By Locals regular illfeel shows up on 'Fantanyel' and goes toe-to-toe with Bleng on 'Blikii', trading blows over one of Onsy's most ominous productions. Recommended.
items._cn_summary: 开罗制作人Mostafa Onsy在独立厂牌Drowned By Locals发行的这张专辑，将亚特兰大陷阱音乐的核心元素——疾速hi-hat、厚重808底鼓、酸性 trance riser——与埃及本地mahraganat节奏和经典90年代埃及流行音乐巧妙融合。Onsy此前以IDM作品闻名，此番跨界不仅展示了陷阱与实验电子之间天然的亲缘关系，更通过本地艺人Fara7、Bleng、Sakt和illfeel的参与，构建出独特的埃及都市音乐景观。专辑中半速处理的本地打击乐与FM合成器音色、phonk风格节拍交织，呈现出高度原创的跨文化声响。Boomkat评论认为这是一次成功的融合尝试，对熟悉IDM和陷阱两种风格的听众尤具吸引力。

items.body:
Polish performance artist, musician, and poet Wojciech Kosma spills the contents of his heart on 'Tajemnica', a postmodern pop deconstruction that's between David Sylvian and Yung Lean.

There's a confusing quality to 'Tajemnica' that makes it difficult to engage with at first. It's produced almost ineptly, made with demo-like sounds that create a haze of preset nostalgia around Kosma's voice. It's only after a few tracks that the sound rights itself, and Kosma's intention makes itself clear. The record couldn't be any other way; the minimalism of the production just makes his voice stand out even more. Listen to the ominous 'Skrzydła', where a beat barely scratches the surface of Kosma's light synths - it's left to his lyrics, in Polish of course, to do the heavy lifting. And when different club sounds are referenced, it's inevitably oblique - a dancehall beat here, a log drum there. The sketchiness makes it sound like pop music that's been plucked out of a brain scanner, not completely whole, but not inhuman either.
items._cn_summary: 波兰音乐人Wojciech Kosma的专辑《Tajemnica》是一张后现代流行解构作品，融合了实验电子声响与诗歌性表达。专辑以粗糙的demo质感制作呈现，刻意采用极简主义编排，旨在突出人声与歌词的表现力。音乐中穿插的舞曲元素如dancehall节拍与log drum被以间接、抽象的方式引用，营造出介于清醒与迷醉之间的氛围感。波兰语歌词配合暗色调的合成器编排，透露出阴沉且具仪式感的情绪。Boomkat评价这张专辑为“从脑扫描仪中抽出的流行音乐”，草图般的质感反而赋予其独特的亲密性与实验性。对于偏好实验与暗潮风格的用户而言，这张专辑提供了一个兼具解构美学与舞曲暗示的独特聆听入口。
