items.body:
Aged well this one, Steven Hitchell aka Echospace aka Intrusion with set of analogue dubs very much in the spirit of Rhythm & Sound, including a strong contribution from Paul St. Hilaire aka Tikiman just to complete the act of worship. Now 15 years since it was last in circulation, the album has been remastered and is available as a double LP for the first time ever.

The Deepchord/Echospace axis is definitely having a moment. After a period where it was dismissed by some as a sort of unnecessary facsimile of Mark & Moritz’s OG blueprint, the benefit of hindsight has marked Hitchell and Modell’s productions as very much their own thing, still indebted to Berlin, but with their own signature. 

Perhaps it’s the analogue production that lends the material an air of slightly uncontrolled brilliance; the hiss of the mixing desk feels tangible rather than just digital decoration - less cosplay, more weighty and propulsive.

However - be in no doubt - if you’ve a love for anything on the line from Basic Channel to M-Series, Main Street, Burial Mix, Rhythm & Sound and Chain Reaction, this stuff is absolutely your next port of call - and this one here is one of the best from the label too, just check the clips and you’ll know exactly where you are.
items._cn_summary: INTRUSION的《The Seduction of Silence》是Steven Hitchell以模拟dub手法创作的一张电子氛围作品，延续了Deepchord/Echospace厂牌一贯的柏林电子传统，与Basic Channel、Rhythm & Sound等经典厂牌的脉络紧密相连。专辑采用全模拟制作，调音台噪音被有意识地保留下来，赋予音乐实体感与重量感，而非数字化的装饰效果。Tikiman的献声为作品增添了dub音乐的人声元素。经过重新 mastering后以双LP形式首次发行，专辑在保持经典韵味的同时展现了制作团队独立于前辈的独特签名风格。对于偏好电子音乐与实验氛围的用户而言，这张专辑体现了模拟声响设计的深度与沉浸感，在当代电子场景中具有明确的艺术定位。

items.body:
Recorded straight to tape in Glasgow, poet/performer Lisa Jones and VOM's Chas Lalli's Gilchard debut is refreshingly human, a grotesque blend of ugly reality and absurdity that situates itself between Electrelane, Arab Strap, Dry Cleaning and early Factory biz.

'Chins for Lefty' might be Gilchard's first recording, but Jones and Lalli are hardly newcomers. Since the mid-'00s, Lalli has been a member of Glaswegian post-punk/noise rock trio VOM, moonlighting in Bad Aura and the art-punk outfit Dragged Up, where he first collided with Jones. A writer and poet with a background in the local spoken word/improv scene, Jones' lyrics provide the backbone for Gilchard's sound, building a surreal parallel Glasgow that Lalli meets head-on with jangling guitars, frazzled drum loops and murky synths. Even the recording process itself plays a part, lending the album a timeless quality - honestly if you assured us this was an excavated private press gem from the late '80s we'd probably believe you.

"I turn your picture to face the wall," Jones deadpans on 'Posthumous Hologram', breaking her monotone to sing a real chorus while Lalli stacks organ vamps and Vini Reilly guitars in the space beneath. And the duo decelerate their sound significantly on 'Break Up with Johnny Dogbirth', sounding as heroin-addled as The Velvet Underground as they work in slow motion, batting emotional reflections to each other over an almost inaudible drum beat.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张来自格拉斯哥的实验性后朋克专辑，融合了诗歌朗诵、噪音摇滚与艺术朋克元素。Lisa Jones的诗人背景为音乐提供了文学性的歌词骨架，Chas Lalli则以粗粝的吉他、失真的鼓循环和阴暗的合成器构建声音景观。专辑直接录制到磁带，呈现出被比作80年代私人出版物的复古原始质感。风格上可参照Electrelane、Arab Strap与早期Factory唱片的交汇处，兼具阴暗氛围与荒诞表达。格拉斯哥独立发行的这张作品在实验性与可听性之间取得了平衡，诗歌与噪音的结合方式体现了独特的艺术视角，与用户的实验/暗潮音乐偏好高度吻合。

items.body:
Nearly 15 years have passed since the original version of this LP was released (the first iteration as a 4X12" LMTD set back in 2012).

"This release features five timeless cuts from the mind and soul of cv313 and a truly mesmerizing otherwordly dub of the illusive radius project, mixed and recorded near the heart of Detroit! (with nearly all of the tracks making their debut on wax) This entire project has been beautifully remastered by dub innovator and pioneer, Stefan Betke [POLE] @ scape mastering in Berlin, DE.

You can just drop the needle and close your eyes for a near 20 minutes of fathomless sonic depth, massaging your brain and mind, a deep dive into an immersive analogue world. A new addition to this newly minted vinyl iteration of the "Altering Illusions" series now includes cv313's blistering analogue assault on the darkest radius bit in the interpolation tapes series. Expect sub-harmonic deep space exploration in some seriously out-there electronic quadrants, some of the deepest techno reductions ever captured to tape!"
items._cn_summary: 底特律电子音乐人CV313的《Altering Illusions》 remastered版本，收录五首经典曲目与radius project的dub作品。这张专辑融合了深邃的dub质感、模拟合成器声场与techno的极简主义美学，营造出次谐波空间探索的氛围。Stefan Betke（POLE）在柏林scape mastering进行的母带处理进一步强化了声音的层次感。专辑以近20分钟的超长音景段落考验听众的沉浸能力，属于暗潮与实验电子的跨界作品。对于偏好实验电子和暗潮风格的用户而言，这张来自底特律独立厂牌的remastered版本具有较高的收藏价值和聆听意义。

items.body:
Bruce remixes Quade's 2025 LP 'The Foel Tower' on a limited cassette for his Poorly Knit label.

"Back in 2023, Bruce was approached by a band of young and ambitious lads, who wanted him to mix their debut album 'Nacre'. Being fans of his music, they hoped to utilise his renowned, club-informed and emotive sound design to add a shade of hypnotism and psychedelia to their singular strand of post-rock. The band of course were Quade, and the union proved to make perfect sense: Bruce excelled in gracefully fulfilling the band's vision, sealing their relationship for projects to come.

A couple years on, both Quade and Bruce had really proved the scope of their abilities: the sophomore album 'The Foel Tower' won the hearts of fans and critics across the board, who celebrated its "gorgeous" and "tender" sound to great acclaim. The world they had built clearly stood defined and dignified, though at the same time, Bruce couldn't help but wonder if there was more to be said. Besides, the sheer abundance of emotion and rich textures therein, suggested a great deal of potential for further exploring. So with the band’s blessing, he embarked on versioning the album.

Bruce was off the leash: total freedom leant him the ability to dub in wild style, weaving and wrestling with drum, bass et al, connecting to the arrangements' true feelings and expanding them to full frame. The "doomer sad boy, ambient-dub, folk, experimental post-rock" of the original, was blown into a whole new, hypnotic realm: through rattling analogue distortion and huge spaced out effects, Bruce's efforts stand as an exploding supernova of dub and noise, refracted through the band's themes of grief, beauty and the great British countryside.

To be released on his label Poorly Knit, this remix album once again proves Bruce's deft of touch and skill in reworking material. Maximising the sonic potential of such a promising and talented band he marks his personal contribution towards what will surely continue to be a fulfilling and illustrious musical journey for Quade."
items._cn_summary: 这张Remix专辑由Bruce重新诠释Quade的2025年专辑《The Foel Tower》，原版以实验后摇、氛围dub、民谣与悲伤情绪交织著称。Bruce在独立厂牌Poorly Knit上发行此作，延续了双方在《Nacre》合作后建立的默契。Remix版本中，Bruce以模拟失真、空间化效果和狂放的dub处理手法，将原曲中的情感与纹理进一步放大，构建出迷幻而催眠的声响空间。音乐融合了后摇、噪声、氛围电子与dub元素，跨越多个流派边界，展现出高度的实验性与创新意识。独立厂牌的发行背景和小众定位也为其增添了艺术可信度。对于偏好实验与暗潮风格听众而言，这是一张兼具深度与探索性的再创作作品。

items.body:
Following last year's long-overdue reissue of 'bloweyelashwish', Numero deepen the narrative with a new edition of Lovesliescrushing's prescient second album 'xuvetyn', compiled from hissy cassettes 4-tracked between 1991-'95 and a crucial stepping stone between shoegaze, tape music and power ambient -  essential biz if you're anywhere on the line from MBV to Jefre Cantu-Ledesma, Flying Saucer Attack to Windy & Carl.

We're still not sure how this one passed so many people by when it appeared first time around, way back in 1996. 'xuvetyn' is the duo's most perfect statement, a record that lacks the sheer shock of their debut but surpasses it elsewhere on almost every level. Producer Scott Cortez and vocalist Melissa Arpin-Duimstra assembled the album over a five year period, slowly collecting rudimentary experiments with a few pedals and a busted TASCAM Portastudio. And unlike its predecessor, it sounds as if it's been rounded out at the edges - still noisy, of course, characterised by tape fuzz and distortion that positions them somewhere between 'Loveless' and 'Endless Summer', but it flows seamlessly, foreshadowing the next few decades of euphoric, shoegaze-adjacent ambient gear. 

Without exaggeration, Lovesliescrushing just puzzled out a sweetspot between noise, minimalism, euphoria and repetition a little earlier than the rest. Inspired by Robert Fripp, Cocteau Twins, Eno, Jon Hassell, Glenn Branca and, of course, MBV, you can hear exactly how they absorbed all those influences, stretching Arpin-Duimstra's breathy vocal next to swelling, almost orchestral guitar drones. Stars of the Lid would get the flowers for their own response to many of the same influences a few years later, and - by the mid '00s - a more organic, shoegaze-aware brand of "ambient" began to seep into the underground's top levels: Fennesz, Tim Hecker, Jefre Cantu-Ledesma and others. The crazy thing is, so many of those artists' ideas were prototyped here; using 4-track tape tricks rather than granular effects or Max/MSP patches - Cortez and Arpin-Duimstra inadvertently mapped out a language that would define the laptop age. Just listen to the FM gamelan-cum-bleep techno experiment 'Virgin Blue-Eyed' and tell us they weren't years ahead of their time.

Prophetic, essential gear.
items._cn_summary: Lovesliescrushing的《xuvetyn》是一张发行于1996年的自赏派/磁带氛围专辑，由Scott Cortez和Melissa Arpin-Duimstra二人使用老式TASCAM Portastudio和4轨磁带录制。音乐融合了噪音、极简主义与欢欣的ambient声响，在lo-fi磁带质感中创造出流畅而富有层次的声音景观。评论认为这张专辑预见了此后二十多年Fennesz、Tim Hecker等艺术家的ambient电子语言，以磁带技巧而非数字工具预言了后来的laptop music时代。融合了Fripp、Cocteau Twins、Eno、MBV等影响，风格跨界至实验、先锋与暗潮领域。对于偏好实验电子和ambient的用户而言，这张来自Numero厂牌的独立发行具有较高的参考价值。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — After the revitalization of his solo career by reuniting with Brian Eno, Robert Wyatt, Andy MacKay and Paul Thompson on 6PM in 2004, 50 Minutes Later continued in 2006 with the same team, and it is also called that because as they were recorded in the same recording sessions, it is 50 minutes long, which is the duration of 6PM, then put its continuation.Phil Manzanera had returned and Revolution begins to prove it; Brian Eno's hand is evident in the song, we can imagine Eno singing it, and yet Manzanera plays and the duo works as well as in the 70s, even better, because they sound current, they sound alternative, and if Technicolor UFO can sound like a typical Roxy Music rock, That's All I Know shows us another unequivocally solo facet, where after an acoustic beginning, the sum of instruments will make it esoterically mysterious, enhanced by the chorus as well.50 Minutes Later begins with ambient sound...and although it is not clarified in the credits, the tango that is heard in the background, as if playing in the middle of the street, is sung by Adriana Varela, an Argentine singer and this inclusion is not accidental, because later the theme will develop a kind of suggested electronic tango, which will never end up exploding, it is the atmosphere that floats, its spirit, with included recitation, the piano and the cornet of Robert Wyat are so jazzy that they end up being tango, because both are urban genres born around the same time and that at times touch each other.Desparecido continues the tango flirtation, sung half in English, half in Spanish, with guitar work that perfectly understands the provocative, streetwise nature of the genre, I know this because I know tango and I've liked it for a long time, and at the same time fuses it with something more rock-oriented and contemporary. But tango allows for many fusions, ever since the 70s, and just as Kurt Weill fused opera with cabaret, this tango with alternative rock and Floydian airs flows naturally, especially because Manzanera knew what he was getting into.The tracks are linked, like a suite within the album. You can hear a train, and Dusza with his folkloric percussion, also related to the fusion that Fernando Samalea (Charly Garc�a's drummer) has been doing on his solo albums for years, until "One Step" returns with the sharp electric guitar, traversing a nighttime street illuminated by car headlights, painting it like a rainbow shimmering in the humidity.A drum'n'bass track with guitar and chorus sounds as current as the entire proposed fusion, a step further, daring not to stagnate their vision. The guitar changes tones during the same long and sinuous solo, shifting from rock and ambient...to distorted jazz, until "Swimming," which wouldn't be out of place on Brian Eno's Before and After Scene, glides serenely with melodies that seem to belong to another world, which is definitely what Bible Black would do, making us not miss the 70s, because by turning the right way, everything is in the present; that's what the cover logo is about. Till the End of the Line with just a double bass creating an atmosphere almost like John Cale's, and that's what the song is about in its cosmic country rock, how the extremes are touched at the end...that ending with a heartbreaking, emotional and clarifying guitar solo.This comeback not only features furious guitars, but also atmospheres, sensations, and suggestions to be taken and expanded upon, making the album interactive, with subtle moods, melodies...as well as "no man's land," virgin territory to claim, call it psychedelia, Canterbury Scene, call it part of Phil Manzanera's return to the most elaborated rock scene.
items._cn_summary: PHIL MANZANERA 50 Minutes Later是实验摇滚与电子氛围的深度融合之作，延续了2004年6PM的团队阵容。专辑最大亮点在于探戈音乐与电子、实验摇滚的跨界融合，Robert Wyatt的钢琴与短号演奏带有强烈的爵士即兴特质，配合电子音效营造出神秘的氛围感。Brian Eno的参与为专辑注入了电子与ambient元素，而探戈节奏的融入则体现了世界音乐的融合野心。曲目之间以音效串联形成套曲结构，长篇吉他独奏在摇滚、氛围与失真爵士之间游走，展现了高度的艺术实验性。该专辑符合用户对实验、前卫、爵士及世界音乐的偏好取向，评分8分。

items.body: Review by tszirmay — Dutch composer and multi-instrumentalist Ruud Dielen unleashes another thrilling album, progressing now into the upper echelons of quality prog, as this is a standout release that had me smiling all the way through. Ably assisted in the task, bassist Tim Ros and drummer Kike Paglia man the rhythm section with authority, introducing three vocalists into the process, Frank van der Borg and Jyoti Verhoeff on lead and backing while Ties van Diesen on backing duties. Harrie Knapen adds Hammond and piano, Thomas Zunk with theremin and mellotron and sax player Reg Parham completing the line-up. The progression is obvious from the first note, as the album unleashes a snarling five-part title track opus that revs on all cylinders like a well-oiled machine. All the ingredients are in place, from an extended electronic introduction that seems to float above the clouds , settling the sonic groundwork into a comfortable zone. The mighty mellotron shows its impeccable grandeur in creating the symphonic mood that it manages so well. On "Part 2: Carrying the Yoke", the arrangement opens up the throttle in a more conventional neo-prog setting, laden with sharper tones, coarse guitar interventions and bombastic keyboard sweeps that elevate the vocals, at times gentle and then more forceful. Veering into more fleecier realms, where ethereal vocalizations (Jyoti) rule the heavens, "Part 3: Into the Clouds" showcases Ruud playing a rolling fretless undertow that hits the mark, thumping drum attack, as the tempo increases into a fiery hurricane of interweaving sounds. The splendid lead guitar work portrays a diversity that oozes class. Another brief instrumental bridge only adds even more pace and drama to the entire opus, setting the stage for another swift turn into the unexpected. "Part 5: Chaotic Spell" swerves into more intricate signatures, a demanding almost Zappa-esque escapade with bold jazz-rock tendencies, a platform for some delirious saxophone ramblings (Parham) and lead guitar forays that exude utter confidence. The drums flutter with a maddening splurge that defies the norms, propelling this finale with resolved expertise. Well done! "If You Please" is an extended instrumental rocker, an opportunity for Ruud to exploit his talents on electric guitar, using a wide variety of tonal shifts, assorted pedals (including the much-beloved wah-wah pedal). At times, it felt like Hillage-era Gong mixed in with ZZ Top zaniness, perfectly egged on by a dynamic rhythmic engine. Well-dressed fish ! Brooding strings, a hint of theremin, distant organ and mellotron on "If I Only", setting the table for an ominously sombre vocal 'devoid of empathy', both pleading their case with measured conviction. The biting guitar snarl heightening the theatrics, both rhythm shavings and lead flickers, the manic percussive attitude pervasive and threatening. Another excellent slice of prog rock. Keeping the thrill vibrant, the tentacular keyboard display on "Whirlwinds & Maelstroms" does the trick, a piece where the mellotrons blaze, the extended Hammond organ eventually overtaking the mood with a thorough onslaught of gloomy thunder, enough room left for the acerbic guitar shards to cut hard and deep into the flesh. These boys know how to play. Masterclass effort. The finale "Everything Must Break to Grow- Part 2 Reprise" surprises once again, as the female vocals (Jyoti and Ties) take over rather brilliantly in a vaporous premise, with huge harmony backing vocals, a dreamy soundscape floating in psychedelic karma. This turns into a rockier variation that shows plenty of backbone, as if the Legendary Pink Dots were the reference point, mostly evident on the voice effected final section with hallucinogenic tendencies that cannot be overlooked. Effing splendid, if I say so myself! The entire project did not need to rely on any 'elements of hope' to succeed but rather was dependant on raw unadulterated talent, cohesion, inspiration and dedication to create interesting musical statements. The Glorious Wolf has truly arrived.4.5 Cosmic hunters
items._cn_summary: 这张2026年的《Elements of Hope》出自荷兰音乐家Ruud Dielen之手，是一张融合了电子、前卫摇滚与爵士元素的跨界作品。专辑以五部分构成的同名标题曲为核心，融合了Zappa式的复杂编排、爵士摇滚倾向以及实验性声响设计。器乐编排丰富多元，包括电子合成器、mellotron、theremin、萨克斯等元素，即兴与编曲相结合。ProgArchives平台的评价显示其已跻身高质量前卫音乐行列。对于偏好实验与前卫风格的用户而言，这张专辑提供了足够的创新性和融合性。

David Torn: Now I Imagine A Place Not The Same
By Maciej Stasiowski
May 30, 2026
View read count
Lacking recognizable features, yet constituting a genre of their own, John Constable's 1821-1822 cloud studies come up as an evocative metaphor for David Torn's Only Sky (ECM Records, 2015). What Constable referred to as "skying," almost two centuries later, made a comeback as an arrangement of distortions, loops, and cascaded signal processing, which Torn jokingly nicknamed "guitaring." That album collected improvised compositions for a solo guitarist and a halo of effect pedals and—with a little help from the cover photograph—connoted explored weather phenomena in the troposphere. But if visuals are a mere appendix to the musical abstract, why is it that already upon the first listen to the 2026 record Now I Imagine a Place Not the Same, it feels far more terrestrial and encroaching than 2015's Only Sky?

Now I Imagine a Place Not the Same sculpts its presence slowly, lullingly, almost distracting attention from the waves of warm fuzz up ahead. Visceral, contemplative, transcendental—the bigger the words get, the easier it becomes to burst them, drawing attention back to what is actually at work here: a reinvention of language that Torn has persistently pursued throughout his own and countless front-page artists' catalogues. This chapter was opened a few years before ECM's Only Sky. After what might seem like a "Scott Walker pause" of almost 11 years, Torn's sonic palette breaks into another dimension behind a generic shredder's dimension with the 2026 Kou Records offering. The pause is itself limited only to physical releases. Digitally, much has been going on, beginning with 2020's Fur/Torn, through a downpour of Bandcamp-only self-produced releases: Fall to Rise, So Fell to Feel (2024), Finally the Sweetness (2024), Sway the Palms (2024), The Beautiful Names (2024), Peace Upon You (2025). This amounts to a sprawling aural cartography, with multiple pieces still percolating and germinating on SoundCloud (Jayapala, 2011- 2020) and in Facebook posts.

The human brain is an ingenious pattern-recognition algorithm: Listen for a melody, and you will find scraps and snippets to glue together. Listen for rhythm, and the sine wave function rebounds just in time. But allow the sound to shroud you in its shingles, burrs and velvets, and you will never think of music again as an experience removed from the tangible. Given the scarcity of stable points to hold on to—rhythmic loops stretched out chord progressions, and controlled erring guides us through the journey of Now I imagine a Place Not the Same, its landscape brooding, gnawing away at the rock formations depicted by Arik Roper— the Roger Dean of the Twilight Zone. A red door glowing like a Stranger Things opening sequence secures a passage for the listener, burning through the nightfall. The opening "Ice-Cold Shock of Illusion" welcomes us with the signature mix of Terje Rypdal's pristine tone and Neil Young's pyroclastics, slowly breaking into a deep dream.

A sudden cut-off point is followed by an almost acoustic "Shapes of Newborn Warming Stars," mildly disturbed by a nebula of reversed passages. In a calmer mood, we make our way towards "The Red Door #1" in this sonic equivalent of a point-cloud model of a marshland. Despite a decade-long solo trek, Now I Imagine a Place Not the Same is nowhere near the dry echo chambers of Fur/Torn, just as that release sounded time zones apart from the open plains roaming on Only Sky. Coming from a generation of artists building what Jon Hassell labeled Fourth World music, located along the tectonic faults of ambient, jazz, and new classical, Torn amplifies this cross-cultural collage into a form of future folk. He navigates this textural territory like a John Fahey of the data center Rust Belt. And this proves to be a hauntingly infinite space, roughly surveyed on "Bones of Home, Fly East..." and "The Road (Pass the Beehive) to the River," all the way to the concluding "The (Once Green) Red Door #2." Conclusion might be a misleading term, though, as in Torn's world things do not simply disappear but gestate and decay—often at the same time—to eventually resurface further down the great insular outdoors.

As the first not-exclusively- digital album in over a decade, Now I imagine a Place Not the Same indeed sounds like a decade-long nebulous buildup to a 70-minute snapshot. With the sheer volume of projects looming on the horizon, the 2026 LP is far from a culminative statement. Marking Torn's ascension into an aural ecosystem that is self-contained and unperturbed by anything outside the cascading instrument- musician feedback loop, the record is at once a daunting and exhilarating place one cannot help but re-enter, erring through the red door.

items.body: Review by The Progolyte — I've already posted my review of Flea's Topi O Uomini, which I enjoyed very much, so I was excited to see that the band members had another project by the name of Etna. And even better, it was a jazz fusion record, and I do love me some good Italian fusion. So, going into this, I already had some high expectations, and to be honest, I think they were indeed met. This record has that classic, fast-paced, and energetic sound that I love about jazz fusion, never leading me off an edge and keeping my ears open right up until the end. Sure, maybe not the most original music out there, but some strong tunes nevertheless! The album cover also stood up to the musical performance in terms of quality, displaying a provoking collage of various exploding colors and indistinguishable yet intriguing images. Francesco Pennisi did a great job with the art here. As it turns out, his brother, Carlo, played guitar and mandolin in the record. The other musicians include Antonio Marangolo on keyboards, Elio Volpini on bass, and Agostino Marangolo on drums. The record opens with the shortest song on the album (being only a little under 4 minutes long), but I think it does a great job at representing this quirky and fun music that is present throughout the entire album. It may be a little lacking in energy, however, and is the weakest song on this project. However, the material just gets better from here on out. Pretty much every song here is amazing and incorporates very interesting and well-put-together aspects of the band members' capabilities. It's very reminiscent of Arti E Mestieri, weaving and bending across these jams of intricate arrangements that twist every few seconds while simultaneously expanding into every moment. It feels very powerful the way they have their tight grooves kicking throughout the whole record and songs like South East Wind, Golden Idol (which is also the longest piece on the album), and Sentimental Lewdness. Don't be fooled by all this energy though, as the band knows how to make good use of dynamics and includes laid-back and relaxed bits to refresh the listener in a way, sometimes being things such as ambient improvisation and soundscapes, which I find really interesting. In conclusion, Etna is a lovely little record that fits nicer with the Italian fusion and wider Rock Progressivo Italiano scene. Not an essential per se, but definitely a good second-tier album for fans of that type of stuff or those who are generally just looking for more high energy and exciting music along the same lines as Mahavishnu Orchestra or Jean Luc Ponty (but without the violin, unfortunately). This is, in my eyes, deserving of a very strong 4.25/5.
items._cn_summary: ETNA是1975年意大利爵士摇滚融合乐队作品，属于学院派爵士范畴，具有快速、充满活力且编曲复杂的特征。专辑在紧密的节奏groove中融入动态变化，既有高能量段落，也包含ambient即兴和声响景观等放松段落。音乐风格类似Arti E Mestieri，通过错综复杂的编排和巧妙的转调展现技术实力，但评论者认为原创性并非极致。专辑体现了意大利摇滚进步运动中爵士融合的独特视角，呈现了1970年代意大利融合音乐的典型特征，适合对高能量爵士摇滚感兴趣且关注欧洲融合音乐发展的听众。

Including rare and long-lost tracks from Caustic Window (Aphex Twin), Tranquility Bass, Spacetime Continuum, and more, comes with a 20-page booklet packed with photos, artwork, and memorabilia from 1992–1995 and liner notes by founding members Mario Aguera and Kevin Foakes and an Obi strip featuring Simon Reynolds’ quote from Energy Flash

Hardcore jungle revival label Fundamental Frequencies gouch out with a gorgeous ode to pivotal chill out party Telepathic Fish, compiling blissed kisses from the likes of its regular DJ Mixmaster Morris, aka The Irresistible Force, and live performers AFX (Caustic Window), Global Communication and NoW, packaged with an illustrated, 20-page zine 

Who wants a head massage/back rub?! One for fluffier ravers and backroom posse; ‘Telepathic Fish: Trawling The Early 90s Ambient Underground’ yields a head-first dive into sublime waters that flowed around, between likemind labels such as Warp, Ninja Tune, and Rising High, and quenched crowds’ thirst for esoteric alternatives to full-bore rave. 

Originating in the sacred spaces of second rooms, squats and house parties, but soon enough a main room attraction in its own right, the Telepathic Fish events were run by Chantal Passamonte (aka Mira Calix - RIP), David Vallade, Mario Aguera and Kevin Foakes (aka DJ Food) - collectively named Openmind - who would be joined by the sound’s standard bearer Mixmaster Morris to throw a series of events in London often distinguished by their decor installations and paralleling similar happenings like Megatripolis, who were also informed by a certain sort of ‘60s-into-‘90s spirituality and techgnostic futurism.

Compiled by Mario, David and Kevin with fellow space cadet Chantal in mind, the picks and sequencing are impeccable and hold up the sound in its lushest light. The Irresistible Force’s remix of Barbarella is tumescent with loved-up glow, and NoW’s downbeat bliss-out ‘Nights Interlude’ is still adorable despite its ubiquity of that time. Global Communications’ ‘Incidental Harmony’ needs a Fish branded bean bag to cushion your swoon, and the nostalgia keeps on keeping on with RDJ’s deliciously whimsical ‘Cordialatron’, thru David Morley’s inversion of Golden Girls trance glyder, along with lesser known but no less loveable gems in No Man’s vignette or Keiichi Suzuki’s scalp-tingling ambient house trodder.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张收录1992至1995年间罕见作品的合辑，汇集了Aphex Twin（Caustic Window）、Global Communication、Mixmaster Morris等电子音乐先驱的ambient与实验电子作品。专辑以伦敦90年代的Telepathic Fish chill out派对为背景，展现了ambient underground与rave文化的交汇。选曲和编排由Openmindcollective成员完成，包括A FX的实验作品、Global Communication的氛围乐章以及RDJ的独特曲目。合辑附带的20页手册提供了丰富的历史资料。对于偏好实验电子和ambient的用户而言，这张专辑提供了珍贵的历史梳理，展示了当时电子音乐的前卫探索。

items.body: The sharp pluck of a Wayuu classical guitar opens “Cardón” before the bass drops and Afro-Caribbean percussions floods in. Ghetto Kumbé built the track around classical guitarist Henry Pimienta Pushaina and singer Lido Pimienta. Pushaina, a concert musician from Uribia, brings material from his Portafolio de Obras Wayuu para Guitarra, a project that translates ancestral Wayuu melodies to classical guitar. This pairs naturally with Lido Pimienta’s background; born in Barranquilla of mixed Afro-Colombian and Wayuu descent, she blends traditional rhythms like cumbia and bullerengue with synth-pop. Her high, clear vocal cuts straight through the percussion layers. The lyric she wrote with Ghetto Kumbé’s Edgardo Garcés follows someone standing in a river at night, cold water over their feet, their sins going downstream with the current, praying the moon holds the frost back till morning. The chorus keeps returning to “Solo deja que la brisa arrastre todo consigo”, let the breeze carry everything away with it, and Pimienta’s voice delivers it each time like the decision has already been made. Co-produced with London’s The Busy Twist, the Afro-Caribbean percussion drives underneath while the vocal stays above it. “Cardón” opens Cardones, the new Ghetto Kumbé album released on May 15, an eight-track record built around collaborations: Pimienta Pushaina also opens the album on “Wayakana”, while Nidia Gongora and Akilín appear on closing track “Belén”. In support of the LP, the Cardones Tour Europa 2026 runs through June and July, taking in Fusion Festival in Larz, Colours of Ostrava in Ostrava and Les Suds à Arles among the stops.   Stream “Cardón” HERE and get your copy of Cardones following THIS LINK. The post Daily Discovery: Ghetto Kumbé – Cardón Ft. Lido Pimienta & Henry Pimienta Pushaina appeared first on Rhythm Passport.
items._cn_summary: Ghetto Kumbé联手Henry Pimienta Pushaina与Lido Pimienta创作的世界音乐融合之作。作品以Wayuu古典吉他演奏为主干，结合Afro-Caribbean打击乐与Lido Pimienta擅长的合成器流行元素，形成传统与当代的对话。Lido Pimienta高亢清澈的嗓音在层叠的节奏中保持辨识度，歌词以月夜河畔意象展开，带有洗涤灵魂的仪式感。专辑《Cardones》强调合作属性，汇聚加勒比海与南美原住民音乐传统。这张作品契合用户对世界音乐与电子元素的兴趣，跨文化融合具有独特视角。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — Schicke & F�hrs & Fr�hling had gone from a trio to a quartet with the addition of Edward Brumund Ruther on bass for their second album, and Wizzard demonstrates a development not only in symphonic elements but also in jazz-rock, particularly in the guitar riffs. "Autumn Sun in Cold Water" reminds me of Vangelis, but the guitar, along with the synthesizers, drives the development, with the drums fragmenting here and there, creating a sense of solar expansion. "Artificial Energy" sounds like krautrock, where Fr�hling plays Fripp-esque soundscapes with a Mellotron in the background.Driftin' continues this collection of frescoes illustrating this space epic, as if witnessing, through the spaceship window, the formation of nebulae, black holes, and all manner of deep-space phenomena where neither the ocean nor light usually reaches...except when the sun approaches. From the funk of Driftin' to Troja, where acoustic and classical contrasts blend seamlessly with Steve Howe-esque electric solos featuring synthesizers.Space can become the most scorching desert, with which it shares many similarities, and this oppressive atmosphere is precisely captured by the quartet, until 1580 arrives like an acoustic Mahavishnu Orchestra, whose piano and guitar electrify in cascades that flood the desert...filling the space with light.With that prominence of the piano, accompanied by the drums and bass, comes Explorer, with that prominence of the piano, accompanied by the drums and bass, comes Explorer, with a keyboard that plays jazz rock but with that air of the most martial Vangelis, taking the time, as if it were a waltz, to develop the climate conducive to the end that encompasses reminiscences of disco, jazz rock, and symphonic music from the late 70s that could even have fit with Genesis at that time.Without the brilliance, cohesion, or originality of its predecessor, Sunburst stands on its own with well-crafted compositions, where they do achieve the status of photographs, which in their heterogeneity complete the symphonic stage in all its complexity.
items._cn_summary: 1977年德国交响前卫摇滚专辑，展现出爵士摇滚与合成器氛围的跨界融合。乐队从三人扩展为四人阵容后，在交响元素基础上强化了爵士摇滚的即兴张力。专辑受Vangelis电子氛围、King Crimson声响景观及Mahavishnu Orchestra爵士融合影响，融合了Krautrock的实验特质与Steve Howe式的电吉他独奏。曲目从冷冽的太空意象渐进至炽热的沙漠场景，钢琴与吉他交织的爵士摇滚段落尤为突出。虽未达到前作的闪耀高度，但整体呈现了一幅兼具科幻氛围与古典底蕴的交响画卷，对1970年代末期的前卫摇滚与爵士融合爱好者具有参考价值。

items.body: Review by Aussie-Byrd-Brother — Always a recurring home for titles and artists on the darker end of the Italian prog spectrum, Black Widow Records brings together theatrical doom metal band ExpiatoriA and established gothic/symphonic/dark RPI group Il Segno del Comando for a glum and evocative split album `Voci Notturne', inspired by an Italian TV series from 1995 of the same name. Working alongside each-other, the two acts have set out to recreate, in their own unique and individual styles, the eerie, cryptic and perplexing atmosphere of the show, and listeners essentially receive an EP's worth of new music from each of them.An aura of intrigue hovers over director Pupi Avati's broadcast and the subsequent distribution of the TV series `Voci Notturne' ("Nocturnal Voices" in English), considered a masterpiece of darkness and mystery. The ambiguous narrative weaves together politics, religion, history and the supernatural across continents and decades, with an unsettling atmosphere that grows as truth and illusion blur together. The fact that the series is not readily accessible in the modern era (outside of a heavily reworked and reedited version) has only enhanced its allure and reputation.Formed in Genoa in 1987, ExpiatoriA only released their debut album `Shadows' in 2022, with a live cassette following two years later. Taking the opening side here, the band offers a set of three murky doom metal dirges of branching passages and moods. Front and centre are vocalist AngeleX's pained vocals, moving between despairing wailing and slurred, guttural growling, and they envelope the band's sludgy riffing, mud-thick fuzzy bass rumbles and battering-ram drums with a suffocating and disorientating fervour. Spectral choirs, ghostly church organ and spoken word passages intensify the sombre ambience, but there are fleeting little glimpses of light and grandiosity.The flip-side comes from Il Segno del Comando, with over 30 years of standout modern dark RPI and gothic rock works to their name. Over the years, the group has constantly refined and altered their approach, moving between heavy underground rock and more overtly progressive rock arrangements (lots of vigorous and upfront keyboard soloing these days!). In contrast to ExpiatoriA's interpretations, ...Comando's pieces are more up-tempo, punchier and rockier, with many bombastic and stirring moments.Riccardo Morello's soulful commanding croon purrs throughout `Le due vie', where reflective reaching guitar strains kick in with a strident power, and no shortage of wavering Moog trills and glistening synths. `Il crittogramma' thrums with slinking electronics and runaway guitar-soloing, and `Litania per Emily e Giacomo' is a rousing and sophisticated ballad with elegant orchestration, making it the most overtly melodic moment of the album (a track that would actually be welcome on any RPI album). Closer `Egregoro' is a tasty instrumental of heavy guitars and plentiful synth soloing, contrasting reflective passages with ballsy hard-rock crunch, not unlike UK band Arena in parts. Infectious and addictive, what a powerful and memorable way to close the LP!Available on LP, CD and downloads, if you're one of those drawn to the shadowy corners occupied by darker Italian prog and unconventional metal acts, `Voci Notturne' just might be the temptation you need to fall for.Three and a half stars, rounded up to four for the Archives.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张意大利分裂专辑，由黑寡妇唱片旗下两支黑暗系乐队合作完成。ExpiatoriA提供厄运金属一侧，以浑浊的riff、病态的人声和教堂风琴营造阴郁氛围；Il Segno del Comando则带来更具活力的意大利进步摇滚，结合交响键盘、Moog合成器和摇滚吉他，有一定旋律性。专辑主题源自意大利1995年同名电视剧的黑暗神秘氛围，音乐上呈现厄运金属与暗潮哥特摇滚的交汇。意大利进步摇滚传统与当代暗潮美学的结合，对偏好暗潮与实验音乐的用户有一定吸引力，但整体创新性中规中矩，属于类型融合较为稳健的作品。

items.body: The new single S + M from Staytus has the crackling charge of a bad idea unraveling like a ball of blood red yarn. Sam Grundemann, the Los Angeles artist behind Staytus, has built the project around industrial pressure, electronic gloss, horror-film glamour, and the private emotional mess that keeps people returning to situations they swore they had outgrown. With her new single and video, released following her signing to Cleopatra Records, she turns separation, obsession, and the pull of reconciliation into something sleek, strange, and seriously messed up. The track moves through industrial, electronic, and nu-metal influences with a sleek sense of threat, all pressure points and polished unease. Working with producers Sean Beavan, whose resume includes Nine Inch Nails and 8mm, and Matt McJunkins of A Perfect Circle and Puscifer, Staytus lets S + M breathe inside a space built from serrated textures, heavy electronics, and vocals that shift between control and surrender. There is weight in the programming, but also a strange glamour to the way the song carries itself, like it knows obsession often looks better from a distance. Lyrically, “S + M” circles the afterlife of attachment: how someone can remain lodged in your identity even after distance has supposedly done its job. Desire becomes less a simple want than a feedback loop, intimate and magnetic, with every return carrying the faint humiliation of knowing better and reaching anyway. Directed by Vicente Cordero of Industrialism Films, the video initially shows how seduction gets more interesting when something feels slightly off. The clip begins in a place of closeness, teasing erotic tension and emotional dependency, then gradually tilts into psychological distortion. By the ending, the relationship at the center of the video has been rearranged in the viewer’s mind, less romance than a private fantasy gone rancid. A bold choice in these times. Staytus frames that narrative shift with precision: “I’ve always been inspired by films and visual storytelling that leave people unsettled in a beautiful way,” she says. “S + M starts off feeling seductive and emotionally intimate, but as the story unfolds, it becomes something much darker and more psychologically distorted. I wanted the ending to completely reframe the emotional experience of the song.” Watch the music video for Staytys’ “S + M” here: Follow Staytus: Facebook Instagram Spotify YouTube Bandcamp Website The post Los Angeles Alt-Industrial Artist Staytus Shares Video for Unsettling Thriller “S + M” appeared first on Post-Punk.com.
items._cn_summary: Staytus的《S + M》融合工业、电子与另类暗潮元素，作品以separation与obsession为主题，声音设计采用industrial pressure与electronic gloss的交织，具有horror-film glamour的视听氛围。制作人Sean Beavan（Nine Inch Nails）与Matt McJunkins（A Perfect Circle）的参与确保了作品的工业实验性与声音层次。作品在歌词层面探讨attachment的 afterlife，呈现desire作为feedback loop的心理张力。视觉叙事由Vicente Cordero执导，将亲密关系逐渐扭曲为心理畸变的进程。整体而言，这是一张在暗潮与工业电子边界上具有实验探索的独立作品，与用户的暗潮/电子口味匹配度较高，尽管nu-metal元素略带主流倾向，但整体艺术定位偏向独立与边缘。

Home » Jazz Articles » Album Review » Daniel Rotem: Solo II - Under Construction At Bluewhale

Daniel Rotem: Solo II - Under Construction At Bluewhale
By Dan Bilawsky
May 30, 2026
View read count
This album plays as a story of second comings, both for a beloved West Coast jazz spot and a compelling artist's solitary explorations. Back in the fall of 2024, bluewhale—one of L.A.'s most welcoming clubs, permanently shuttered at its original location during the pandemic—was in the midst of starting a new lease on life in a different space.  On November 10 of that year, venue proprietor Joon Lee held an open house to signal the shape of a scene to come.  He invited Daniel Rotem to play for the event, which drew a crowd intent on bringing positive energy into the atmosphere, and the saxophonist's thirty-minute solo performance was a hit. More than that, it led the reedist to reflect on his horn's sound in those confines.   A bare room with no acoustic treatment to speak of—a foundation ready for further development—the unadorned area offered a reverberant, enveloping warmth. In doing so, it called to Rotem. 

Having tested the waters, the saxophonist yearned to record there before things changed. And performing alone, which served him well on that November night—and on the fascinating, COVID-era Solo (Self Produced, 2021)—was the obvious way to go.  Luckily, time was on his side, with a long road ahead for the club's renovations. Subsequently, a video series—"under construction," documenting musicians working in the evolving, unfinished space—was developed, giving Lee an opportunity to promote both structural progress and musical ingress.  And Rotem's hopes were fulfilled within that project, allowing him to capture his tenor (and soprano)  in resonant recital mode.

Rotem's episode, recorded on August 21, 2025 and available for viewing on YouTube, features 16 minutes of riveting sound exploration.  But that's not the whole story or set. Solo II—under construction at bluewhale, elaborating on that offering, features six numbers—approximately 30 minutes of music, split evenly between originals and classics. Opening on his own "A Peace That Starts Within," Rotem is intent on moving inside, beyond and around an arresting motif.  His dual gift for melodic invocation and extrication is ever apparent throughout. What follows—an extemporized introduction to and performance off "God Bless the Child"—proves equally spellbinding.  The slow decay of a soulful melody hanging on air, the light click of sealing pads at play, the knowing embrace of history and mystery, and a stirring exit strategy come together as one.

Shifting gears, and presenting with somewhat desiccated sonics, Rotem visits Thelonious Monk's "Pannonica" on soprano. Unfurling the High Priest of Bop's portrait of the Jazz Baroness with appropriately puckish charm and class, he puts a noticeably different sound and spin on his solo work.  Only a brief departure with the small horn, he then returns to the more sonorous tenor and materials of his own making with the brief and thought-provoking "Starting From the Smallest Place." The haunting "B Team," holding the penultimate position, proves complementary, offering turns of the mind and musical spine.  Prime examples of the virtues of patient curiosity, those shortest of tracks leave the deepest of impressions.  Closing with dry sound and sincere sentiment(s), everything is front and center on "Till There Was You."  The longest yet somehow most direct statement of the bunch, it's a perfect nod to one's true love—person, concept...or room.
Track Listing

items._cn_summary: 这是一张在洛杉矶 bluewhale 爵士俱乐部未完工空间录制的萨克斯独奏专辑，融合了即兴爵士与现场环境声学探索。演奏者丹尼尔·罗特姆（Daniel Rotem）运用次中音萨克斯和高音萨克斯，在约30分钟的音乐中平衡原创作品与经典曲目（如《God Bless the Child》《Pannonica》）。乐评指出其音乐具有“引人入胜的声音探索”特质，录音环境本身也构成了独特的声学元素，为即兴演奏提供了自然的空间响应。作为独立发行、现场独奏形式的爵士作品，它与用户的学院派爵士和实验音乐偏好相匹配，但跨类型融合度有限，整体评分适中。

items.body: I want to personally direct you to a remarkable piece of music titled "Two Views of a Prayer," composed and written by David Dzubinski as part of the Prism Quartet's new series of collaborations called Unlocking Your Inner Composer. If you have listened to my radio programs, you are probably familiar with the quartet's ground-breaking, genre-blurring music. If not, there's no better introduction than this. Performed in November of 2025 at the Free Library of Philadelphia, they invited vocalist Ursula Rucker, percussionist Tyshawn Sorey, and violinist Carlos Santiago to collaborate on the arrangement and performance of Dzubinski's composition. It travels from raw to lyrical and back in the course of just under 4 minutes, with both finesse and energy. - Cliff Furnald, editor Find Prism Quartet online. items._cn_summary: Prism Quartet推出的跨界合作系列Unlocking Your Inner Composer，邀请了人声艺术家Ursula Rucker、打击乐手Tyshawn Sorey及小提琴手Carlos Santiago，与作曲家David Dzubinski共同完成这首约四分钟的实验作品。该作延续了Prism Quartet一贯的流派模糊风格，在原始粗粝与抒情柔美之间快速切换，展现了爵士即兴与当代作曲的融合潜力。评论虽篇幅有限，但明确点出了作品在技巧与能量上的双重追求，适合关注实验/学院派爵士与当代古典跨界融合的听众。

items.body: Króta, the latest release on Norway's Taragot label, features a Swede and two Norwegians playing interpretations of mainly traditional tunes from their respective countries. Fiddler Mats Edén has long been involved in Swedish folk music, as a player, composer and teacher, and in the process exploring and integrating different musical styles and approaches. Tellef Kvifte was in the pioneering Norwegian crossover band Slinkombas in the 1970s and has continued to play a central role in Norwegian folk music, both as a musician and an academic. Most often heard playing the sjøfløyte, more widely known as a recorder, Kvifte has employed other instruments from outside the Norwegian tradition, in particular the saxophone and bagpipes. His son Knut Kvifte Nesheim, a drummer and composer, has also shown a determination to blur the lines between different musical genres, both in his solo and group projects. It comes as no surprise then to find this trio offering a far from conventional take on the tunes they have chosen. While dance tunes may be the source of most of the material here, this feels more akin to chamber music; not that it is remotely classical in style, but in the sense it conveys of three players engrossed in a musically intimate conversation. This is not a performance appropriate for accompanying dancers but might instead be seen as an exploration of hidden possibilities of meaning in the music. In so doing it reveals some of its underlying mystery, including, perhaps, a darker side. Just as in an Ibsen play, where the surface bonhomie, jollity and social nicety can be hiding something more sinister, in Scandinavian dance music there are at times hints of a troublesome undercurrent below the surface. So the decision to open proceedings with “Fossgrimen,” a fiddle tune from Norway's Setesdal valley, is perhaps significant. A fossgrimen is a mythical creature, a kind of water-sprite living in waterfalls from whom fiddle-players were considered to have learned their skills and for that were not universally welcomed, with the fiddle considered to be the devil's instrument. Tellef Kvifte takes the lead melody on most tracks but on the Swedish “Polska from Per Myhr,” having played a repeated introductory riff on the sjøfløyte, with Mats Edén providing an amorphous textural accompaniment below and Nesheim adding some quiet tinkling, it's Edén who introduces the tune on the fiddle with Kvifte proceeding to play in unison. It's a short track and almost as soon as it gets going things start to fragment and everything grind to a halt.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张来自挪威独立厂牌Taragot的斯堪的纳维亚民谣专辑，汇集了瑞典小提琴家Mats Edén与挪威演奏家Tellef Kvifte、Knut Kvifte Nesheim。专辑对挪威与瑞典传统舞曲进行非常规演绎，抛弃伴奏舞者的功能性，转而追求三人如室内乐般的亲密对话。评论者强调音乐中潜藏的神秘感与阴暗面，如同Ibsen戏剧表面和谐下的暗流。虽以传统曲调为基础，但解构式演奏手法与即兴元素使其带有实验性质，介于世界音乐与当代跨界民谣之间。对于偏好实验与跨界融合的听者而言，这张专辑提供了传统斯堪的纳维亚民谣的另一重解读可能。

items.album: Hear the voices of these Chicago gunfire survivors. »
items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we’d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow— both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That’s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house—right in the heart of the “‘hood,” beneath the Midway Airport’s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. We were in a section of town that one man defined as “the forgotten parts.” Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city’s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin’ Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who’d asserted “you’ll really want to hear my story,” was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder’s tough facade broke down as she shared how she’d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, “I’m sorry. I’m sorry. I’m sorry.” But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology— for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global, who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It’s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles." items._cn_summary: 这是一张非传统意义上的音乐录音专辑，聚焦芝加哥枪支暴力幸存者的真实声音记录。Ian Brennan在芝加哥南城进行街头录音，收集了25位不同年龄参与者的讲述与即兴说唱，保留了原始环境音并辅以极简的loop与drone作为背景。作品介于声音艺术、社会纪实与实验音乐之间，既是民间音乐的延伸，也是对城市创伤的直面。尽管缺乏传统意义上的音乐创作，但其独特的社会介入视角与环境录音的实验手法，对于关注实验与前卫音乐的用户而言，具有一定探索价值。所有收益捐赠给Cure Violence Global组织。

items.body: EMEFE spent nine years watching “Sun Spat” live a life they never planned for it. Written by saxophonist Jas Walton and tucked into the band’s 2015 self-titled album as a deep cut, it was never released as a single, and never backed by any promotional machinery. It just moved. Slowly, through streaming algorithms and word of mouth, the track gathered millions of plays, a quiet breakout for a New York horn-led ensemble that had already gone on indefinite hiatus in 2016. The live version captured here, “Sun Spat Live in Brooklyn,” was recorded at The Sultan Room in Bushwick and filmed by Isaac Gillespie. It appears on the band’s new four-track EP Sun Spat 2026, released 22 May. The performance features a nine-piece lineup: Walton on tenor sax, Lynn Ligammari on baritone sax, Julie Acosta on trumpet, Aani Kisslinger on trombone, Miles Francis on drums, Doug Berns on bass, Jake Pinto on keys, Harry Terrell and Tim Allen on guitars, and Javier Ramos on congas and percussion. Mixed and mastered by Shiftee, the Brooklyn-based mix engineer and two-time DMC World Champion, with live recording by Sharif Mekawy. EMEFE formed in 2009 when Francis, then a 19-year-old freshman at NYU who had just joined Antibalas and was studying under afrobeat pioneer Tony Allen, assembled a group of jazz school classmates drawn to Fela Kuti’s rhythmic architecture. Over time, the band folded in funk, new wave and neo-soul, keeping the horn section as the ensemble’s lead voice and Berns’s bass as its anchor. Members went on to tour with Mark Ronson, David Byrne, The Roots and Sharon Jones during the hiatus years, but “Sun Spat” kept pulling people in. When EMEFE reconvened for their 2025 album FORWARD and played sold-out rooms, Francis asked the crowd who was seeing the band for the first time. Most of the room put their hands up. But when the band played “Sun Spat,” every one of them already knew the words. Listen to and get your copy of Sun Spat 2026 following THIS LINK The post Daily Discovery: EMEFE – Sun Spat (Live in Brooklyn) appeared first on Rhythm Passport.
items._cn_summary: EMEFE是一支以纽约布鲁克林为基地的融合爵士/Afrobeat乐队，其音乐根植于Fela Kuti的节奏架构，同时融入放克、新浪潮和neo-soul元素。铜管声部（萨克斯、小号、长号）担任主旋律角色，贝斯作为节奏锚点，形成了具有学院派爵士特征的声音框架。九件配置的现场演出体现了器乐编排的丰富性，铜管与节奏组的互动具有一定即兴张力。乐队成员曾与多位主流音乐人合作，但自身保持独立姿态。这张现场EP延续了乐队2015年热门曲目「Sun Spat」的传播势能，属于融合风格扎实但实验性有限的独立制作，与用户偏好的实验/前卫和学院派爵士有一定交集但不够深入。

items.body: Review by siLLy puPPy — SOLAR BLOOMS is the three piece band of David Margalitadze (vocals, guitar), Andrew Shvai (guitar),Serj Jaroschuck (bass) and Paul Vesnianka (drums) from the Ukrainian city of Lutsk that formed in2019 and spent five years crafting its debut release AKH�LI DZ�LIS DABAD�BA which translates as"Birth Of A New Power" in the Georgian language. This somewhat hard to classify progressive rockalbum is the band's debut and features a blend between psychedelic rock, hard rock, stoner metal andwhat to me sounds a bit like neo-prog at times. Loose comparisons yield hints of Porcupine Treestyled atmospheric effects along with Riverside-like heavier rock, Anekdoten also comes to mind aswell as emotive vocals more akin to neo-prog.This debut was released in 2024 and features nine tracks that add up to 49 1/2 minutes. Pushing playand simply listening to the first opening sounds of "Solid Soil" one may believe they just initiateda post-rock type of album with hints of Pink Floyd and indeed many of the intros do share those samecharacteristics but SOLAR BLOOMS has become adept at seamless blending of prog styles that for 2024may sound a bit dated as this Porcupine Tree production type of album was most prominent in theearly 2000s but nevertheless SOLAR BLOOMS offers enough variety and delivers it all in such atasteful manner that it's really hard to complain about any sort of retro effect. The track quicklybecomes enveloped by thick atmospheric backing and English lyrics which really give no indicationthis band emerged from the Slavic nation of Ukraine.The catchy hook-infused compositions continue with the guitar-centric riffing of "Rays Of Sun"however this more tender approach may remind a bit of the 80s new romantic singing style of bandslike Spandau Ballet more than a prog band but then the harder rock aspects kick in and things shifta bit to a more melodic style of prog with more elegant singing. "Tombstone Cities" begins much likea neo-prog style with arpeggiated guitar sweeps and thick atmospheres before emotive vocals deliverythe tale du jour. The track doesn't remain firmly in that style and the mood shifts to morerambunctious with heavy guitar more in the heavier Porcupine Tree camp or bands like OSI for thatmatter yet atmospheric touches remain a main staple of the musical flow. "Deliverance" continues theheaviness while "Space Will Remain" delivers a more space rock approach but not anything remotelyFloydian. Same goes for "Indifference."My favorite track on board is the feisty "Defeated" which is the heaviest and fastest on board andis the one track that qualifies as bonafide metal with fiercely strummed guitar works and pummelingpercussion however even at this agitated mode, vocalist David Margalitadze's vocal style remainscool and calculated belying the thundering din underpinning it all. "Transform Us" is anothercrunchy rocker but less emphatic skirting on mid tempo but features a wily variation of rhythmicchanges. The closing title track is the lengthiest on board at over nine minutes and features mostsophisticated build up and crescendo effect of any track on board. Once again kicking off more as apost-rock type of style slowly oozes into a more rock oriented atmospheric heavy space rock styleending the album on a very satisfying note. This album was quite effective on the first exposure andholds up over repeated listens. The band members deliver admirably and the production is perfect.While influences are abound the band sounds unique and demonstrates a sense of maturity that wasunexpected.

items.body: Review by siLLy puPPy — While ITOIZ was one of the most popular acts to emerge from the prog rock boom from the Basquespeaking region of Spain in the late 70s, this band actually extended its career far beyond its 1974formation and made it all the way to 1988 before disbanding but like virtually every other Spanishprogger to play catch up during a small window of time that emerged after the collapse of the Francoregime and the end of the prog window closing at the end of the 1970s, ITOIZ too had to simplify itsmusic to join the world of radio friendly pop music although the band continued to performexclusively in the Basque language. Following its 1978 self-titled debut the band had one more progrelease in them with its second album EZEKIAL before succumbing to pressures of the marketplace.This sophomore release expanded the core five members to include a three additional musicians thatadded the violin, mandolin, saxophone, cuatro and extra piano. In addition to that an additionalvocalist and children's choir. This was the band's most acclaimed release.As the title suggests this is indeed a concept album referring to the prophet EZEKIAL which thealbum uses as a template for related biblical themes. The album followed the trend of Basque progacts eschewing the Andalusian flamenco influences and infusing the local folk flavors with elementsof progressive rock and jazz. The flute aspects evoked the fluttering tenderness of a classic JethroTull album while the dreamy pastoral folk passages seemed more inspired by Genesis or Camelespecially with the thick atmospheric keyboards adding layers of dreamy ambience however musicallythe melodic touches were fueled by Basque folk with the contrast emerging in more powerful guitarrock. The album features eight tracks with each tackling a different theme based on the prophet. Thealbum runs about 37 minutes and displayed a much more ambitious last hoorah for its prog leaningsbefore plummeting into the simplified pop arena devoid of any such complexities. The album is a lot mellower than even the mellow debut with its acoustic-fueled folk aspects as theunderpinning that finds the world of rock and jazz invited over to have a conversation. The opening'Ezekielen Prophezia' sets the stage with a standard introduction to the flavors of the debut alongwith the addition of a violin. As the tracks continue the saxophone is added and by the third trackwe find a strange mix of symphonic keyboards melding with a Tull-ish flute flurry and a smooth jazzsaxophone joining in which to my ears is the weakest part. Imagine if you will Kenny G joining Cameland Tull for a jam and you'd not be too far off. The album continues these same characteristics withvocalist Juan Carlos P'rez delivering the same somewhat underwhelming vocals that were present onthe debut. The fourth track simply titled 'Ezekiel' features the children's choir along with asimple campfire type of guitar accompaniment. It's a bit campy actually and sounds rather out ofplace. For my ears the first half of the album sounds rather clunky without any true cohesiveness to asupposedly concept album and the musical deliveries are very steeped in progressiveness. It's notreally until the fifth track 'Ezekielen Ikasgaia' where the albums comes to life with Itziar Egileorpicking up vocal duties which makes me wonder why she wasn't the lead vocalist on the whole album asshe blows the dude away big time however once again the Kenny G soft sax parts rub me the wrong wayespecially with the psychedelic organs by their side since it all seems to cancel each other for theproper effect. The best tracks for me are the ending ones. 'Ezekielen Ametsa' at last offers somemore interesting song structures and vocal performances (by the girl) which basically continues intothe following track 'Ezekielen Erantzuna.' Here the band sounds more in sync and the elements geltogether much better which is thankfully features less sax interruptions. Overall this is a decentalbum but too many irritating aspects for me to warm up to. So many other better Basque bands IMHOso i'm not sure why this one has appealed to so many more than the rest.

items.body:
One of thee heaviest records of the C.21st - stoner rock or otherwise - returns to orbit with a 20 year reissue of Al Cisneros & Chris Hakius frankly fucking sexy Om debut - essential FFO Sleep, Earth, Sunn 0))), Les Rallizes Dénudés, Father Dionysis Tabakis.

Like the ultimate death fart of twentieth century rock, ‘Variations on a Theme’ utterly reeks of leather, ganja, incense and stale booz, and that only makes us love it so much more. On three keeling parts Al Cisneros’ flaming riffs and monotone vox knit with Chris Hakius’ slow swingeing stickwork in longform mantras that have stuck in mind since its day of release, and have long become a go-to when nothing else will suffice. That may sound like blasphemy to disciples of Cisneros & Hakius’ former incarnation as ‘90s stoner rock/doom metal pioneers Sleep - infamous for inclusion on the Gummo soundtrack - but we’ll take Om over them any day. A hill we’ll die on, with this album blasting full volume.

Like the hellbound offspring of Led Zeppelin, Black Sabbath, and Popol Vuh, the duo set extraordinary levels in the A-side ‘On the Mountain at Dawn’, channelling heavy histories of modal hard rock and aspects of Tibetan, Byzantine, and Ethiopian mysticism into 23 minutes of molten churn that does not let go. It just builds and collapses into itself with a peerless, sustained intensity of vision, making the slightest changes feel like epic moments, and saving a turbo-charged afterburn for the 2nd half, when the driving cymbals double up and the riff goes full sicko mode. Throw in the B-side’s slower, slightly more succinct heck of ‘Kapila’s Theme’ and reaper-scythed percussion that pushes the axe to new depths on ‘Annapurna’, and you have a total masterpiece that hits like nowt else.

items.body:
A Detroit house/jazz masterpiece, 2004, mercifully back in circulation on vinyl for as long as stocks last (ie, not long) - don’t think twice if you spent the last 20 years kicking yourself for missing out - really is the GOAT.

'Black Mahogani’ first landed some 10 years into Kenny Dixon Jr.’s catalogue and firmly pinned him on the map with its hugely ambitious scope and attention to detail. His 5th and arguably most celebrated studio album, it’s also by far his most coveted, partly due to being neglected from reissue schemes, which has led to a status that’s grown in step with KDJ’s renown. 

It still fully kills with ten top shelf cuts sifted from prized 12”s dating back to the late ‘90s and here stitched with exclusive gear into a sort of deep jazz soundtrack updated with a Detroit house heartbeat and leagues-deep soul, effortlessly bridging epochs with timeless steez.

To pluck a few jewels from its crown, centrepiece ’Shades of Jae’ is a masterclass in deferred kick drum gratification that never fails in the dance, and the lush, jazz-taught sashay of ‘Runaway’ and sampledelia of ‘Mahogani 9000’ still take our breath away. But it’s really all best taken in longform context, from the first frisson of hi-hats and Roberta Sweed’s aching croon on ‘Holiday’ thru the filter chicanery of a closing title tune that only sets one up to do it over and again...
items._cn_summary: 底特律浩室与爵士的融合之作，Kenny Dixon Jr.（Moodymann）的这张2004年专辑以深邃的灵魂感和Jazz元素为核心，将90年代末期的12寸单曲进行重新整合，形成兼具舞曲功能性和艺术深度的聆听体验。专辑融合了延迟底鼓、爵士钢琴段落、灵魂乐人声采样等元素，在传统底特律电子音乐框架内展现了独特的个人风格。然而相比用户的实验/学院爵士偏好，该作品的实验性和前卫程度有限，整体更偏向成熟的舞曲制作而非突破性探索，适合对电子音乐有进阶兴趣的听众。

Beamed in direct from his Space Station Ø studio for longtime patrons Ostgut Ton, ‘Planetary People’ trades in a patented style of machine music that Slater, along with Detroit legends such as Jeff Mills, Claude Young, and Terrence Dixon, plus European heads Donato Dozzy or Steve Bicknell, have made
items.body:
Luke Slater’s pioneering bleep techno vessel PAS returns to a club landscape that he helped spawn in the ’90s, with a striking exposition of techno purism primed for the new wave of pouting pumpers.

Beamed in direct from his Space Station Ø studio for longtime patrons Ostgut Ton, ‘Planetary People’ trades in a patented style of machine music that Slater, along with Detroit legends such as Jeff Mills, Claude Young, and Terrence Dixon, plus European heads Donato Dozzy or Steve Bicknell, have made into the the prevailing sound of Berlin and contemporary techno clubs worldwide. 

Slater’s feel for effortless momentum continues to make his work stand out from the crowd on these 13 new missives, each eagerly awaiting application in warehouse endurance tests and late-for-work crosstown trots. As such it rolls out in thru-line for those who consume albums as intended, with expert harness and whip control from the acid afterburn of intro ‘Into the Night’ to what sounds like Konono No.1 at Berghain in ‘Labyrinth’, peak time canter in ‘Thunder Major’, and 9 minutes of sublime tension to closer ‘Presently My Soul Grew Stronger’.

But if you just need to big rockets, ‘Quadrant 10’ will electrify any ‘floor with its rattling buzz, and the tight knit arps of ‘Brave Cosmo’ will piston tendons along with the cavernous slay of ‘Retina Burn’, and you just know the recoiling bounce of ‘Beton Brut’ is going to soundtrack some of the heaviest club and festival moments of summer ’26 and beyond.

items.body: Album reviews CAMiNOS Introduces Mediterranean-Focused Debut EP Angel Romero May 30, 2026 No Comments CAMiNOS Flamenco French music Mediterranean music world fusion world music CAMiNOS – CAMiNOS (Piment Rouge Production / ACEL WORLD WIDE / InOuïe Distribution, 2026) Marseille-based group CAMiNOS recently released its self-titled EP titled CAMiNOS (paths in Spanish). Led by composer and guitarist Germain Chaperon, the project presents original, inventive guitar compositions and a repertoire deeply grounded in Mediterranean traditions. CAMiNOS reflects a life journey, signified by the paths we follow, cross, and create. The EP features songs in Occitan, Spanish, and Italian. Musically, CAMiNOS skillfully amalgamates flamenco , jazz, contemporary music, and world music influences from India, Eastern Europe, North Africa, and South America. Chaperon’s guitar work gives the project a strong flamenco flavor. Vocalist Neda Cainero brings a passionate multilingual approach influenced by chanson, jazz, cumbia, reggae, and tarantella. Bassist Marek Eichler adds experience from the Czech and Dutch jazz-rock scenes, as well as later work with Gnawa music and flamenco. Drummer Sven Clerx contributes a background in experimental jazz and live performance. Together, the quartet has developed CAMiNOS as a finely crafted cross-cultural project that celebrates movement, encounter, and shared musical exchange. Author: Angel Romero Angel Romero y Ruiz has dedicated his life to musical exploration. His efforts included the creation of two online portals, worldmusiccentral.org and musicasdelmundo.com . In addition, Angel is the co-founder of the Transglobal World Music Chart , a panel of world music DJs and writers that celebrates global sounds. Furthermore, he delved into the record business, producing world music studio albums and compilations. His works have appeared on Alula Records, Ellipsis Arts, Indígena Records and Music of the World.

items.body: Review by tszirmay — It's always a fine green morning (wink, nod) in ProgRogue Land when I get a message from Ally Carter, with a nice download for me to peruse. Because it invariably means a new album is about to be released from this talented band that I happen to admire since their debut. Their seventh album is the second volume of last year's tasty The Land, the Sea, the Air, which garnered rave reviews from yours truly as pretty much the majority of the Prog community. Ally, Tree, David and Tom are back once again, as if it was only yesterday , consolidating their musical stance on the degrading ecology of our tired planet. At the risk of repeating myself, this band sticks to its principles with orthodox zeal, maintaining not only their style and their immediately recognizable sound, but also keeping continuity with a personal artwork display that is applause worthy. Three mega tracks are their usual recipe, and why change that, after all they are not the Ramones! "Song of the Rainforest" will dominate 21 minutes and 21 seconds of your time, keeping you far away from those pesky cell phones, as well as all other modern technological distractions. Tree Stewart settles the proper mood on her perennially silky keyboards, stitching into the melodic fabric a sundry of effects, bassist Dave Greenaway laying down his basso profundo with meticulous authority, Tom Jackson ticking, tocking and otherwise locking, straight into the groove. Ally glides in with his jade green guitar unbothered , caressing his neck with one hand , while the other performs various wrist flickers on his six strings. The atmosphere is set, perhaps somewhere deep in the Colombian forest where it rains more than anywhere else, an ode to the mighty power that Mother Nature chooses to unleash willy nilly, at her discretion. When Ally interjects with his brassy saxophone, the instrument most resembling the human voice, he pleads the case for all mankind. When the blowing gets severe, it's surely a sign of repentance and begging for forgiveness. Heavy weather jazz time. The sweeping keyboards convey the sorrowful resignation of endless human intrusion into where it shouldn't belong, her ominously angry synthesizers (and famed Roli Seaboard) slash fiercely in defence of the despairing jungle and its right to survive, I daresay even flourish. Still heavy but not quite jazzy, more like organized bedlam. And then, extended peaceful interjections of velvety softness come across as soothing panacea, Tree's flutes leading the serene parade, ethereal yet very much alive. The crushing solemnity in the final section is heart stopping, Tree and Ally laying down a magic carpet ride of contemplative introspection, maybe even self healing, in essence. When the rhythm section forcefully slams its foot down, it serves as a defensive anchor being cast, a line in the forest that will not be invaded anymore, come hell or (gulp) high water! In my mind, and assuredly yours when you hear it, this is their finest track and finest hour ever. There is a reason why Tree Stewart was voted among the top keyboard players in prog recently, she can play like the wind, as witnessed by her immaculate display on piano on "Rivers of Tears", mastering not only technique but also impeccable emotion, as one can hear the rivers and the tears in her performance. Throw in the lush orchestrations, Ally's discreet guitar tremors, the subtle cymbal work, and the reverence in the bass, the only discovery left is Tree's vocal which is delivered with empathy. The swerve into a jazzier surroundings becomes obvious as the piano and sax conspire to whip up some well-deserved groovy frenzy, after all, these are consummate musicians! This 15-minute epic refuses to stick too long in any redundancy, so the mid-section suddenly flips the script by injecting more sombre sequences, led by a forcefully darker vocal chant, and then plummeting into complex rhythmic polyrhythmic chaos that will drop that jaw of yours. The churning keyboards swirl and twirl like dervishes on fire. Tree even daring a few 'space shanties' made famous by the late Gilly Smith of Gong. This section surely owes some winks toward that legendary band; there are many little hints one can discern. And just when you may think 'what could they possibly come up with next after such a two-handed slap across the musical face', the band opt for a swooning melody so immediately attractive that I fell to my knees hearing the first time, sung with utter conviction, as a cross between Olivia Sparnenn of Mostly Autumn and hint of Janis Joplin, I swear on my honour! Here, total simplicity rules, the orchestral keyboards convey harmony only a song title called "Paradise" could get away with. Indeed, this is most heavenly, even the sax plays the gentle card. Nearly 9 minutes of bliss that could have/should have/and would have continued for another 10 minutes, making my day and night. Wow! Their best yet. 5 seasons of Green
items._cn_summary: 这是一张新前卫摇滚专辑，围绕生态主题展开，分为三首长篇作品。专辑以21分钟的主打曲目《Song of the Rainforest》为核心，融合了爵士元素（萨克斯风）和实验音效（Rol i Seaboard合成器、环境氛围营造），长笛编排增添了世界音乐色彩。乐队保持了新前卫摇滚的传统结构——长篇叙事、键盘主导、吉他驱动，同时加入即兴爵士段落。主题聚焦亚马逊丛林保护，以哥伦比亚热带雨林为背景。音乐上既有沉重的爵士摇滚段落，也有宁静的氛围过渡，展现了生态主题的戏剧张力。整体风格稳健，符合新前卫摇滚的典型范式，融合度较高但创新性有限，适合喜欢长篇前卫摇滚与生态主题融合的听众。

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — Having been listening to this album for years now, I still find the opening track 'The City Has NoEmpathy' the most interesting and memorable part of it. 'Scenes from Ephemeral City' is the 2011self-released debut studio album from Australian progressive rock/metal band Caligula's Horse, whowere founded by guitarist Sam Vallen (who is the engineer and producer of this release) and vocalistJim Grey sometime in 2010. The band's powerful and melodic style is quite impressive and immediate,as heard on this daring debut collection, which is also fairly accessible. Achieving a fine balancebetween the technical guitar-heavy parts and the dreamier melodic passages, C-Horse deliver arecognizable style that definitely emphasizes the warm and expressive singing style of Jim Grey, whois a truly excellent performer. 'Scenes' was definitely composed by guitar player Sam Vallen, whoexhibits a fabulous command of his instrument, including several crafty acoustic bits, a good amountof really technical, proggy riffs, and an abundance of musically acute solos.The music on this album resembles the output of Scale the Summit, Plini and Haken, all of which arecontemporaries of Caligula's Horse, and are often mentioned together in discussions on the new waveof prog metal. As for the album itself, the original track list features seven songs, of which theaforementioned opening track is a really strong contender for being one of the most memorable piecesof modern prog metal, with its gritty guitar playing and inviting vocals. The two instrumentals'Singularity' and 'Calliope's Son' are really good, too, but some of the longer tracks like 'Alonein the World' (sitting at eleven minutes) and 'Silence' (at seven) fail to leave a lastingimpression and miss that characteristic sound or hook that the band would deliver on subsequentreleases. The Inside Out Music reissue of this LP features two extra tracks, of which the single'Colossus' is a really fine entry and once again exhibits the inherent melodicism within Caligula'sHorse's songwriting. Overall, this is an impressive debut album, especially given the fact that itwas self-produced and self-released (it does sound great all the way through!), but it lacks notableideas, which makes it one of the least impressive corners of the band's discography.
items._cn_summary: 澳大利亚前卫金属乐队Caligula's Horse的首张专辑，融合技术性吉他演奏与旋律化的演唱风格，作品中可见与Scale the Summit、Plini、Haken等同期乐队的相似性。开场曲《The City Has No Empathy》以及两首器乐曲表现出色，吉他手Sam Vallen的演奏技术精湛，整体制作质量不俗。作为独立发行的出道作具备一定诚意，但乐评指出作品在创意层面缺乏突破，长曲目未能形成令人印象深刻的主题hook，与乐队后续作品存在差距。对于偏好实验前卫金属的听众而言具有参考价值，但融合度相对单一，与用户口味中的爵士、电子、实验等跨领域融合偏好匹配度有限。
