items.body: Review by tszirmay — "Gil Gilad was formed in County Durham, UK, in 1979 by university students interested in long-form music. The original members went their separate ways sometime after 1981. Three of the original members (Paul Dobson, Kev Stevens, and Nev Tobin) started writing music again starting around 2015 when the band made its appearance with a Facebook page sharing tracks from Soundcloud. After many years, the band finally released its debut album in 2024 titled 'A Record of the Unworldly and the Strange' inspired by entrepreneur and chemist John Walker. The current line-up as of December 2025 is Paul Dobson (guitars, keyboards, backing vocals), Nev Tobin (lead vocals, keyboards), Kev Stevens (drums, keyboards, guitar, backing vocals), and Geoff Parkin (lead guitar, backing vocals)". This is the second chapter in the Walker saga, and as such, the band take us on a sweeping 70-minute sonic adventure, with nods and winks to a series of classic British writers as well as harkening back at classics like Jeff Wayne's War of the Worlds.HG Wells is the ignition for the opener "Prisoners of Time", a prototypical neo-prog track that features all the instrumentalists showing off their wares, blitzing synthesizer and keyboard runs, solid bass underfoot, concrete drum propellants and Nev Tobin's rather attractive vocal tone and delivery. 'We all have time machines?those that take us back are memories and those that carry us forward are dreams.'Up next under the auspices of philosopher, logician, mathematician Bertrand Russell "We Are Scientists Not Philosophers" selects a lighter approach to complex thought based on 'Science is what you know. Philosophy is what you don't know'. Here the tempo is first leisurely and playful, with a sudden plunge into darker spheres where the austere narration challenges the weakness of mind. The rhythmic piano is maddeningly efficient, as it sits front and center, its ivory keys glowing brightly. There is a definite art-rock slant, perhaps winking at bands like 10cc or even Alan Parsons Project. "The Traveller: Altered Destiny" has theoretical physicist Charles Peacock as an influence, and musically, the APP hint comes across luminously, swirling keyboard setting the foundation on which basic bass and drum stakes are planted 'We explore the vagaries of time; Parallel worlds where everything happens in tandem with everything else. However, our minds are ill-disposed to extract the truth behind the thin veils that blind us.' An exuberant electronic prog workout that offers a most attractive plane to enjoy, melodically powerful, yet accessible, full of thrilling spills. There is an 80s electro feel to the vocals which are extremely attractive, as it comes across well with all the backing mellotrons, a fascinating track to be sure! John Walker speaking of his loss of Hai-Yun is expressed on "A Chance to Speak" , a short two-minute waver, dispensing a very elegant British sound, focused on piano and aery vocals. 'I last saw her on the outskirts of Durham?How she danced on those silken, silver threads I will never know: She was elegance and strength, and light as floating feathers?'. A proggier trio of tracks form the middle core of this release, and my favourite section , first up "The Watchers", owner of a cinematic slice of imaginary sights and sounds, caught in a lush whirlwind, immediately attractive with a strong melodic spine and dramatic vocals that include amazing, hushed backing vocals and effects galore. 'The primary objective of a Watcher is to ensure the safety and security of the community, by whatever means necessary within the limits of the primary directive set out in Principles of Service'. This track could have ben a segue to APP's I Robot masterpiece "The Voice". Next of kin, "Escape from York" possesses a cosmic urgency that felt like running from the devil. Hurried, panting and awesome electronics make this cascading piece of energy most compelling. The looping bass finale a killer. 'We need to go, or you will not live out the hour!' . Who else but the perennial JRR Tolkien as inspiration on a Kate Bush-like vocal to die for on "A Walk in the Woods" (6:14), a stylistically dynamic tour de force, showing intense attention to mood and atmosphere, a comfortable sense of freedom of pace, even though engulfed in the mysterious solitude of nature. 'I thought all the trees were whispering to each other, passing news and plots along in an unintelligible language; and the branches swayed and groped without any wind.' The loving screech of Geoff Parkin's electric guitar does the piece justice. A definite highlight. A welcome return to "Dreams of Samira" channels a page from Percy Byshe Shelley's Love's Philosophy, recalling German band RPWL in terms of style and structure, keyboard and rhythm section heavy, sliced open by a bitter guitar recollection, weaving expertly with a companion synthesizer expression, piano and mellotron to finish off. 'Nothing in the world is single, All things by a law divine. In one spirit meet and mingle. Why not I with thine?'On the two next thrilling pieces, William Gibson the American-Canadian writer ("Neuromancer") provides the essence for the more experimental "The Burghers", a clanging glance into the impending fate of mankind, based on sociological conflicts that are now a global spectacle. Cyberpunk rebellion of yore now transforming itself into internet anarchy. 'The future has already arrived; it's just not evenly distributed yet'. Musically, it's a deliberate ball of confusing distortions, oblique settings and a desperately gloomy finale. "Before Today is Yesterday" suggests too many voices in our heads, forming a dangerously growing series of phenomena as insomnia, depression and data fatigue. No time left for yesterday's reality, only tomorrow's incertitude. Opinion-peddling rules the day. 'And we danced on the brink of an unknown future, to an echo from a vanished past'. Nev Tobin stars on the grim "Darkened Embers of Suspicion" has a slight Kashmir-ian aura (the Led Zep version , not the disputed region!), a brooding snarl of reflection, the result of the previous discussed tracks, focusing on endless negatives, eschewing whatever progressive good has been achieved on so many levels. Negativity sells. 'In the wastelands of memory, our past haunts us when all is dark and rested. We become robed in lost moments, and half remembered phrases that twist and torment'.The pleasantly lilting "The Strange Long Night" hides an underlying message of disbelief 'Believe what? That tomorrow night beneath the full moon, I'll sprout hair and fangs and eat people? It's bulls**t!'. The piece is somewhat dark, quirky and oblique, the way an odd lengthy evening may easily become. What better segue than the tempestuous fury of "The Storm", a six-minute+ tornado of sound with raging synths, howling gales of mellotron, booming bass curvatures and tectonic drum patterns that will stimulate the blood flow. 'Batten down and lock up! Sound the alarm! Storm coming!'. A relentless pummeling can do wonders for the energy levels, lest we forget that Mother Nature can be cruel to be kind, in the right measure. The 70-minute opus finalizes its run on "The Nature of Time", a hint from William Wordsworth's "Composed During a Storm", showing abundantly the painstaking details marshaled by the band in maintaining flow, thematically as well as infusing sufficient musical variety to keep the headphones on, all along the adventure. "He raised his eye Soul-smitten; for, that instant, did appear large space ('mid dreadful clouds) of purest sky, An azure disc, shield of Tranquillity; Invisible, unlooked-for, minister of providential goodness ever nigh!". A solitary two-note piano puts this to bed effortlessly.An excellent album, that caught me quite by surprise, as the first audition had not grabbed me completely. By the second, it was hook, line and sinker. Bravo, lads , well played! 4.5 whiskey sours.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张融合哲学思考与文学意象的交响前卫摇滚长篇专辑，时长约70分钟，将HG Wells、Bertrand Russell等经典英国作家的思想脉络编织进音乐叙事中。专辑采用典型的新古典主义交响摇滚框架，键盘与合成器的闪烁编排占据主导地位，钢琴段落尤为突出，在艺术摇滚向度上有所表现。电子化元素和80年代电子音效的运用为作品增添了一层现代感，旋律线兼具力量与可听性。尽管与10cc、Alan Parsons Project等经典艺术摇滚存在明显关联，整体制作扎实，但在实验性和突破性上并未超越传统前卫摇滚的范畴。对于偏好实验与前卫风格的用户而言，这张专辑提供了还算丰富的声响层次和跨界的文学底蕴。

items.body: Starsign emerged in the 1990s and was driven by the German duo Oliver Teßmer and Matthias Blechschmidt. At the time, they released several EPs, along with an album that appeared in 2003. After that, things went quiet for more than two decades, but the duo revived the project a few years ago. Following several high-profile singles, they released “Silver Linings” earlier this year, featuring 10 tracks. The influences running through “Silver Linings” are quite diverse, yet they fit perfectly within the Electro-Pop genre. The songs move between quiet, floating pieces on the one hand and more danceable tracks on the other. Depeche Mode can occasionally be felt lurking around the corner, while other tracks seem inspired by Mesh. However, Starsign is by no means a copycat; rather, they have managed to blend these diverse elements into a smooth and enjoyable whole. Some songs are beautifully crafted and reveal subtle details in the production. Personally, I prefer their ‘heavier’ tracks, and although I do miss an undeniable standout hit on the album, “Silver Linings” still has a great deal to offer. (Rating:8). Listen to “Shiver”: https://infactedrecordings.bandcamp.com/track/shiver
items._cn_summary: 德国双人组合Starsign的回归之作《Silver Linings》是一张Electro-Pop风格专辑，收录10首曲目。专辑在氛围感强的慢歌与可跳舞的节奏感曲目之间游走，明显受到Depeche Mode和Mesh等合成器流行乐先驱的影响，同时融入了轻柔与力量感的对比。评论者肯定其制作精细、细节丰富，能够将不同影响有机融合而非简单模仿德国电子乐队的模式。然而专辑整体更偏向流行电子范畴，缺少实验性、极端或暗潮特质，与用户偏好列表中的实验/前卫、爵士、电子（IDM/glitch）及暗潮类型存在一定差距，在创新性上虽有良好制作水平但未展现突破性探索。对于偏好实验与暗潮的听众而言，这是一张扎实的电子流行作品，但难以满足更深层的先锋或跨界期待。

Home » Jazz Articles » Album Review » Sharon Minemoto: Goodbye, Strawberry Hill

 LIKE 1
Sharon Minemoto: Goodbye, Strawberry Hill
By Jack Bowers
May 30, 2026
View read count
The years 1942 through 1945 embody a dark chapter in American and Canadian history—not only in terms of the grievous losses of life and treasure during World War II but also for the abandonment of human rights and the cruel and indefensible treatment of many thousands of their fellow citizens, more specifically those of Japanese descent.

Generations have passed, and most people today have either forgotten or never knew about what happened during those few horrendous years—but many Japanese-Americans remember all too well how their families and friends were badly mistreated and interned in prison camps simply because they looked and often spoke Japanese.

Canadian-born pianist Sharon Minemoto, whose family was forced to leave its farm in Strawberry Hill, British Columbia, imprisoned for the duration of the war and later banned from ever returning to western Canada, pays tribute to her dehumanized forebears on Goodbye, Strawberry Hill, a splendid quartet date for which she wrote or co-wrote nine of the ten intimate and often heartbreaking numbers.

Minemoto's compositions (and one other, "Akatombo," by Kosaku Yamada) are thematic in that they depict people, places, events or other aspects of the mass confinement. But that becomes irrelevant once the music starts. What does matter is that Minemoto's able quartet is squarely focused on every measure, endowing each tune with an abundance of warmth and awareness.

Even though this is Minemoto's gig, an argument could be made that hers is not the most impressive voice in the room; that honor would be reserved for tenor saxophonist Jon Bentley who is astute and admirable on every number. And that is not meant to suggest that Minemoto is less than persuasive, as her solos are invariably pleasing and she embraces the keyboard with an earnestness born of love.

Minemoto wrote the buoyant opening theme, "Rosebud," for an aunt who survived an abusive family relationship, "Eulogy" for a grandfather whose own father died when he was only seven years old. "No Way Out" characterizes anti-Japanese sentiment after the war, "Captive Voyage" her mother's family's arduous return to Japan from Canada, "Ashes Falling Like Leaves, "her father's memories of the atomic bomb attack on Hiroshima (he was living near the site), "An Ocean Between Us" her father's return to Canada as a teen-ager after restrictions on Japanese residency were eased.

The solemn "Meditation," inspired by Minemoto's vision of her grandfather and others using prayer beads during their internment, is given added color by drummer Bernie Arai's use of the flute-like Japanese hotchiku. Yamada's lone composition, "Akatombo," translates into "Dragonfly," which signifies change and transformation in British Columbia's First Nations culture. "Eulogy," which follows, includes the first of several adept solos by bassist Darren Radtke.

Setting aside its disheartening provenance, Goodbye, Strawberry Hill is a consistently pleasing and well-played session. That it is also one with a positive and inspiring message to impart makes it even more fascinating and desirable.
Track Listing

Rosebud (for Keiko Robson); Meditation; Nenju (Prayer Beads); Eulogy (for Sunawa Minemoto); No Way Out; Captive Voyage; Ashes Falling Like Leaves; Akatombo; Dragonfly; An Ocean Between Us.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由加拿大日裔钢琴家Sharon Minemoto领衔的爵士四重奏演奏，作品围绕二战期间日裔加拿大人被囚禁的历史经历展开。九首原创曲目与一首传统作品的组合，通过爵士语汇呈现个人化叙事，兼具历史文献价值与音乐表现力。音乐风格偏向传统的学院派爵士，但融入日本传统乐器hotchiku及亚洲音乐元素，形成与用户偏好相契合的世界音乐与爵士跨界融合。 Tenor萨克斯手Jon Bentley的表现尤为突出，钢琴演奏则以真诚的情感表达见长。作为独立发行的专辑，其独特的主题视角与文化深度为作品增色，但整体音乐语汇仍以传统爵士框架为主。

items.body: Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris café, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur. Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth. Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I’m guessing here), and musical saw. Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt) The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle, just to get the list started. Ukulele Lady (excerpt) The liner notes point out that “Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.” Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous “Ukulele Lady” from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie’s 1971 album Hobo’s Lullaby. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler. N'oublie pas Gréco (excerpt) A more serious item is “N’oublie pas Gréco” (Don’t Forget Gréco”) is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gréco, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like “Fumée aux yeux” (“Smoke Gets in Your Eyes”), “Boude pas” (“Take Five”), and “Prive d’amour” (“As Time Goes By”). This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, “The young have fire, but we have light.” In its own little corner, Les Crimes du Musette shines bright. items._cn_summary: 法国乐队Les Primitifs du Futur的《Les Crimes du Mussette》展现了跨时代的音乐融合，汇聚bal-musette、ragtime、jug、美国skiffle及法国chanson等多元风格。27首短曲目以手风琴为核心，辅以萨克斯、颤音琴、单簧管、班卓、尤克里里、泰勒明琴等复古乐器，营造出难以归类的独特声响。乐队从78转老唱片中汲取灵感，将长年被遗忘的音乐形式重新赋予生命力。Dominique Cravic以类同莫里斯·谢瓦利埃的念唱风格演绎，向朱丽叶·格雷科等法国文化偶像致敬。音乐虽非实验/前卫导向，但在传统与跨界层面具有独特的融合价值，体现出独立音乐人对于历史音乐遗产的执着与热忱。

items.album: John Alan Urquhart shares their master class in artistic brevity. »
items.body: Tiny Sun creates tiny songs that give off light and heat well out of proportion to their size. Composed, performed, and produced by Martina Sorbara, Jonathan Goldsmith, and Don Rooke, the record is vaguely Americana, with plucked guitars and ukuleles, chiming keyboards, and the lonesome slide of the guitar. Vanishment contains eighteen sparkling miniatures - that take a scant 34 minutes to negotiate - notable for their economy of arrangement and the subtle directness of the lyrics. The tracks glow with Martina’s clear, high, and sometimes fragile voice. The songs are about loss: lost love, lost confidence, but sometimes about resignation to the enigmatic quirks of the world. The tone of wry fatalism mirrors the fact that this project is the work of many years of collaboration and email exchanges while the trio pursued their musical day jobs. Jonathan Goldsmith is an award-winning composer for television and film, Don Rooke fronts the Toronto roots band The Henrys, and Martina Sorbara is known for folk, electropop, and her band Dragonette. Kerosene Madrigal The range of backgrounds leads to many styles, and the record betrays interesting influences. The opening track, “Kerosene Madrigal,” is a sort of miner’s blues reminiscent of Michelle Shocked. The soul-country of “Imagined Love” reminded me of fellow Torontonians Cowboy Junkies, especially the sweet organ. The stoic and twangy “Don’t Fault the Stars for Falling” could have been a Dolly Parton tune. A Grand Expanse “A Grand Expanse” has a more ambitious arrangement. It sounds like the end-credits song from a long-ago film we only vaguely remember. It says everything it needs to in one minute and twenty seconds and exactly 38 words. It is quintessential Tiny Sun. The entire recording feels like music from a dream, and since no one knows exactly what dream music sounds like, this could be it. Berceuse Tiny Sun will perform the entire album at Toronto’s Koerner Hall on May 14, 2026. Where do you find the recordings? items._cn_summary: Tiny Sun的《Vanishment》是一张充满极简美学的Americana风格专辑，收录18首短曲，总长34分钟。专辑以拨弦吉他、尤克里里和键盘为主，Martina Sorbara高亢且略带脆弱的嗓音为音乐增添光彩。歌词主题围绕失落、自信丧失及对世界荒诞的听天由命，透着一种讽刺的宿命感。Don Rooke来自多伦多根源乐队The Henrys，Jonathan Goldsmith是获奖电影配乐师，这些背景使专辑在传统民谣中融入了叙事性与氛围感。曲目如“Kerosene Madrigal”和“Imagined Love”分别致敬Michelle Shocked和Cowboy Junkies，但整体更注重结构的精简与歌词的直接。专辑适合喜爱独立民谣与世界音乐融合的听众，但缺乏实验性或前卫元素。

items.body: After nine previous albums and a 25-year career at the forefront of world music, Lucas Santtana is fluent in the many genres of Brazilian music. His new project, Brasiliano, is a musical exploration of the languages of Brazil. With songs sung in Portuguese, French, English, Spanish, Occitan, Cape Verde Creole, and Tupy-Guarani, a Brazilian native language, Santtana has assembled guest lyricists and vocalists representing a range of musical and linguistic influences. The result is a warm and compelling musical treatise on the diverse cultural history of Brazil, expressed through the Brazilian variant of Portuguese, best described as Brasiliano. Returning to his roots, the opening cut and lead single “A história de nossa língua” features Gilberto Gil, a national treasure with whom Santtana worked early in his career. As the liner notes explain, Brasiliano, the language, is depicted in the song as a feminine character meeting other people (languages) on her travels, tracing the history of the language as an offshoot of Latin, including “Occitan, Celtic, Galician, Portuguese, Mozarabic, and others. The chorus features Indigenous words that are part of everyday Brazilian culture: Itapuã, Ipanema, Maracanã, Capoeira, etc.” This song acts as a sort of abstract for the dissertation to follow. Santtana and Gil call and respond over what has become the composer’s trademark mixture of detailed, layered, human-played instruments, including on this track violins and violas, piano, guitars, mellotron, and synths. Throughout the record, Santtana creates an inviting effect with a contemporary gloss, combined with the warm resonance of wood, drum skins, wire strings, sticks, bows, and voices. The album features a range of styles, from the lively party track “Ver meu povo se abraçar” to the convincing reggae of the second single, “Que seja um reggae”. With sophisticated songcraft and inspired arrangements, the songs remain inviting and accessible. Fitting with the theme of the interrelationships among languages, Brasiliano is a celebration of international collaboration. For example, “Independência” features Karyna Gomes, a singer from Guinea-Bissau; Anglo-French performer Piers Faccini sings “Battre des ailes” accompanied by an appropriately French-sounding accordion; and popular Brazilian singer Flavia Coelho is featured on “Dans le sud feat”. The gentle “Strati di tempo” is the closest to Santtana’s earliest singer/guitarist style, with Italian star Dimartino taking the lead vocals. Language is culture; so too are politics. And with the involvement of Gilberto Gill, who served as Minister of Culture in President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s government and was jailed and exiled for his political affiliations in the 1960s, it is no surprise that this album is overtly political. For example, on “Línguas Gerais,” French rapper Oxmo Puccino “speaks about colonization.” Continuing to quote from the liner notes, “Indigenous languages and cultures in South America were buried under European colonization.” Tainara Takua and Oxmo Puccino sing “Cocanha” in Occitan. Their music is part of a movement to prevent this endangered romance language from dying out. Like his popular previous recording O Paraíso (2023), which was concerned with the environment, Brasiliano is a concept album that explores the role of linguistics in culture. And like on O Paraíso, Santtana is never preachy. The high-minded intellectual roots of the project are made palatable by the creative and appealing music assembled to tell the story. It is a message of inclusion, collaboration, and the joy of our shared occupancy in this place and at this time. With many languages, many musical styles, and the artistry of many talented and effective musical partners, Brasiliano is a remarkable achievement in curation and musical skill with a compelling contemporary message. items.album: Meninas do Sol, Safekeepers of Brazil’s Caiçara Fandango
items.excerpt: The caiçara fandango of the Marujá region, on the southern coast of São Paulo, represents one of the most spirited expressions of Brazil’s traditional coastal…
items.body: Artist Profiles Meninas do Sol, Safekeepers of Brazil’s Caiçara Fandango Oswaldo Lucon May 31, 2026 No Comments Atlantic Forest Biosphere Reserve Brazil Brazilian music caiçara caiçara fandango mangroves Marujá Meninas do Sol Natural World Heritage Site puxirões rabeca world music The caiçara fandango of the Marujá region, on the southern coast of São Paulo, represents one of the most spirited expressions of Brazil’s traditional coastal culture. More than a musical genre or dance practice, fandango embodies a complex social and cultural system that intertwines music, collective labor, spirituality, craftsmanship, and community memory. Firmly established in the traditional caiçara way of life — historically linked to artisanal fishing, small-scale agriculture, canoe building, and mangrove use — the fandango survives as a living testimony of the intimate relationship between local communities and the Atlantic Forest coastal landscape. The communities surrounding Marujá, located near the Tumba Island Reserve and the Cardoso Island State Park, maintain cultural traditions that are deeply connected to the ecological dynamics of the Lagamar estuarine complex. The management plan of the reserve itself recognizes caiçara culture as one of the region’s essential sociocultural attributes, highlighting traditional fishing fences, artisanal practices, and community-based uses of natural resources as part of the territory’s heritage. In 2012, the caiçara fandango was officially recognized by the Instituto do Patrimônio Histórico e Artístico Nacional (National Institute of Historic and Artistic Heritage), also known as IPHAN, as part of Brazil’s Intangible Cultural Heritage. This recognition emphasized that fandango is not merely a folkloric performance, but rather a repository of ancestral knowledge transmitted orally across generations. Its universe includes handmade instruments such as rabecas and violas, poetic singing traditions, rhythmic footwork, communal celebrations, and rituals associated with fishing cycles, religious festivities, and collective work gatherings known as puxirões. In the Marujá region, fandango historically accompanied celebrations after fishing seasons and community efforts, reinforcing social cohesion and cultural continuity. The cultural significance of this territory is further amplified by its environmental and historical importance. According to the reserve’s management plan, the broader Jacupiranga region was protected by the CONDEPHAAT (Brazilian Heritage Council) and later recognized by UNESCO as part of the Atlantic Forest Biosphere Reserve and a Natural World Heritage Site. Within this context, fandango emerges not only as an artistic manifestation, but also as a cultural expression intrinsically linked to biodiversity conservation and territorial permanence. The continuity of caiçara culture depends directly on the preservation of traditional livelihoods, ecological knowledge, and sustainable interactions with mangroves, forests, estuaries, and coastal waters. Contemporary cultural groups have played an important role in renewing and strengthening this heritage. Among them, Meninas do Sol stands out as a female-led caiçara musical collective from the Cananeia region. Their work bridges tradition and contemporary cultural expression, incorporating elements of fandango, coastal rhythms, oral histories, and the everyday life of fishing communities. The group also highlights the role of women in caiçara cultural transmission, an aspect often overlooked in traditional narratives centered on male musicians and fishermen. By performing in festivals, cultural gatherings, and socio-environmental events, Meninas do Sol contributes to the safeguarding of intangible heritage while promoting cultural identity and environmental awareness. Their music reinforces the connection between territory, memory, and community resilience, helping younger generations recognize the value of caiçara traditions in a rapidly changing coastal world. In this sense, the group represents not only a musical ensemble, but also a contemporary expression of cultural resistance and ecological belonging. Together, the fandango tradition and the work of groups such as Meninas do Sol reveal how cultural heritage and environmental conservation are inseparable in the Lagamar region. The preservation of the Atlantic Forest coastline is deeply tied to the survival of the communities that have historically shaped and protected these landscapes through sustainable practices, collective memory, and artistic expression. Discography: Meninas do Sol , EP (2024) More at: — Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/meninasdo_sol/ — Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=61559934119127 Author: Oswaldo Lucon

items.body: Review by The Progolyte — Riccardo Zappa's debut album, by the name of Celestion, is another one of the heavily unknown albums I pulled from various conversations with friends and colleagues alike about the more underground artists of Rock Progressivo Italiano. It was much more on the lighter and delicate side of the spectrum, with classical Italian folk music playing a big part in the overall makeup of this project. Overall, it's pretty good, with a little too much meandering here and there, but I can still tolerate it. It seems like it had a few too many upbeat, rocking sections than I would've liked, but it was enjoyable nonetheless. Moving on, when it comes to the other musicians on this project, the personnel includes Vince Tempera on keyboards, Julius Farmer on bass, Ottavio Corbellini on drums, and George Aghedo on percussion. All guitars, vocals, and (from what I can tell) songwriting are done by Ricardo. The music can feel a little dull at points, not bringing much interesting nor original material to the table. Sure, it's good, and there are some cool moments of jazzy prog and jamming going on that (admittedly) sometimes ruin the mood of the softer acoustic sections, but for the most part I would say it's quite forgettable. The production also didn't help, as I didn't enjoy the actual sound of the record. I feel like out of the five songs that only add up to around thirty-four minutes of runtime, the opening composition and longest of the bunch, Frammenti, is the strongest. It does a good job at introducing us to the sound we'll be having for the majority of the album, that being mysterious folk bits, sometimes mixed in with vibrant ambience, and then short bursts of fun rock music sprinkled in every few minutes or so. I feel like what this album does get right, however, is the soothing and dreamy feeling of some of the music here. It can flow into a hazy state for a while and float the listener along, but sometimes it can feel inconsistent, and I feel like this album would've actually been better if it was more acoustic-based instead of exciting, though at times tension-breaking, rock music slips into the cracks. Other than that, the songs can go in one ear and out the other and don't really stick that much. In conclusion, this will be one of the weaker records from the Rock Progressivo Italiano scene in my opinion. Without keeping an interesting sound going, I find it hard to really enjoy this record or give anything above a light 3/5.
items._cn_summary: 《Celestion》是意大利前卫摇滚场景中一张偏轻柔和民谣风格的作品，融合了古典意大利民间音乐与爵士味的前卫元素。专辑开场曲《Frammenti》奠定了神秘的民谣基调与梦幻氛围，但整体缺乏足够的实验性和创新力度。评论者指出作品存在摇滚段落过多、某些段落略显沉闷、记忆点不足等问题，制作层面也未能增色。尽管带有意大利地下音乐的地区特色加分，且与用户偏好中的实验/前卫和世界音乐有所交集，但1977年的传统前卫摇滚框架限制了其与现代实验审美的契合度。

items.body:
Justin K. Broadrick aka Godflesh & Mick Harris aka Scorn - both one time members of Napalm Death - shell out the nastiest Brum techno clodhoppers on US label Give/Take.

Reprising a double team formation last heard on a split 12” in 2021, the elder statesmen of Birmingham techno and industrial musick deliver eight heavy duty cuts of bin bag-kicking club music. JK Flesh takes the lead with a batch of Regis-esque Brum techno, getting into a kinky, dubbed swing with ‘Conditional’ and slathering on the noise with ‘Transactional,’ beside the fang-toothed attack of ‘Disagreeable’ and Chi-spurred canter of ‘Used / User’ like a DJ Rush with a proper devilish glint in eye.

On the flip his former spar Mick Harris also throws back to the heyday of House of God and early Downwards with a rough batch of bangers taking in the overdriven romp ‘Night Before Rake’, cavernous warehouse shudder of ‘Slightly Over;’ and extra spicy shuffle of ‘Double Red’, plus the Surgeon-esque rave riff riddled into ‘Shelf.’
items._cn_summary: 这是两张前Napalm Death成员的工业Techno合作专辑，JK Flesh呈现Regis风格的伯明翰 techno，带有噪声处理和粗粝的舞曲质感；Mick Harris则以Scorn名义延续早期House of God和Downwards厂牌式的工业节拍，加入Overdrive效果和仓库感声响。整体属于暗潮与电子舞曲的跨界融合，符合用户对工业/暗潮和电子音乐的偏好，但作品风格较为模式化，缺乏实验性突破，更多是对经典工业Techno语境的回归与致敬，而非创新性探索。Boomkat评论信息量一般，未涉及太多创新性评价。

Jack Cooper and Tara Cunningham (1/2 of Modern Nature) present an LP as duo 'The Sleeves'.

"The Sleeves are the duo of Jack Cooper and Tara Cunningham, both likely known to you as one half of Modern Nature. Following an all-instrumental Mossy Tapes release last November, Cooper and Cunningham have recorded 10 new songs showcasing their vocal and guitar interplay with only the faintest echoes of prior efforts (individually or collectively), representing a fully realized leap forward from their largely improvised debut.

'The Sleeves' is a somewhat counter intuitive take on the guitar/vocal duo formula (provided you think there is such a thing) though it's not nearly as simplistic as "the space between the notes" - it would be the height of exaggeration to say an album this simultaneously expansive and incandescent is unprecedented. But it doesn't happen nearly often enough, either.

“What I initially found so familiar and exciting about playing guitar with Jack - and continually do - is that our approach to music is pretty much exactly the same. And that is - to celebrate the space that frames ideas, embraces silence, to play simply, simultaneously championing our respective unembellished guitar sounds, whilst looking for sounds that aren’t like a guitar at all - bells, birds, switching between radio stations etc. It’s rare to find someone who - whatever this means to you - ‘gets it’ - and I think when we started playing guitar together, we both knew the other had something of whatever our ‘it’ was.”

“‘The Sleeves’ is the sum of our shared musical journey thus far, an exciting mix of familiarity and uncharted territory in its approach to structure and how we use our guitars and voices. It feels to me like we are both citing shared references and traditions, whilst floating in our own, single-cell world that is completely genre-less. That grey area is where we seem to thrive. As Jack says, it feels like music that really couldn’t be made by anyone else.” - Tara Cunningham

“Tara and I started playing guitar together at the start of 2024. It was an improvised music night in a railway arch in South London. The set was great but there was a couple of minutes in particular where Tara and I really sort of locked in. We made a record a few weeks later. There was something in the way we played together that felt very intuitive from the start. We recognised a shared approach right away and an affinity to the way each other played.”

“During the summer we got stuck in a traffic jam coming home from a show in Glasgow. We spent a few hours singing along to the Mamas & The Papas and Simon & Garfunkel and over the course of the day, like magic we became The Sleeves. We're excited about it because it feels like music that really couldn’t be made by anyone else. We don’t bring different elements to it. We both bring exactly the same things. It’s the result of our similarities.” - Jack Cooper "
items._cn_summary: Jack Cooper与Tara Cunningham以吉他/人声二重奏形式呈现这张专辑，强调简约编配与空间留白。音乐融合即兴元素与现代民谣风格，融入非常规声响如钟声、鸟鸣与收音机采样。评论指出这张作品跳脱传统流派框架，兼具熟悉感与探索性。然而整体风格更接近独立民谣而非实验或前卫领域，对习惯激进实验的听众而言可能显得温和。Boomkat平台发布，定位独立音乐市场。

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — 'A Dramatic Turn of Events' is the eleventh full-length studio album from Dream Theater and theirfirst with then-new drummer Mike Mangini, who filled the spot for the leaving Mike Portnoy. To myunderstanding, the majority of the drum parts for this album had actually been written prior to thearrival of Mangini, and therefore, he does not get any songwriting credits. Nevertheless, thisrecord delivers the familiar sound of Dream Theater in spades, and despite a few moments ofexperimentation or play-around with other styles, many would safely call this a typical DT release.Compositionally, this is one of the strongest and most sophisticated works from the band, with themajority of the songs being rather lengthy, whereas the album itself bolsters a running time ofseventy-seven-plus minutes, which is a certain prerequisite for a demanding listen. I personallyenjoy this album every time I play it - the riffs sound really refreshing and the unbridledcomplexity of the instrumental sections genuinely blows my head off in a way that only Dream Theaterare able to achieve.Kicking off in a typical melodramatic fashion, we have the excellent song 'On the Backs of Angels',which sees Jordan Rudess playing a continuum in the intro section, and John Petrucci laying down oneof the most effective solos on the album. Apart from this, this song is by far one of the most"typical" Dream Theater compositions on here, which is definitely not a drawback, having become oneof their most well-known songs in recent years. Next up is 'Build Me Up, Break Me Down', a shortersong that instead tries to break away from the band's usual sound and introduces a crunchy nu-metalaesthetic, which is pretty interesting (given that the end result is really solid). The third albumtrack 'Lost Not Forgotten' is an intense piece of prog metal containing all the delightfully complextwists and turns one would expect from Rudess and Petrucci's writing, who would establish themselvesas the primary songwriters of the band for years to come. More melodic guitars enter the scene onthe following track 'This Is the Life', which among other things, slows down the album after thebombastic beginning. With the synth-laden prog rollercoaster 'Bridges in the Sky' and the anthemicsuite 'Outcry', Dream Theater mark a return to their epic sound, offering two lengthy songs thatimpress with some truly creative sections, very musical and ornately composed. The final tracks onthis record include the elegiac 'Far from Heaven', the theatrical epic 'Breaking All Illusions' anda decent pop song that closes off ADTOE.This album does not redefine the progressive metal genre, but in my view this was never the point ofit. It simply serves as an excellent example of songwriting mastery and in my ears happens to be oneof Dream Theater's most consistent efforts in the last fifteen years or so.
items._cn_summary: 前卫金属乐队Dream Theater第十一张录音室专辑，由新任鼓手Mike Mangini参与录制。作品保持了乐队标志性的技术性演奏风格，曲目长度普遍较长，编曲复杂精妙，体现了扎实的古典音乐功底与摇滚能量。专辑中Jordan Rudess与John Petrucci展现了卓越的创作能力，如《On the Backs of Angels》等曲目展现了高水准的独奏段落，部分作品如《Build Me Up, Break Me Down》尝试融入nu-metal元素。作为典型的Progressive Metal作品，其技术性和连贯性表现出色，但对于追求实验性突破或跨界融合的听者而言，整体风格较为传统，未能提供足够的前卫创新与多元融合。

items.body: Review by siLLy puPPy — After a very eclectic debut that eschewed the typical Rock Andaluz playbook that was rockin' Spainin the latter half of the 1970s, the Madrid act AZAHAR followed "Elixir" two years later with itssecond album simply with an eponymous title and refined its sound to a more mainstream stylecourtesy of the addition of drummer Willy Rodriguez de Trujillo who hailed from Seville and honedhis chops with local bands such as Fly, Blizzard and Manantial. He replaced bassist Jorge Barral andsurprisingly the band didn't employ a new bassist for the part but rather used two sessionmusicians: Julio Blasco and Enrique Carmona to fill his shoes. Likewise keyboardist Gusatovo Ros(who left to form Azabache) was replaced by the less flamboyant Manolo Manrique so when the dustsettled it was really only vocalist Dick Zappala and guitarist Antonio Valls returning with acompletely different set of musicians around them.It's immediately apparent on the opening track "Expresso a Ketama" that the band shifted gearssignificantly by adopting the standard Rock Andaluz format of guitar, bass, keys and drums with thefocus on the flamenco rhythms in a standard rock format and deemphasizing the keys that were sodominant on the debut to more of an accent piece with piano runs, and more symphonic light elements.In this regard the band emulated the more pop infused bands such as Alameda or Triana, in a waysounding like something in between the two. While the debut fearlessly treaded in highly progressiveterrain, this second offering plays it safe which was usually the case with the late to the progparty Spanish scene with bands sowing their prog oats on the debut and then forced by financiallimitations to simplify their approach.The second track "La Naranja y el Lim�n" continues the simplified style and was released as a singleshowcasing the band's ability to craft beautiful flamenco infused pop hooks like the best of theSpanish bands. The album pretty much sticks to the new sanctified playbook alternating betweensomewhat faster paced tracks including the instrumental "Zahira" and the slower tracks with thelengthiest track "El Mago Acidote" serving as the best example at 9 1/2 minutes in playing time witha slow ballad-like demeanor yet salvaged by Zappala's passionate vocal delivery which showcases hisrange and creative singing style. The track "Aire y Fuego" offers some interesting syncopationoddities while retaining its flamenco rock sensibilities along with some of the Middle Easternflavors from the debut. The closing "Espresso de Ketama" closes with a another flamenco flavoredinstrumental with a bit more emphasis on the keyboards.Overall this is a major departure from the uninhibited creativity of the debut which for my tastesyielded one of the best progressive rock albums in all of Spain. This self-titled followup is muchmore streamlined for the marketplace and features a fairly uniform approach rather than theexcessive extravaganza of "Elixir." While i much prefer the crafty compositions of the debut, for amore commercial approach, AZAHAR did a really great job of suppressing their most uninhibited progartistry and kept in on the leash while fortifying their standard approach with many of the sameflavors only used more as accent sounds rather than the whole enchilada. While the debut ranks highin my world, this second album is still decent although in this more mainstream style i'd preferTriana, Alameda or even the super slick pop rock band Asfalto nevertheless this is a reallyenjoyable album when taking it at face value and leaving comparisons to the debut behind. This wasthe end of the road for AZAHAR despite 1979 being the peak year of prog releases emerging in Spain.
items._cn_summary: 西班牙马德里乐队AZAHAR于1979年发行的第二张专辑，相比首张专辑《Elixir》的大胆实验性，本作转向更为主流的摇滚安达卢西亚风格。专辑以弗拉门戈节奏为核心，结合标准摇滚编曲（吉他、贝斯、键盘、鼓），键盘部分从首张的主导地位退居为点缀元素，整体更接近Triana、Alameda等流行化西班牙乐队的路线。曲目如《La Naranja y el Limón》展示了弗拉门戈流行钩子的创作能力，而《El Mago Acidote》长达9分半的慢板演绎则通过主唱Zappala的激情演唱保留了艺术张力。专辑仍带有中东风格元素，但整体更为商业化、安全，是西班牙70年代后期prog乐队向市场妥协的典型案例。

items.body: Dessau old-school EBM project T.A.N.K., led by Reinhard Hüber, has released its third album “Broken Mirror” via Electro Aggression Records. The release is available as a digital order and CD order through the label’s Bandcamp page. We first reported the album in January 2025, when Electro Aggression Records announced a new batch of upcoming releases. Broken Mirror by T.A.N.K. The Bandcamp pre-order already unlocked three tracks: “Fight or Suffer”, “Reject” and “Bloodsucker”. Electro Aggression Records has also posted the YouTube previews “Broken Mirror album snippets”, “Fight or Suffer | EAR 019 preview” and “Reject | EAR 019 preview”. About T.A.N.K. Reinhard Hüber, who has a 1990s German punk background, launched T.A.N.K. in Dessau in 2001. The name stands short for “Taktischer Angriff (auf’s) Nervenkostüm”. The first live appearance took place at the first Electric Tremor Festival in Dessau on March 22, 2002. The self-released “T.A.N.K.” EP landed in 2002. It was followed by the debut album “Musica Denaturale” on Ars Electrique in 2003. In 2011, the project contributed “Game of Men” to the 4CD set “Old School Electrology Volume One”. The second full-length, “Return”, came out in 2017 on Electric Tremor Dessau. In the Electro Aggression Records orbit, Hüber also turned up through remix work connected to R010R and Synaptic Defect before “Broken Mirror” moved into the foreground as the next full album. “Broken Mirror” is be the project’s third album holding 19 tracks.
items._cn_summary: T.A.N.K.是德国Dessau的老式EBM项目，第三张专辑《Broken Mirror》收录19首曲目，由独立厂牌Electro Aggression Records发行。乐队主脑Reinhard Hüber拥有1990年代德国朋克背景，T.A.N.K.这个名称取自德文“战术攻击神经”。从乐评信息来看，专辑延续了old-school EBM的复古路线，属于暗潮/工业音乐范畴，符合用户偏好中的暗潮类别，但old-school EBM风格相对传统，实验性和创新元素有限，缺乏与其他音乐类型的跨界融合。评论内容为新闻稿性质，信息基本完整但缺少深度乐评分析。综合来看，该专辑对暗潮听众有一定吸引力，但在实验性和前瞻性方面表现平平。

items.body:
Posthumous reminder of MF Doom’s landmark classic, following the late, great MC’s death at the end of 2020 - with 11 tracks of bonus material.

A staple of our listening diet upon release in 2004 (probably preceded or followed by a listen to his ‘Special Blends volumes), ‘MM….Food’ still stands up among the greatest and most coveted hip hop albums of our time. Beats to bars, it’s a peerless example of Daniel Dumile Thompson’s MF Doom alias, playing out as a sort of stoned comic book fantasy voiced by a cartoon supervillain, literally inspired by Marvel Comics’ Doctor Doom, whose moniker sounds a bit like MF’s real middle name.  

The album oscillate between Doom’s mind-boggling metaphoric wordplay and his signature instrumentals, adapting the golden era ‘90s style of sampledelic collage and rugged rhymes to his singular purpose, and making a marked step on from his earlier work as Zev Love X with the legendary KMD. By choice or osmosis there’s probably a whole generation of headz who’ve committed the bars of ‘MM….Food’ to memory, and we can only recommend a refresher session right here if you’re rusty. Packing bags of nostalgia and vibes for days, it’s a true evergreen.
items._cn_summary: MF DOOM的经典专辑MM..FOOD是一张以采样拼贴为核心的地下嘻哈作品，融合了漫画角色人格与90年代黄金时代的嘻哈美学，歌词编排富有创意且具有强烈的个人风格。然而从用户的实验/前卫音乐取向来看，嘻哈类型本身与用户核心偏好存在距离，专辑虽在嘻哈领域具有开创性地位，但缺乏实验性声响设计、先锋爵士融合或电子元素，采样手法也相对传统。适合对嘻哈有深度兴趣的听众，但对于追求实验性或跨界融合的乐迷而言匹配度有限。

items.body:
Graduate of Mahogani Music and Databass, Detroit’s Sheefy McFly hits critical jit x juke x ghetto-tech x footwork momentum on six vocal bangers for Amsterdam’s Cape St. Francis. Big one FFO Hi-Tech, Omar-S, Urban Tribe, DJ Assault

Known to 313 locals for his colourful murals all over the city, and on this sleeve, Sheefy McFly also trades in a mean vein of uptempo booty music, as heard at his Ghettotechtopia parties and recently on a self-released LP and an ode to local ghetto-tech hotspot, ‘Belle Isle 2099’. His ‘Baddies Only’ EP elevates a signature sound of scudding 808 bass, claps, and keys with a spotlight on six original vocalists from his ends, each characteristic of classic-contemporary Motor City club music and its bridges to Chicago ghettotech.

From the front, he loops bars by duo Etherpussy on undulating subs and electrosoul chords in a style shared by Lola Damone’s bars on ‘Pretty World’, and also calling to mind Andrés’ class GT Flips - a reference point for the choppier soul of ‘You’re Mine’, which tilts more into footwork angularity. Tiptonaires also brings a fierce but warm energy with her faux naïf bars on the chromatic synths of ‘Cute2Nite’, while your trunk’s Cerwin Vegas get a proper test in the Miami Bass-type tremors of ‘Young N Turnt’, voiced by DJ Mobetta.

Party guaranteed!
items._cn_summary: 底特律制作人Sheefy McFly的《Baddies Only》是一张融合jit、juke、ghetto-tech与footwork风格的EP，收录六首以当地vocalist为核心的俱乐部作品。音乐以808贝斯、claps和键盘为主干，融入electrosoul和弦与Miami Bass元素的振动感，带有典型的底特律舞曲特征。虽然并非实验性或前卫性作品，但在舞曲范畴内展现了底特律ghetto-tech的地方特色，融合了与芝加哥音乐文化的关联。对于偏好实验、电子或暗潮的听众而言，此作的商业舞曲属性使其匹配度较低，但对于关注电子舞曲/俱乐部音乐的听众来说，它提供了Detroit派对能量的在地化表达。

items.body:
Following frontman Elias Rønnenfelt's indie throwback smash 'Speak Daggers', cult Danish band Iceage continue to shave down post-punk until it looks more like Britpop. RIYL Fontaines DC, Liars or Gilla Band.

It wouldn't be fair to say that Iceage divided its fanbase when they released the sleek 'Seek Shelter' back in 2021. The album was a surprise to their early champions who'd watched them move from noisy hardcore towards a Talking Heads-indebted post-punk sound, but it was also pretty universally acclaimed, its relative polish deemed acceptable because the songs were genuinely pretty catchy. 'For the Love of Grace & the Hereafter' arrives five years later and in the wake of Rønnenfelt's newfound notoriety - both as a solo star and a tabloid staple. So you can almost predict what direction the band have gone in; their sixth album is their most digestible yet, making its predecessor sound almost rough around the edges in comparison.

Rønnenfelt, for his part, actually sounds refreshed, his voice falling between Shane McGowan's and Bobby Gilespie's and for our money handling the pitchy oddball routine a lot more convincingly than Geese's Cameron Winter. But still, it's better suited to angular material like the Byrne-esque 'Match Head Girl' than it is to melodramatic indie-pop gear like 'No Fear' or Strokes-ish material like 'Tender Blades'. The album will probably be huge, it's just chewy like that - they should take Dean Blunt on tour with them.
items._cn_summary: 丹麦后朋克乐队Iceage的第六张专辑，从早期的噪音硬核和Talking Heads风格的后朋克，进一步转向流畅的Britpop式编曲，是一张面向更广泛听众群体的作品。Rønnenfelt的声音在独立民谣与后朋克之间游走，部分曲目如'Match Head Girl'保留了角度分明的后朋克特质，但更多歌曲呈现出标准的独立流行或车库摇滚面貌。整张专辑制作精良、旋律上口，但与用户偏好的实验/前卫/爵士/电子/暗潮路线存在较大距离，属于主流独立摇滚范畴内的成熟作品。

items.body: Review by Finnforest — Another Mystifying Turn While 1989 saw the release of the wonderful archival Donna Plautilla, it also brought asecond release that year in the form of Non Mettere Le Dita Nel Naso. Google translates thisto "Don't Put Your Fingers in Your Nose," which sums up pretty well, unintentionally or perhapssubconsciously, how unnecessary this release actually was. Confusing labeling indicates both a Bancoalbum and a Francesco Di Giacomo solo album, almost as if the PR team involved couldn't figure outwhat it really was. After hearing the music, one can understand why.I will give them credit for keeping the songwriting in house. Other established pop/rock artistsbegan subbing out this most important part of their craft to paid "hitmakers." While that practicehad always happened for non-songwriter "performers," it is tragic when it becomes embraced by actualmusicians who have proven their songwriting skills already in the past, only to capitulate theirpersonal artistry to product movers due either to label pressure or lost artist confidence. The material here is sadly reminiscent to E Via, though not identical. It has perhaps morerange of styles, better arrangements, and just slightly longer tracks for elaboration. As always,the Banco musicians and the long roster of guests are fantastic players, and we are treated totalent and production quality that stands with anyone. However, as with E Via, the problem isthe material. Who are they making this record for? Despite the treasure they have in Di Giacomo'svoice, despite the finesse of all players involved, there is nothing here that is going to excitethe progressive rock fans of the Darwin era. There is nothing that excites me as a fan ofBuone Notizie's surprisingly fun concoction of mischief and chops. It has a few interesting performance and sound choices here and there. "Qualcosa che rimane" is thestandout moment showcasing Francesco in the spotlight with only very subtle and refined keyboardsand guitar as support. But even if the goal here was pop perfection, others do it better. Thesetracks are a bit long-winded and middle-of-the-road to capture the succinct sugar high pop fanscrave. What to even compare this to? Mid '80s Meatloaf, Celine Dion, a lesser Steve Winwood moment?Answer: It doesn't matter. The only thought I have while listening is pondering what else I could belistening to instead. There is a templated contrivance to the song structures which stranglesimmediacy---very "session-y" sounding instrumental leads laid atop an almost programmed-feeling,often generic backing.The music is not necessarily bad if you have a fetish for sophisticated, middle-aged empty-caloriegloss, and I again resist giving Banco the one-star treatment out of respect for these legendary RPImusicians. But I just can't recommend this album enthusiastically to anyone either. It doesn'tconnect with me in any way. It feels lost in terms of finding its own niche or even finding its ownnecessity. The apparent lack of direction at this point would be further evidenced two years laterwhen they would remake their first two classic albums. I can't get excited about that either. I haveno interest in hearing progressive rock icons attempt to re-conjure the magic of glorious youth,whether that is Banco or Roger Waters. So in my eyes, it does feel like Banco is now firmly lost inthe wilderness artistically. All that said, I also worry this overly harsh take may stem from my own myopic taste profiles, and Iadmit to being less certain about the rating than I was with E Via. Thus I hope others herewill double check me on this---listen to this album and review it. Am I missing the genius somehow?
items._cn_summary: 意大利前卫摇滚乐队Banco del Mutuo Soccorso 1989年发行，风格偏向主流流行摇滚，与真正的实验/前卫精神有较大距离。专辑制作精良，Francesco Di Giacomo的演唱功底依然出色，部分曲目如"Qualcosa che rimane"展现了细腻的键盘与吉他配合。然而整体缺乏创新突破，歌曲结构模式化，编曲偏商业化、中规中矩，被评论者比作80年代中期的Meatloaf或Celine Dion风格。专辑信息混乱，定位模糊，对于追求实验性和艺术深度的听众而言缺乏吸引力。

 LIKE 1
Angela Verbrugge With Ray Gallon: In The Wonder Of The Night
By Pierre Giroux
May 30, 2026
View read count
Canadian jazz vocalist and songwriter Angela Verbrugge understands something that too many contemporary singers miss. Intimacy in jazz is not about shrinking the music but about drawing the audience in. On In  The Wonder of the Night, her duet recording with acclaimed New York pianist Ray Gallon she works within the voice-and-piano format with uncommon confidence, keeping the music in constant motion. The album may carry a nocturnal and lunar thread across its eleven tracks and twelve songs, but beneath the moonlight, there is real swing, harmonic invention and conversational interplay.

The session opens brightly with "S'posin," and the chemistry between the two artists is immediately evident. Verbrugge has a beautiful, inviting voice, digging into the lyrics and dancing atop Gallon's swinging feel. There is power in her delivery, yet she balances it with subtlety and restraint. The originals possess an inner strength that emerges from the same emotional landscape as the standards. Her original bossa nova "Paradise Defined" rests on the notion that genuine human connections are paradise itself, and she delivers it without a trace of sentimentality.

There is also an artful emotional continuum linking the originals "I'm 99% Sure Of You" and "I'm A Cliché." In the first, Verbrugge gives a clever, self-protective voice to someone hesitating on the edge of commitment, still clinging to independence. By the time "I'm A Cliché" arrives, it becomes a quiet ballad that captures the moment when logic begins to yield to love's pull.

Verbrugge also programs the album thoughtfully, pairing "Moonlight Becomes You" with the title track, "In The Wonder of the Night." The former receives a straight-ahead treatment, while the boppish vocalese title track deepens the twilight atmosphere, giving Gallon room to stretch rhythmically and harmonically. Throughout, Gallon proves to be the ideal collaborator. Rooted in the language of bebop and the blues, he continually reshapes the music beneath Verbrugge's vocals with harmonic sophistication and an elevated sense of rhythm. He listens closely, reacts instantly, and never settles for predictable accompaniment.

Irving Berlin's "Reaching for the Moon" offers a delightful juxtaposition as the arrangement shifts the number from a waltz to Latin jazz. Gallon is never distracted by these tempo changes. He has rhythmic elasticity that continually propels the music forward.

The duo closes with "Moonlight in Vermont," showcasing what is self-evident, namely the absence of ego and musical trust. They have accomplished something deceptively difficult by making a familiar format sound newly alive.
Track Listing

S'posin; Paradise Defined; I'm 99% Sure of You; I'm A Cliché; The Gift (Recado Bossa ); On a Night Such as This; Moonlight Becomes You-In The Wonder of the Night; Reaching for the Moon; It's De-Lovely; Goodbye, Little Dream Goodbye; Moonlight in Vermont.

items.body: A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene’s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There’s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout. The opener, “Svennedal,” with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer’s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to “Nordgård,” the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus. Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional “Agnete Of Bjergmanden,” with Guldhammer’s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, “Ormsø,” mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental. Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning – what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?

items.body: A little before the end of the last century, a revelatory compilation appeared, seemingly from nowhere. From Where I Stand: The Black Experience In Country Music opened a window on something so many didn’t even know existed to show that country music had never been a white preserve. That album was a few years before the Carolina Chocolate Drops burst on the scene, reclaiming the Black heritage in country and string band music, plus a great deal more. Genuine Negro Jig, their third release, saw them move up to the prestigious Nonesuch label, a powerful artistic imprimatur, winning them a Grammy for an album very far removed from the mainstream.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Carolina Chocolate Drops的第三张作品，标志着他们从独立厂牌升至Nonesuch，并凭借对黑人乡村音乐和传统弦乐乐队遗产的重新诠释获得格莱美奖。评论指出这张专辑远离主流市场，具有文化上的开创性意义，展现了乡村音乐历史上长期被忽视的黑人音乐传统。作为传统美国民间音乐的重新演绎，该专辑在文化传承层面有其价值，但音乐本体更接近传统民谣与弦乐风格，与用户偏好的实验、前卫、电子、爵士等类型距离较大。Nonesuch虽为知名厂牌，但在此项目上保持了较高的艺术性。评论内容较短，信息量有限，难以进行更深入的音评分析。

items.body: Review by TenYearsAfter — The idea for this musical project came from Flamborough Head's keyboard player Edo Spanninga by accident when he tested some recording equipment in order to record Seventies styled music as a fun-project. Eventually Edo was so excited about the results that he recruited fellow Flamborough Head member Eddie Mulder (guitars and bass) and Odyssice drummer Menno Boomsma to make an album. The name Trion is a contraction of the words 'trio' and 'Mellotron', simply because the band is a trio and because Edo used only Mellotron samples (flute, oboe, strings, organ, cello, vibe and choir) for his keyboard sound on this album. The trio had total freedom to exchange ideas and to work on the arrangements.In 2003 the Dutch trio Trion released their debut CD entitled Tortoise, in 2007 followed by Pilgrim and in 2013 by Funfair Fantasy, all wonderful symphonic prog albums, layered with beautiful Mellotron samples and moving guitarwork. These 3 albums were received very well on Prog Archives by the progheads of Mellotron drenched symphonic rock. In between Colossus (Finnish Progressive Rock Society) invited Trion to contribute to the 2-CD The Spaghetti Epic (featuring progrock bands from all over the world). Trion was OK and delivered the epic Frank. This composition can be found on their second album, in a re-arranged version (close to 23 minutes).And now, anno 2026, Trion's new album entitled Terra Tiempo, after a 13-year hiatus. It contains 12 tracks, mostly instrumental (only two with vocals), ranging between 3 and 7 minutes. The sound is very melodic and harmonic, rooted in the 70s symphonic rock tradition, with a pleasant variety and an own musical touch.Terra Tiempo: The first composition delivers flowing shifting moods and tasteful work on keyboards (from sparkling Grand piano to majestic Mellotron violins) and guitar (from sensitive to fiery), topped with a fluent and dynamic rhythm section. Focus and Camel come to my mind but Trion also presents lots of interesting musical ideas. I notice that the trio sounds as a four-piece formation and has matured during the years.Nautilus: The music alternates between dreamy, a slow rhythm, a tight mid-tempo beat (intro and outro) and bombastic outbursts, embellished with a wide range of keyboards (orchestral, church organ, Hammond, Mellotron flute, synthesizer flights) and wonderful, very moving guitar work.The Return Of Jemetrion: After an intro with tender piano the music turns into a slow rhythm with Mellotron violins, sensitive electric guitar (including slide), floods of Hammond and synthesizer runs. What a wonderful interplay between the guitar and keyboards, firmly rooted in the 70s symphonic rock tradition (from Focus to Camel). Next a dreamy interlude with Mellotron flute and a spacey synthesizer solo, and in the end the sensitive electric guitar play returns.Aftertouch: After flashy synthesizer flights, Hammond and powerful drum beats a slow rhythm follows, featuring a blend of Mellotron violins, synthesizer runs, soaring Hammond and moving guitar runs, it sounds very dynamic and compelling. Halfway slide guitar, blended with lush Mellotron violins and Hammond, and topped with Mellotron flute work.Melloreed: First military drums, a spacey synthesizer sound and soaring Mellotron violins, then a slow rhythm featuring tender synthesizer flights, an accordion sound and Mellotron violins, backed by a deep bass sound and slow drum beats. It sounds as very tasteful and elaborate symphonic rock, with hints of 76-77 Genesis.Intermission: This short track starts in a dreamy climate with soaring synthesizers, the atmosphere is a bit melancholical, then tender piano play, pretty intense.Red Dust: The intro features an impressive choir, taken from a 1938 Mattheus Passion vinyl record! Then a slow rhythm with an electric guitar that rocks, fiery and howling. Next spacey synthesizers and Mellotron flute, blended with dreamy English vocals, a bit fragile. The emotional undertone is emphasized by the soaring Mellotron violins, moving electric guitar and slow synthesizer runs. This track features vocal parts done by drummer Menno Boomsma.Far Away: In this track Trion showcases its variety and musical ideas with folky acoustic guitar, subtle assorted percussion (like Neil Peart from Rush) and majestic Mellotron violins, in a slow rhythm, simply beautiful.One: This excellent composition alternates between dreamy, a slow rhythm and bombastic, what a tension and dynamics, wonderfully coloured with tasteful and varied work on keyboards (lush Mellotron violins, synthesizer flights, orchestral keyboards and tender Mellotron flute) and guitar, from intense slide to moving runs. The rhythm-section does a good job, from subtle to powerful.Growing Clouds: This short piece contains dreamy and intense interplay between acoustic guitar and fragile vocals again done by Boomsma.Paradox Groove: First an exciting contrast between a soaring synthesizer (phaser sound) sound and rock guitar, backed by tight drum beats. Then a slow rhythm featuring sensitive and distorted electric guitar, blended with spacey synthesizers. Another fine example of the interesting musical ideas on this album.Space For Everybody: First a slow rhythm with jazzy electric piano and a flashy synthesizer sound, then a wonderful electric guitar solo with howling runs. Halfway an acceleration (evoking Camel) featuring moving guitar and powerful Hammond, in a mid-tempo beat. The final part delivers first a slow rhythm, embellished with Hammond, synthesizer flights and awesome Mellotron choirs, then another moving guitar solo. In the end the music fades away with Hammond, Mellotron and guitar, a subtle goodbye from the band.After Elements Of Hope by Glorious Wolf (Ruud Dielen project) and E.D.O. (solo project Edo Spanninga) with The Past Is A Foreign Country here is another strong and interesting new Dutch prog album, thumbs up for Trion!
items._cn_summary: 荷兰三人乐队Trion的专辑延续了经典的70年代交响摇滚传统，以Mellotron采样为核心乐器，融合键盘与吉他的交响式对话，整体音乐性扎实但创新性有限。作品强调旋律美感与氛围营造，结构上遵循传统前卫摇滚范式，节奏编排工整，属于该类型的忠实继承者。对于偏好实验与前卫边缘化表达的听众而言，该专辑过于遵循既有模式，缺乏突破性的声音探索或跨界融合，未能满足更高的创新期待。

 LIKE 4
The Greg Hopkins Jazz Orchestra: Chronography
By Jack Bowers
May 31, 2026
View read count
On Chronography, Boston-based trumpeter and composer Greg Hopkins and his 16-member Jazz Orchestra revitalize ten of the leader's never-before-recorded compositions and arrangements, most of them well-known standards from the Great American Songbook, that span more than half a century of astute and perceptive songwriting.

The earliest, Willard Robison's "Old Folks," was arranged for the Buddy Rich band in 1972; the most recent, Duke Ellington's "In a Sentimental Mood," for his own orchestra in 2018. Between those dates rest half a dozen standards, each one adeptly scored by Hopkins. Three charts—Rodgers and Hart's "My Romance" (1982), Ellington's "Come Sunday" (2006) and Dori Caymmi's "Like a Lover" (2007)—were later revised, and the more recent versions are heard here. After eight standards, Hopkins closes the album with a pair of his original compositions: "For 'O'" and "Dr. Diz," the last a medley of Dizzy Gillespie's "Hot House," "Con Alma" and "A Night in Tunisia." Irving Berlin's "What'll I Do" and a second Rodgers and Hart theme, "Spring Is Here," round out the engaging program.

Guest artist Renese King sings on "Like a Lover" and "Come Sunday," and a second guest, tenor saxophonist Billy Pierce, solos on the opening number, Johnny Green's desirous "Body and Soul." While other soloists are unlisted, baritone Brian Landrus and pianist Tim Ray clearly share the honors on "Old Folks," tenor Rick DiMuzio is front and center on "Spring Is Here" and "Dr. Diz," soprano Lihi Haruvi on "A Night in Tunisia," while Hopkins presumably reserves some if not all of the trumpet solos for himself. Even though well-written, Hopkins' charts lean toward slow to moderate tempos, and there is nothing here that could be mistaken for a barn-burner.

"This recording," Hopkins writes, "is a kind of panoramic chronology of my work over fifty-five years." Whatever the reasons behind Chronography, it is a pleasure to have these well-drawn charts at last on record and available to a wider audience.

items.body: Music videos Rafael “Pollo” Brito Leads Tribute to El Salvador on “Una Nueva Vida” World Music Central News Room May 30, 2026 No Comments Rafael “Pollo” Brito Salvadoran music world music Rafael “Pollo” Brito has released the music video for “ Una Nueva Vida ,” a tropical-inspired single issued worldwide by LatinWMG. The track forms part of Renacimiento: Música de El Salvador Reimaginada Vol. 1 , a project produced and directed by Salvadoran producer Samuel Quirós. The release follows earlier singles from the album, including “Reencuentro,” performed by Aymée Nuviola. In addition, the album features contributions from an international cast of artists, including Sandra Carrasco, Enrique Heredia Negri, Carlos Puchi, Edmundo Alfaro, Mauro Iglesias Cordova, Michelle Tejada and R.U.T.. R.U.T. appears on the bolero “Coatepeque,” another featured track from the project. According to Quirós, Renacimiento seeks to reinterpret traditional Salvadoran music through contemporary arrangements while preserving its cultural identity. Rafael “Pollo” Brito “Una Nueva Vida” features an original composition by Salvadoran songwriter Carlos Alfaro. Olga Castro wrote the lyrical adaptation dedicated to El Salvador, while Samuel Ignacio Quirós Badillo composed the music. Alejandro Campos handled the arrangements and tropical instrumentation. Samuel Quirós also served as executive producer of the project. Author: World Music Central News Room World music news from the editors at World Music Central

items.body: Music videos Geary & John Introduce Countrified Steak With “I’m Just Too Lazy” World Music Central News Room May 31, 2026 No Comments Bluegrass Geary & John Geary Allen John Gooding world music Geary Allen and John Gooding, the duo performing as Geary & John, have released their debut single, “ I’m Just Too Lazy .” The track previews their forthcoming guitar album, Countrified Steak . Recorded in one take with no overdubs, the bluegrass song features both musicians on vintage 1951 Martin guitars. The lyrics follow a man whose lack of motivation has left his life in disarray. However, his easygoing outlook gives the song a humorous edge and a candid view of human weakness. The duo also plans to share behind-the-scenes material, performance clips, and updates through their social media channels. Author: World Music Central News Room World music news from the editors at World Music Central

items.body:
Prolific deep house fetishist Tom Carruthers helms a tight clutch of jab-jacking zingers by himself and the extended family on Indulgence Records, a sub-label of his ceaseless Non Stop Rhythm label.

Classic late ‘80s and cusp-of-‘90s house sauce is the mode for a handful of artists who share the same passion for timeless forms, as extensively heard on the brilliant Non Stop Rhythm label. Label alum DJ Split leads the way with the ruddy garage-house bass and kinky parry of ‘Tape Zone Xoxo Mix’, and stablemate Raymond Owen follows suit with the deep NYC square bass ’n bleep pressure of ‘Beyond The Pleasure’ on a 1990 Fourth Floor tip. David Boning knocks out two tuff jackers, the freestyle and garage-house inflected budge of ‘Second City Thoughts’ with Ba.dido, and solo darkroom sashay of ‘Not a Camera’, while Kaluki’s Toby Simpson lends atmospheric levity with vocal house belter ‘Temptations’, and Manchester’s Jimm brings organ-led heat on ‘Feela’.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张以复古八九十年代浩室风格为主的合辑专辑，由Tom Carruthers主导的Indulgence Records发行，收录了多位延续经典house传统的艺术家作品。音乐风格偏向车库浩室、纽约式bass与bleep元素，以及人声浩室和组织乐驱动的曲目。对于偏好实验、前卫、电子暗潮及学院派爵士的听众而言，此类复古舞曲与核心口味存在较大距离。虽然制作水准扎实，但创新性和实验性有限，属于单一风格内的致敬性作品，难以满足追求音乐前沿性和跨界融合的需求。

items.album: Chris Nickson reviews this multi-media memorial to working class heroism. »
items.body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter’s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages – and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy, with its famous lines: “Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.” Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It’s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he’s selected some great talent to help – guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator. For a small ensemble, they make a powerful noise. The songs capture the feel of the day; the anticipation and excitement at the summer gathering, the joy that turns to terror and flight as the troops charge, then the bitter, mournful aftermath, voiced some powerful melodies and very well-chosen images. As a writer, Cooney often focuses on the personal in the small tales of people like “Sam Bamford” and “Mary Fildes,” while the three short pieces that comprise “The Monkey Rides The Mare” capture the bluster and arrogance of the soldiers. Cooney is a persuasive singer, and on this heartfelt project, he puts plenty of emotion into his voice. Having two other outstanding vocalists alongside him makes for a wonderful triple threat. In these days when governments across the world are cracking down on protest, this stands as a sobering and very timely reminder. It’s a history lesson, yes, but the detail of the history stays in the book, while the music creates a set of songs that will resonate and remain for a long time. Find the artist online. items.body: Live at Rockpalast 1999 documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm “Mac” Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms. Taped at the height of Dr. John’s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close. A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac’s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions. Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic “Iko, Iko,” a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast “Qualified,” wherein the singer warns, “I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.” Any Dr. John fan will recognize “I Walk on Guilded Splinters,” a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper’s immersion in “funknology” (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: “Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.” Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own “Sweet Home New Orleans” and “Goin’ Back to New Orleans,” and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington’s “I'm Gonna Go Fishin’.” Among other gems are Mac’s Top–10 hit “Right Place, Wrong Time,” and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King’s “Big Chief,” another Mardi Gras burner. Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, “I always play a little bit of everything. I think that’s what music’s about: a little bit of somethin’ old, somethin’ in the middle, somethin’ new, and somethin’ as yet uncreated.” Dr John's’s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of At the Rockpalast is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, “If you’re gonna get off on somethin’ you don’t need to know nothin’ about it. Music is a universal language.”
